label: Pitfall 1: use raw counts layer scvi_counts, sum aggregation
text: PITFALL: Pseudobulking the wrong matrix. In this AnnData, .X holds log-normalised floats and layers['scaled'] holds scaled values; only layers['scvi_counts'] looks like raw integer UMI counts (PopV stores raw counts there). Summing or averaging log-normalised values and feeding them to DESeq2/edgeR gives wrong log2FCs (compressed and pseudocount-distorted). CHECK: confirm the matrix you aggregate is non-negative integers (np.allclose(data, np.round(data)), max well above 10) and that per-cell sums match obs nCount_RNA / n_counts. IF FOUND: aggregate layers['scvi_counts'] by SUM (not mean) per sample x cell type and run the count model on those sums. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/conditions/differential-gene-expression/ ; https://decoupler.scverse.org/en/stable/notebooks/scell/rna_psbk.html ; https://github.com/YosefLab/popV/blob/main/popv/preprocessing.py

label: Pitfall 2: cell-level logFC is not pseudobulk log2FC
text: PITFALL: Doing cell-level DE (e.g. scanpy rank_genes_groups / Wilcoxon) instead of pseudobulk and reporting its 'logfoldchanges'. Scanpy computes log2((expm1(mean of log1p values)+1e-9)/(...)), i.e. a ratio of geometric-like means, and Seurat adds a +1 pseudocount; both differ, sometimes by several log2 units for sparse genes, from a count-based pseudobulk log2FC, and cells are pseudoreplicates of the sample. Also uns['log1p'] here is an empty dict, so rank_genes_groups can raise KeyError 'base'. CHECK: make sure the reported log2FC comes from a model fitted on a samples x genes pseudobulk count table (here 4 samples x 2 monocyte types = up to 8 columns), not from a per-cell test. IF FOUND: replace with pseudobulk DESeq2/PyDESeq2 (or edgeR) and take log2FoldChange from that fit. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/864 ; https://divingintogeneticsandgenomics.com/post/do-you-really-understand-log2fold-change-in-single-cell-rnaseq-data/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-21038-1

label: Pitfall 3: contrast direction non-classical over classical
text: PITFALL: Sign flip from the contrast or reference level. PyDESeq2 contrast is [factor, tested_level, ref_level] and reports tested/ref; DESeq2 in R uses the alphabetical first level as reference unless relevelled ('classical monocyte' sorts before 'non-classical monocyte', which happens to give non-classical/classical, but do not rely on it). The task wants log2(non-classical / classical). CHECK: after fitting, compute for 2-3 genes a crude log2 ratio of summed CPM (non-classical over classical) straight from the pseudobulk counts and confirm it has the same sign as the model log2FoldChange. IF FOUND: set the contrast explicitly as [celltype, non-classical, classical] (or negate the LFC) and re-verify. Renaming the two levels to simple tokens without spaces/hyphens before building the design avoids formula/level-name parsing problems (this renaming advice is precautionary, not confirmed by a source). SOURCE: https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.ds.DeseqStats.html ; https://github.com/owkin/PyDESeq2/issues/362

label: Pitfall 4: paired design, sample as blocking factor
text: PITFALL: Ignoring that the two groups are paired. Both monocyte subsets come from the same 4 samples (obs 'sample': sample1-4), so a design of ~ celltype treats donor/sample differences as noise, while ~ sample + celltype blocks on sample; the two designs give somewhat different log2FCs and very different dispersions/p-values. CHECK: tabulate cells per sample x cell type and confirm each sample contributes both subsets; run both designs and compare the 8 target-gene LFCs. IF FOUND: use the paired design ~ sample + celltype as primary when every sample has both subsets (it is the standard blocked design); if a sample lacks one subset, drop that sample or fall back to ~ celltype, and report which. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-19894-4 ; https://diseaseneurogenomics.github.io/dreamlet/reference/dreamletCompareClusters.html

label: Pitfall 5: MLE vs shrunken LFC, zero-count genes
text: PITFALL: Reporting shrunken instead of maximum-likelihood log2FC (or mixing them). lfcShrink / PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink (apeglm) overwrites results_df and pulls LFCs toward zero, strongly for genes with low or zero counts in one group; with only 4 samples per group the shrunken and MLE values can differ by more than a log2 unit for genes nearly absent in one subset. PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink has also had a reported bug that changed LFC magnitude or sign for some genes. Conversely, the MLE for a gene with all-zero counts in one group is large and unstable (bounded only by an internal floor). CHECK: record both MLE and shrunken LFC for the 8 genes, and list the raw pseudobulk counts of each gene in every sample to see whether any group is at or near zero. IF FOUND: report the unshrunken MLE log2FoldChange from the standard results table as the default 'log2FC' (that is what a plain DE run returns), mention the shrunken value as a sensitivity, and flag any gene whose value depends on near-zero counts. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/102052/ ; https://github.com/owkin/PyDESeq2/issues/347 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6581436/

label: Data layout of 4T1 h5ad
text: DATA SHAPE (headers only, not analysed): /workspace/data/4T1_viable_post_norm.h5ad has 6420 cells x 19973 genes, one sample; .X is float32 log1p(CP10k); raw integer counts are in layers['counts']; obs has sample, n_genes, n_genes_by_counts, total_counts; var has only QC columns (n_cells_by_counts, mean_counts, pct_dropout_by_counts, total_counts) -- there is NO highly_variable column, no mito/ribo flags, no existing PCA; uns['log1p']['base'] was stored as None.

label: PITFALL no HVG selection before PCA
text: PITFALL: Running PCA on all ~20k genes of log1p(CP10k) data with no feature selection lets abundant/noisy genes set the axes; on log-normalised UMI data PC1 then tracks the per-cell fraction of zeros and log total UMI (Townes 2019 report r=0.8-0.98 between PC1 and zero fraction in negative-control data). CHECK: confirm adata.var has no 'highly_variable' column (it does not here), then run PCA on all genes vs on ~2000 HVGs and compare |Pearson r| of PC1-5 with log1p(obs['total_counts']) and with n_genes_by_counts. IF FOUND: select HVGs (about 2000; mean-variance-trend based) before PCA and treat the HVG set as the 'gene universe passed to PCA' when reporting loadings. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-019-1861-6 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/

label: PITFALL unscaled PCA single-gene PC1
text: PITFALL: PCA on unscaled log-normalised genes weights each gene by its variance, so one or a few very high-variance genes (often abundant lineage/secreted genes) can own PC1; the PC1 loading vector is unit-norm, so max|loading| ranges from 1/sqrt(n_genes) (perfectly spread; ~0.022 for 2000 genes) to 1.0 (one gene). scanpy's sc.pp.pca only zero-centres, it does NOT scale to unit variance. CHECK: run PCA with and without sc.pp.scale on the same HVG set; print the top 10 genes by |PCs[:,0]| and the max; see whether one gene's loading is several-fold larger than the next. IF FOUND: z-score the HVGs (sc.pp.scale, max_value=10) before PCA, or use Pearson residuals, so the axis is distributed across a gene programme. Counter-view to weigh: Aaron Lun argues standardisation down-weights genuinely informative high-variance genes and up-weights noise, and scanpy maintainers say there is no consensus -- so decide by the diagnostic, not by habit. SOURCE: https://ltla.github.io/SingleCellThoughts/general/standardization.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2164 ; https://hbctraining.github.io/Intro-to-scRNAseq/lessons/07_normalization.html

label: PITFALL depth signal survives log-normalisation
text: PITFALL: log1p(CP10k) does not fully remove sequencing depth: the log of a size-normalised count is biased differently in shallow vs deep cells, and high-abundance genes keep a residual depth dependence, so top PCs of 'already normalised' data can still correlate with total counts (Lun 2018; Hafemeister & Satija 2019; Risso 2018 ZINB-WaVE). CHECK: for the exact embedding handed to neighbours, compute Pearson r between each of PC1..PC10 and log1p(obs['total_counts']) (also n_genes_by_counts), report max |r| over PC1-5, and scatter-plot the worst PC against depth. IF FOUND: compare candidate pipelines on this same diagnostic (HVG+scale; HVG+regress_out(total_counts)+scale; analytic Pearson residuals from layers['counts']) and keep the one that lowers depth correlation while cell-type structure stays intact. No transformation guarantees depth removal (a 2022 depth-normalisation benchmark found sctransform still depth-correlated in some datasets; Ahlmann-Eltze & Huber 2023 found shifted-log+PCA performs as well as residual methods overall), so measure rather than assume. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/404962 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-019-1874-1 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10172138/ ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.05.06.490859v1.full.pdf

label: PITFALL depth is partly cell-type biology
text: PITFALL: In a whole tumour, total UMI per cell is partly biology, not only capture efficiency: cell types differ several-fold in transcriptome size (large malignant/epithelial and cycling cells high, small lymphoid/granulocytic cells low), so a PC that separates cell types will correlate with depth across all cells even if no technical depth effect remains; linear regress_out of total_counts cannot tell the two apart and also removes correlated biology. CHECK: make a coarse clustering, compare total_counts distributions between clusters, and compute the PC-vs-log1p(total_counts) correlation WITHIN each large cluster as well as globally; a large global r with small within-cluster r means the depth correlation is compositional. IF FOUND: do not regress total_counts blindly; if you do regress, verify marker-defined populations are still separated afterwards; state in the write-up which part of the depth correlation is between-cell-type. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11787294/ ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/526 ; https://hanbin973.github.io/2022/04/17/single-cell-regression.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/

label: PITFALL HVG flavour vs input matrix
text: PITFALL: Feeding the wrong matrix to HVG selection. scanpy highly_variable_genes flavor='seurat_v3' expects RAW integer counts, while flavor='seurat'/'cell_ranger' expect log data; here .X is already log1p(CP10k) and counts are in layers['counts']. Running seurat_v3 on .X gives a wrong gene set (only a warning), and re-running normalize_total/log1p on .X double-logs the data, compressing variance and changing loadings. CHECK: assert .X is non-integer with max below ~10 and expm1(X) row sums ~1e4; assert layers['counts'] is integer and its row sums equal obs['total_counts']. IF FOUND: use flavor='seurat_v3' with layer='counts' (needs scikit-misc) or flavor='seurat' on .X; never normalise/log .X again. Also test sensitivity of both reported metrics to the HVG flavour and n_top_genes (e.g. 2000 vs 3000). SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/how-to-handle-data-lognormalization-when-using-highly-variable-genes-with-flavor-seurat-v3/1076

label: PITFALL uncentred PCA / TruncatedSVD
text: PITFALL: Uncentred PCA. sc.pp.pca(zero_center=False) (TruncatedSVD), or old scanpy on sparse input, makes the first component essentially the vector of gene means, so PC1 scores track how many genes/UMIs a cell has -- an artificial depth axis and distorted later PCs. CHECK: confirm zero_center=True was used, that obsm['X_pca'] columns have mean ~0, and that PC1 loadings are not all one sign. IF FOUND: rerun with zero_center=True, svd_solver='arpack' (deterministic); a dense scaled HVG matrix (6420 x ~2000 float32, ~100 MB) is small enough to centre. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/393 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.pca.html

label: PITFALL order of HVG/regress/scale and clipping
text: PITFALL: Wrong order of operations around scale/regress_out. sc.pp.scale and sc.pp.regress_out densify the matrix and set gene means to 0; calling highly_variable_genes AFTER them breaks mean-binned HVG selection, and running them on all 19973 genes wastes RAM/time. Separately, unclipped z-scores of sparse genes expressed in a rare population reach very large values and create PCs driven by a few cells and genes (Seurat scale.max=10 and scanpy max_value=10 exist for this). CHECK: HVGs chosen on unscaled data; scale applied only to the HVG subset; max of the scaled matrix <= 10; inspect whether extreme PC1 scores belong to a handful of cells. IF FOUND: order = HVG -> subset/mask -> (optional regress_out) -> scale(max_value=10) -> pca; keep log data in a layer/.raw for annotation. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/single-cell-tutorial/issues/35 ; https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/scaledata ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

label: PITFALL nuisance gene families in HVGs
text: PITFALL: Nuisance gene families can sit in the HVG list and dominate a PC, especially without scaling: mitochondrial (mouse prefix 'mt-', lower case), ribosomal (Rps/Rpl), haemoglobin (Hba-/Hbb-), immunoglobulin (Igh/Igk/Igl), Malat1, and dissociation-stress genes (Fos, Jun, Hsp*); mito/ribo fraction also tracks cell quality and depth. CHECK: list the top 20 genes by |loading| for PC1-PC5 and flag these families; correlate PCs with per-cell mito and ribo fractions computed from layers['counts']. IF FOUND: consider dropping those genes from the HVG mask (not from the object) and re-running PCA; report whether the two diagnostics change. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/1545 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/

label: PITFALL inconsistent metric computation
text: PITFALL: Computing the two reported diagnostics inconsistently. (a) With mask_var/use_highly_variable, scanpy fills varm['PCs'] rows of non-HVG genes with zeros (harmless for a max, but the 'gene universe' is the HVG set); (b) obs['total_counts'] is silently overwritten if sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics is re-run after subsetting to HVGs, which would make the depth covariate an HVG-only sum; (c) PC signs are arbitrary, so use absolute values; (d) both numbers must come from the SAME final PCA object (after any regress/scale), not from an exploratory run. CHECK: save depth = log1p(obs['total_counts']) from the untouched file before any processing and assert it equals log1p of layers['counts'] row sums over all genes; recompute both metrics from the final adata just before writing the answer. IF FOUND: recompute from the saved depth vector and the final varm['PCs'][:,0] / obsm['X_pca'][:, :5]. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.pca.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/main/src/scanpy/preprocessing/_pca/__init__.py

label: PITFALL uns log1p base KeyError
text: PITFALL: After reading an h5ad, adata.uns['log1p'] can be an empty dict because a None 'base' is not round-tripped, and highly_variable_genes(flavor='seurat') / rank_genes_groups then crash with KeyError: 'base' (this file stores log1p base as None). CHECK: print adata.uns.get('log1p') right after reading. IF FOUND: set adata.uns['log1p'] = {'base': None} before HVG selection; do not respond by re-logging the data. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2239 ; https://github.com/scverse/anndata/issues/865

label: Pitfall 6: subset to the two monocyte types before fitting
text: PITFALL: Fitting the model on the wrong set of pseudobulks. The file has about 18 annotated PBMC cell types; if all sample x cell-type pseudobulks are fed into one DESeq2 fit, the size factors (median of ratios against an all-sample geometric mean), the dispersion estimates and the gene filter are driven by T, B and NK cells, and the monocyte log2FCs change. Standard pseudobulk practice is to subset to the cell types being compared first. CHECK: confirm the count table passed to the DE tool contains only classical and non-classical monocyte pseudobulks (at most 8 columns) and that size factors were estimated on those columns only. IF FOUND: subset to the two monocyte labels before aggregation and fitting; if you also try the all-cell-type fit, treat it only as a sensitivity. SOURCE: https://hbctraining.github.io/Pseudobulk-for-scRNAseq/lessons/03_pseudobulk_DESeq2.html ; https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html

label: Pitfall 7: min-cells and gene filters dropping pseudobulks or target genes
text: PITFALL: Default pseudobulk and gene filters silently removing samples or target genes. Non-classical monocytes are a small population, so a sample may contribute few cells; decoupler get_pseudobulk defaults (min_cells=10, min_counts=1000) drop small pseudobulks without error, which unbalances a paired design, and expression filters (filter_by_expr min_count=10, min_total_count=15, or a 'at least 10 counts in N samples' rule) can drop a marker gene that is near zero in one subset, giving NaN/missing LFC. CHECK: print cells and total counts per sample x cell type before and after aggregation, confirm all expected pseudobulks survive, and confirm all 8 target genes (FCGR3A, CX3CR1, CDKN1C, MS4A7, CD14, S100A8, S100A9, VCAN) are present in var_names and in the fitted table. IF FOUND: state the thresholds used; do not let a filter remove a requested gene (relax the gene filter or filter on the union across groups), and if a pseudobulk has very few cells report the result with and without that sample. SOURCE: https://decoupler.scverse.org/en/v1.9.2/generated/decoupler.get_pseudobulk.html ; https://decoupler.scverse.org/en/stable/api/generated/decoupler.pp.filter_by_expr.html ; https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html

label: Pitfall 8: which PopV label column, low-confidence and intermediate monocytes
text: PITFALL: Choosing the wrong cell-type label column, or including low-confidence cells. obs has several PopV label columns: popv_prediction (final ontology-aware consensus), popv_majority_vote_prediction, and per-method columns (celltypist, scanvi, knn_on_scvi, svm, xgboost, onclass); they need not agree, and popv_prediction_score / popv_majority_vote_score count how many methods agree. The label set has only 'classical monocyte' and 'non-classical monocyte', so intermediate (CD14++CD16+) monocytes, dendritic-cell-like cells and doublets are forced into one of the two groups, which dilutes marker fold changes. CHECK: crosstab popv_prediction against popv_majority_vote_prediction for the two monocyte labels, count cells per label per sample, and look at the score distribution within each label. IF FOUND: use popv_prediction as the primary grouping (it is PopV's documented final call), and re-run restricted to high-agreement cells as a sensitivity; if the columns give materially different LFCs, say so rather than picking silently. SOURCE: https://github.com/YosefLab/popV ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-024-01993-3 ; https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2020.01070

label: sc14 data format
text: DATA FORMAT (headers only, no analysis done): the task file 157798553.node is an h5ad with X = dense int64 raw UMI counts, 1689 cells x 20574 genes, mouse gene symbols (older annotation, includes clone-style names such as RP23-317L18.4), cell barcodes as index, and NO obs columns, var columns, layers, obsm or uns. There are no batch, sample, cell-type or cluster labels, so all QC, normalisation, clustering and any cell-type filtering must be done from scratch, and batch effects cannot be checked from metadata.

label: Pitfall 9: composition bias, CPM vs median-of-ratios/TMM
text: PITFALL: Composition bias when comparing two different cell types. Hand-computed log2 ratios of CPM (library-size scaling) are biased when a few very highly expressed genes differ strongly between groups, which is typical between monocyte subsets (a handful of abundant genes take a large share of the classical-monocyte library); every other gene's CPM is then shifted. DESeq2 median-of-ratios and edgeR TMM correct for this but assume most genes are not differentially expressed. CHECK: compare DESeq2 size factors (or TMM norm factors) with plain library-size ratios across the 8 pseudobulks; if they diverge by cell type, CPM-based LFCs are shifted by about log2 of that divergence. IF FOUND: take LFCs from the median-of-ratios/TMM-normalised model, not from raw CPM ratios, and use CPM ratios only as a sign/sanity check. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/gb-2010-11-3-r25 ; https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6171491/ ; https://pseudocount.com/posts/library-size-vs-composition/

label: Pitfall 10: ambient RNA attenuates marker LFC (caveat only)
text: PITFALL: Ambient RNA attenuates between-cell-type fold changes in droplet PBMC data. Abundant monocyte transcripts (S100A8, S100A9, LYZ are the classic contaminating genes) leak into every droplet, so the subset that does not express them still shows counts and the pseudobulk log2FC is pulled toward zero; summing over many cells makes this floor visible rather than averaging it away. CHECK: look at whether these genes have non-trivial counts in clearly unrelated cell types (T, B cells) in the same samples; that level approximates the ambient floor. IF FOUND: do not invent a correction (no empty-droplet profile is in the file); report the uncorrected pseudobulk LFC as the answer and note that the highly expressed classical markers are probably underestimated in magnitude. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.multisample/ambient-problems.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11112958/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7763177/

label: PITFALL contaminant cell types hijack CAF axis
text: PITFALL: Non-fibroblast or fibroblast-adjacent cells (pericytes/vascular smooth muscle, mesothelial, endothelial, immune, epithelial/tumour cells, doublets) left in a 'CAF' matrix form a discrete outlier group that becomes one end of PC1/diffusion component 1, so the 'dominant trajectory' is really a cell-type contrast and the markers are lineage markers. CHECK: cluster coarsely and score canonical sets per cluster: fibroblast (Pdgfra, Col1a1, Col1a2, Dcn, Lum, Pdpn), mural (Rgs5, Mcam, Cspg4, Myh11, Des, Notch3), endothelial (Pecam1, Cdh5), immune (Ptprc), epithelial (Epcam, Krt8, Krt18), mesothelial (Msln, Upk3b, Wt1); look for clusters lacking fibroblast genes or weakly connected to the rest in the kNN/PAGA graph. IF FOUND: drop clearly non-mesenchymal clusters (immune, endothelial, epithelial, obvious doublets) and recompute the trajectory. Be careful with mural-like cells: several CAF studies deliberately keep Rgs5+/contractile cells as a CAF subtype (vascular CAF, or lumped into myCAF), so with a small pre-subset file (1689 cells, no labels) do not strip mesenchymal cells by default; run the trajectory with and without them and report whether the terminal groups and top markers change. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7414220/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7613625/ ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cell-and-developmental-biology/articles/10.3389/fcell.2024.1403122/full
