label: PITFALL cell cycle distorts trajectory
text: PITFALL: Cell cycle is a strong confounder that distorts trajectory inference; a proliferating cluster can become a terminal group and the 'top markers' become Mki67/Top2a-type cycle genes rather than CAF-state genes. In CAF data a 'cycling CAF' cluster has been described that is only the proliferating segment of another subtype, not a separate state. CHECK: score S and G2M gene sets (e.g. Mki67, Top2a, Cdk1, Ccnb1, Birc5, Pcna, Mcm2-7), then correlate the score with PC1-5, DC1 and pseudotime, and see whether either terminal group is enriched for cycling cells or whether cycle genes dominate the top marker list. IF FOUND: remove cell-cycle genes from the highly variable gene set (or regress S/G2M scores) before PCA/neighbours, recompute the trajectory, and assign cycling cells to their parent state rather than treating them as an endpoint. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7671373/ ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.12.22.473434v1.full ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6279758/

label: PITFALL dominant axis is technical depth/quality
text: PITFALL: The leading axis of variation (PC1 or diffusion component 1) in raw-count scRNA-seq often tracks technical quality (library size, number of genes detected, mitochondrial fraction, low-quality or dying cells) instead of biology, so terminal groups become 'high-depth vs low-depth' cells and markers are mito/ribosomal or simply high-abundance genes. CHECK: compute total counts, n_genes and percent mt- per cell; Spearman-correlate each with PC1-5, DC1 and the final pseudotime; compare these QC metrics between the two terminal groups; inspect the top marker list for mt-, Rps/Rpl, Malat1. IF FOUND: filter low-quality outlier cells first, normalise properly (size-factor + log1p, or try analytic Pearson residuals as a sensitivity check), and if a component is still mostly depth (|rho| above about 0.5-0.6 with no CAF-program signal) do not use it as the trajectory; take the next biological component. Do not blindly regress depth out, because cell size can be genuinely different between fibroblast states; instead confirm the axis survives normalisation choice. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-019-1861-6 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6544759/

label: PITFALL dissociation stress signature
text: PITFALL: Enzymatic dissociation of solid tumours induces a stress / immediate-early gene program (Fos, Fosb, Jun, Junb, Egr1, Ier2, Ier3, Atf3, Dusp1, Zfp36, Klf4, Nr4a1, Hspa1a, Hspa1b) that is real transcription but an artefact; it has produced fake 'activated fibroblast' states and can be the major axis in stromal cells. CHECK: score this gene set per cell, correlate with PC1/DC1/pseudotime, and count how many of the top markers between terminal groups are immediate-early or heat-shock genes. IF FOUND: exclude these genes from the highly variable gene set (or regress the score) and recompute; if the axis disappears it was artefact. Do not remove genuine inflammatory-CAF cytokine/chemokine genes (e.g. Il6, Cxcl1, Cxcl12) in the same step; they are biology, the IEG/heat-shock set is the artefact. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6610623/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-019-1830-0 ; https://www.cell.com/trends/cell-biology/abstract/S0962-8924(21)00096-9

label: Data format of og_raw_counts.h5ad
text: DATA FORMAT (headers only, no analysis): /workspace/data/og_raw_counts.h5ad is 11693 cells x 27946 genes, X is a CSC sparse matrix of int32 raw counts with 14,122,787 stored entries, there are no layers, and obs/var have NO columns at all (no donor column; obs_names look like 'sample1_cell10000', var_names are gene symbols such as TSPAN6). Donor/sample identity can only come from the obs_names prefix, and whether the prefix maps one-to-one to the 4 donors is unverified.

label: sc06 data layout
text: DATA FACT (from file headers only, no analysis): /workspace/data/adata_merged_noX.h5ad has 16136 cells x 386 genes, which is a BD Rhapsody TARGETED immune-response-style panel, not whole transcriptome. There is no X matrix; counts live in three layers: Raw_Molecules, RSEC_Adjusted_Molecules and DBEC_Adjusted_Molecules. The DBEC layer has about 11% fewer non-zero entries than RSEC (1,164,478 vs 1,305,936), so genes-per-cell depends on the layer. There are no MT- or ribosomal genes in the panel. obs columns: sample (9 sample tags), tissue, source (PBMC/Tissue), batch (2), treatment (3 timepoints), condition; Cell_Index is NOT unique (16082 values for 16136 cells) so use the obs index cell_id as the key.

label: PITFALL HVG flavor vs input scale
text: PITFALL: HVG flavor and input scale are mismatched. scanpy's default flavor='seurat' (and 'cell_ranger') expects log-normalized data and internally applies expm1, while 'seurat_v3'/'seurat_v3_paper' expect raw integer counts; X here is raw int32 counts, so calling sc.pp.highly_variable_genes with the default flavor directly on X silently gives a meaningless ranking, and calling seurat_v3 after normalize_total/log1p only emits a UserWarning. CHECK: before the HVG call, assert whether the matrix passed is integer-valued (e.g. np.allclose(X.data, np.round(X.data))) and whether adata.uns has 'log1p'; confirm it matches the flavor. IF FOUND: for seurat_v3 run on raw counts (before normalisation, or pass layer='counts'); for seurat/cell_ranger run normalize_total + log1p first; state in the report which flavor and which input were used. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1782 ; https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/1545

label: Data layout of the cytokine PBMC h5ad
text: DATA LAYOUT (header only, no analysis): /workspace/data/Parse_10M_PBMC_100K_subset.h5ad is 100,000 cells x 40,352 genes; X is a CSR float32 matrix whose first values look like raw integer counts; there are no layers, no .raw, no obsm/uns. obs columns include donor (Donor1..Donor12), cytokine (91 levels incl. 'IFN-beta' and 'PBS'), treatment ('PBS'/'cytokine'), cell_type (18 levels incl. 'CD14 Mono' and 'CD16 Mono'), sample ('Donor1_IFN-beta' style, 1092 = 12 x 91 levels). var has gene symbols as index and one column n_cells whose values (up to ~2 million) come from the full 10M-cell atlas, NOT this subset, so it must not be used for gene filtering. With ~92 cells per donor-condition spread over 18 cell types, CD14 Mono pseudobulks will hold only a handful to a few dozen cells each, so the '<5 cells' donor rule will probably bite.

label: PITFALL targeted panel QC defaults
text: PITFALL: Whole-transcriptome QC defaults (min_genes=200, max_genes=2500, percent-mito <5-20%) are wrong for a 386-gene targeted Rhapsody panel: a healthy cell detects only tens of panel genes, so min_genes=200 deletes almost every cell, and the panel has no MT- genes so pct_counts_mt is 0 or undefined and filters nothing. CHECK: plot per-cell n_genes and total molecules for PBMC cells before choosing any cutoff; confirm var_names.str.startswith('MT-') matches nothing; count how many cells any proposed cutoff removes. IF FOUND: set thresholds from the observed distribution (the low tail / knee, or MAD-based outliers on log counts and log genes), with low-count and low-gene filters as the only QC metrics, and report how many cells each filter removes. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.24/OSCA.basic/quality-control.html

label: Pitfall: pseudoreplication, use donor-level pseudobulk
text: PITFALL: Testing cells as replicates (scanpy rank_genes_groups Wilcoxon/t-test, Seurat FindMarkers) treats cells from one donor as independent; this pseudoreplication gives tiny p-values and a DEG count inflated by hundreds to thousands, and it grows with cell number rather than with donors. CHECK: confirm the unit of replication fed to the test is donor x condition (at most 12 IFN-beta + 12 PBS columns), not cells; if a cell-level test was run, compare its DEG count with the pseudobulk count. IF FOUND: sum raw counts of CD14 Mono cells per donor per condition into pseudobulk samples and test with a bulk negative-binomial method (DESeq2/PyDESeq2 or edgeR); pseudobulk outperformed cell-level and mixed-model methods in benchmarks. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8479118/ ; https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21038-1 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-35519-4

label: PITFALL HVG prevalence depends on method
text: PITFALL: The 'median number of cells in which the HVGs are detected' is not a property of the data alone; it depends strongly on the HVG method, because methods select very different gene sets (a benchmark of 47 methods reports significant discrepancies between methods; one user saw only 138 of 500 genes shared between Seurat and scanpy flavor='seurat'; scanpy seurat_v3 vs R Seurat vst agree ~98.65% on 2000 genes). The task names no flavor, only 'top 2,000 HVGs' on a raw-count file with no normalisation step mentioned. CHECK: compute the HVG set and its median detection prevalence under at least seurat_v3 on raw counts and seurat on log-normalised data, and report the overlap of the two sets and both medians. IF FOUND (they differ materially): pick the method that needs no unstated steps for the data as given (raw counts + fixed n_top_genes=2000 corresponds to seurat_v3 / Seurat vst, where n_top_genes is mandatory and defaults to 2000), and report the alternative value and the assumption explicitly rather than hiding it. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12699822/ ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2780 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/how-to-handle-data-lognormalization-when-using-highly-variable-genes-with-flavor-seurat-v3/1076

label: Pitfall: paired donor design vs ~condition
text: PITFALL: Every donor contributes both an IFN-beta and a PBS sample (paired/blocked design). Fitting ~condition alone leaves donor-to-donor baseline variation in the residual dispersion, which inflates standard errors and changes the number of genes passing padj<0.05 (a simulation found paired ~patient+condition detecting ~68% of true DEGs versus ~23% unpaired in DESeq2); it does not inflate false positives but it changes the count. CHECK: confirm each retained donor has exactly one pseudobulk per condition; run both '~donor + condition' and '~condition' and report both DEG counts and how far apart they are; PCA of pseudobulks to see whether samples cluster by donor. IF FOUND (donor effect visible or counts differ): the statistically correct model for a paired design is '~ donor + condition' with the condition term last and the contrast IFN-beta vs PBS; state clearly which design the reported number uses, because a task that does not mention pairing may have been scored with the simpler '~condition' design. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html (multi-factor designs; 'Can I use DESeq2 to analyze paired samples?') ; https://pseudocount.com/posts/paired-samples-rna-seq-design/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9141932/

label: PITFALL Rhapsody layer choice RSEC vs DBEC
text: PITFALL: The file has no X and three count layers (Raw, RSEC, DBEC); picking the wrong one changes both the QC outcome and the median genes per cell. For Rhapsody targeted assays BD applies DBEC after RSEC to remove low-depth artifact molecules (PCR chimeras etc.), and recommends the DBEC table when sequencing is near saturation (mean RSEC depth >6); RSEC still contains noise molecules that grow with depth and inflate genes detected per cell. CHECK: compute n_genes and total counts per PBMC cell from each layer and compare the medians and the number of cells passing QC; state explicitly which layer feeds X. IF FOUND: use DBEC_Adjusted_Molecules as the default count matrix for a targeted panel and compute the reported genes-per-cell on that same layer; if you use RSEC instead, say so and expect a higher median. Never use Raw_Molecules. SOURCE: https://bd-rhapsody-bioinfo-docs.genomics.bd.com/steps/steps%5Ferror%5Fcorrection.html ; https://scomix.bd.com/hc/en-us/articles/360044971032-Bioinformatics-Primary-Analysis

label: Pitfall: donor exclusion rule applied to wrong cells or one arm
text: PITFALL: The donor exclusion rule ('fewer than 5 cells in either condition') is easy to apply to the wrong cell set or to only one arm. Counting cells over all cell types, or dropping only the under-populated pseudobulk while keeping the donor's other arm, gives a different sample set, unbalanced pairs, and a different DEG count. Pseudobulks from very few cells are also noisy; muscat defaults to min_cells=10 and practitioners often want far more. CHECK: after subsetting to cell_type=='CD14 Mono' and cytokine in {'IFN-beta','PBS'}, tabulate cells per donor x cytokine; a donor missing a condition entirely counts as 0 (<5); list which donors are dropped and confirm every kept donor has >=5 cells in BOTH arms. IF FOUND: remove the whole donor (both pseudobulks) so the design stays paired and balanced; follow the task's threshold of 5 for the reported answer, and as a sensitivity check re-run with a stricter threshold (e.g. 10) to see how fragile the count is. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/muscat/man/pbDS.html ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9143599/ ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/conditions/differential-gene-expression/

label: PITFALL DBEC pass status differs by batch
text: PITFALL: DBEC is applied per gene and only to genes with mean non-singleton RSEC depth >=4, separately in each pipeline run. Two merged cartridges (batch 1 and 2) sequenced to different depth will have different genes passing DBEC, which BD warns produces an apparent batch effect in embeddings and can split one cell type into batch-specific clusters. CHECK: per batch, compare per-gene total DBEC vs RSEC counts to see which genes were DBEC-corrected in one batch but not the other; colour the embedding by batch and check whether monocyte clusters separate by batch. IF FOUND: annotate lineages with marker evidence that holds in both batches (or cluster/annotate per batch and combine labels) and do not let a batch-specific cluster be dropped or relabelled; avoid interpreting batch-split clusters as subtypes. SOURCE: https://scomix.bd.com/hc/en-us/articles/360044971032-Bioinformatics-Primary-Analysis

label: Pitfall: gene filter scope and order changes BH and DEG count
text: PITFALL: The gene filter ('at least 10 total counts across all samples') changes the number of genes tested and therefore the BH-adjusted p-values and the DEG count. Common mistakes: computing the total over all 100k cells or all cell types instead of over the pseudobulk samples in this contrast; filtering before donor exclusion; using var['n_cells'] (which comes from the full 10M atlas); or using a per-sample rule such as edgeR filterByExpr or 'count>=10 in >=n samples' instead of a row-sum rule. CHECK: build the pseudobulk matrix (retained donors x {IFN-beta,PBS}, CD14 Mono only), then keep genes with row sum >= 10 across those pseudobulk columns; report genes before/after; verify the filter is applied before dispersion estimation, not after testing. IF FOUND: redo with the row-sum-over-retained-pseudobulks rule; note that the alternative reading (sum over all cells in the file) keeps far more genes and shifts padj, so report the sensitivity. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html (Pre-filtering) ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9136325/

label: PITFALL log-normalisation scale factor on shallow data
text: PITFALL: If a log-normalised HVG route is used, the scale factor is a hidden choice that matters for shallow data. scanpy normalize_total defaults to target_sum=None (median counts per cell) whereas Seurat and most tutorials use 1e4; when per-cell depth is far below the scale factor and most non-zero counts are 1, log1p of scaled counts inflates the contribution of low-abundance genes and creates depth-driven spurious variance, which changes which genes rank as highly variable. CHECK: compare the median UMIs per cell with 1e4, then run the dispersion-based HVG with target_sum=None and with target_sum=1e4 and measure overlap of the 2000 genes and the change in their median prevalence. IF FOUND (results differ): do not treat either as neutral; prefer a count-based selection (seurat_v3 on raw counts, which needs no scale factor) or state the target_sum used as an explicit assumption. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/more-norm.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7989636/ ; https://doi.org/10.1101/2022.05.06.490859 ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/biorxiv/early/2018/08/31/404962.full.pdf

label: PITFALL pooled fixed QC thresholds
text: PITFALL: One global fixed QC threshold applied to the pooled tumour+blood object is biased: tumour-tissue cells and PBMCs, and the two batches, have different count/gene distributions, so pooled thresholds or pooled MADs over-cut one group and under-cut the other, and strict cutoffs preferentially delete small low-RNA lineages. The retained PBMC count also depends on whether you filter before or after subsetting to PBMC. CHECK: plot log total counts and n_genes per sample and per batch for PBMC only; compare number retained under a global cutoff vs per-sample MAD cutoffs (e.g. 3-5 MADs); cross-tab removed cells by provisional lineage to see whether one lineage is being lost. IF FOUND: derive thresholds on PBMC samples (per sample or per batch), keep them lenient, and remove only clear low-quality tails; state the rule and the sensitivity of the retained count to it. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/quality-control-redux.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9912498/

label: Pitfall: shrunken vs unshrunken LFC and post-hoc vs threshold test
text: PITFALL: The '|log2FC| > 1' count depends heavily on WHICH log2FC is used. Unshrunken maximum-likelihood LFCs are huge and noisy for low-count genes (a 10-total-count filter keeps many such genes in small pseudobulks), while apeglm/ashr-shrunken LFCs pull them toward 0, so the two give different DEG counts. Separately, post-hoc filtering (Wald test of LFC=0, then |LFC|>1) is a different procedure from testing against a threshold (results(lfcThreshold=1) / lfc_null=1), which is much stricter. CHECK: compute the DEG count three ways: (a) padj<0.05 from the default LFC=0 Wald test plus unshrunken |LFC|>1, (b) same padj plus shrunken |LFC|>1, (c) threshold test; tabulate mean normalized count of genes that pass only under (a). IF FOUND (counts differ materially): the task wording 'adjusted p-value < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| > 1.0' matches the conventional post-hoc filter on the default results table, i.e. (a); report (a) as the answer and (b) as a sensitivity figure, and do not silently substitute shrunken LFCs or lfcThreshold. Shrinkage does not change padj. SOURCE: https://support.bioconductor.org/p/110307/ ; https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html (Log fold change shrinkage; Tests of log2 fold change above or below a threshold) ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/106073/

label: Pitfall: NA padj, independent filtering and Cook's defaults
text: PITFALL: DESeq2/PyDESeq2 set padj to NA/NaN for genes removed by independent filtering (low mean count) and p-value to NA for Cook's-distance outliers; defaults are PyDESeq2 DeseqStats(alpha=0.05, cooks_filter=True, independent_filter=True) and DeseqDataSet(refit_cooks=True, min_replicates=7). These defaults interact with the design: with '~condition' and >=7 donors per arm, outlier counts are replaced and refit; with '~donor + condition' there are no replicates per design cell, so outlier replacement does not occur. alpha in the independent filter should equal the padj cutoff (0.05; R's results() default is 0.1). NaN padj silently counts as 'not significant'. CHECK: count genes with NaN pvalue and NaN padj; confirm alpha=0.05; count how many genes were Cook's-refit or flagged; re-run with independent_filter=False and cooks_filter=False to see the range. IF FOUND: keep package defaults with alpha=0.05 for the reported number (that is what 'DESeq2 default' means), treat NaN padj as non-significant explicitly (e.g. fillna(1)), and report how many DEGs the filtering switches move. SOURCE: https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.ds.DeseqStats.html ; https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.dds.DeseqDataSet.html ; https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html ('Why are some p values set to NA?', Independent filtering) ; https://www.seqanswers.com/forum/applications-forums/rna-sequencing/38200-paired-design-versus-unpaired-design-in-deseq2

label: PITFALL median genes depends on order and layer
text: PITFALL: The median genes per cell is silently changed by processing order. It differs if computed before vs after cell filtering, on all cells vs PBMC only, on RSEC vs DBEC, or after a gene filter (min_cells) or HVG subset has dropped columns; scanpy's filter_cells writes n_genes at call time and it is not updated later. CHECK: recompute n_genes as (counts>0).sum(axis=1) on the final retained PBMC cells directly from the chosen raw count layer with all 386 genes, and compare with any stored obs column. IF FOUND: report the recomputed value on retained PBMC cells only, and do not filter genes or select HVGs before computing it. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/

label: PITFALL batch_key changes HVG set
text: PITFALL: Adding batch_key (per-donor HVG selection) changes the selected genes and is not asked for. With batch_key, scanpy 'seurat_v3' ranks by median rank across batches and 'seurat_v3_paper' by number of batches first; these gave 764/2000 vs 1990/2000 overlap with Seurat in a scanpy test, so the HVG set is very sensitive to this option. The data has no donor column in obs anyway (only an obs_names prefix), so any batch key would be a constructed, unverified variable. CHECK: confirm obs has no columns; if a prefix-derived sample label is built, count how many groups it gives versus the stated 4 donors; compare HVG sets with and without batch_key. IF FOUND: use a single global selection (batch_key=None) as the primary answer because the task asks for top 2,000 HVGs across the dataset; report a batch-aware result only as a sensitivity check and name the flavor. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/pull/2792 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.16/OSCA.basic/feature-selection.html

label: Pitfall: raw integer counts and sum aggregation
text: PITFALL: Pseudobulk DE needs RAW integer counts aggregated by SUM. Normalizing/log-transforming X before aggregation, averaging instead of summing, or feeding non-integer values makes the negative-binomial model invalid and changes dispersions and DEG counts. This file has no 'counts' layer and no .raw, so everything rests on X. CHECK: on the CD14 Mono subset verify X.data are all non-negative integers (np.allclose(x, np.round(x))), the max is well above ~10, and per-cell row sums match obs tscp_count / expm1(log1p_total_counts); after aggregation confirm pseudobulk library sizes scale with cell number. IF FOUND (X is normalized or logged): do not run DESeq2 on it; try to invert the transform exactly (expm1 then rescale by total counts) and verify integers, otherwise flag that a count model cannot be used. Never call sc.pp.normalize_total/log1p before pseudobulking. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/conditions/differential-gene-expression/ ; https://decoupler.scverse.org/en/stable/notebooks/scell/rna_psbk.html ; https://training.galaxyproject.org/training-material/topics/single-cell/tutorials/pseudobulk-analysis/tutorial.html

label: PITFALL same-tag doublets inflate monocytes
text: PITFALL: Sample-tag demultiplexing removes only cross-sample multiplets; doublets of two cells with the same tag (including heterotypic monocyte+T or monocyte+B doublets) remain and are invisible to tags. With only 3-6 tags per cartridge a large share of doublets are same-tag. Monocyte-containing doublets co-express CD14/S100A9 with CD3E/MS4A1 and inflate both the retained count and the monocyte count. An upper total-count cutoff alone is a weak doublet detector. CHECK: look for clusters or cells co-expressing myeloid markers (CD14, S100A9, FCN1) with T (CD3D/CD3E/TRAC), B (MS4A1/CD79A) or NK (GNLY/KLRF1) markers and with high total counts; run Scrublet/scDblFinder per cartridge (the batch column, i.e. per capture), not per sample tag and not on the merged object. IF FOUND: remove or separately label doublet clusters before counting lineages, and report the monocyte count with and without them. Note that doublet simulators are less validated on 386-gene targeted data, so confirm calls with marker co-expression. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9204188/ ; https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/scDblFinder/inst/doc/scDblFinder.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6625319/ ; https://bd-rhapsody-bioinfo-docs.genomics.bd.com/steps/steps%5Fsample%5Ftag.html

label: Pitfall: size factors under sparsity and global IFN shift
text: PITFALL: Size-factor normalization can be distorted in two ways here. (1) Sparse pseudobulks: with only ~5-30 cells per sample most genes have a zero in at least one sample, so median-of-ratios uses only the few genes non-zero everywhere (or errors with 'every gene contains at least one zero'). (2) Global shift: IFN-beta changes a large, mostly up-regulated block of genes; median-of-ratios assumes the up/down changes are roughly balanced around unchanged genes, and a one-sided shift biases all LFCs and thus which genes cross |LFC|>1. CHECK: count genes with no zeros across the retained pseudobulks (the set that drives size factors); compare DESeq2 size factors with total-count ratios per sample and with cells per sample; inspect the MA plot / LFC histogram, whose mode should sit at 0 for the bulk of non-ISG genes. IF FOUND (few all-nonzero genes, size factors disagreeing with library size, or LFC mode off zero): report it and run a sensitivity analysis with an alternative normalization (poscounts-type size factors, or library-size/TMM factors, or control_genes restricted to stably expressed genes); keep default median-of-ratios for the headline number unless it fails outright. SOURCE: https://rdrr.io/bioc/DESeq2/man/estimateSizeFactors.html ; https://github.com/HelenaLC/muscat/issues/97 ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/113059/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/132144/

label: PITFALL classical vs non-classical monocytes vs DC
text: PITFALL: 'Classical monocyte' is easily over- or under-counted because neighbouring myeloid populations share markers. Usual monocyte markers LYZ, S100A8, VCAN, CST3 are NOT in this 386-gene panel; available classical markers are CD14, S100A9, S100A12, FCN1, CD36, CD33, CCR2, TLR2, ITGAM, SELL. Non-classical (CD16+) monocytes are FCGR3A+, CX3CR1+, VMO1+ with low CD14/S100A12; cDC2 are CD1C+, FCER1A+, CLEC10A+, FLT3+, HLA-DQB1 high; pDC are IL3RA+, TCF4+, IRF8+, TLR7/9+. FCGR3A is also high in NK cells so it is not monocyte-specific. CHECK: within the myeloid compartment, sub-cluster and plot CD14/S100A12/FCN1 against FCGR3A/VMO1/CX3CR1 and CD1C/FCER1A/CLEC10A; confirm the cluster called classical monocyte is CD14-high, S100A12-high, FCGR3A-low, CD1C-low. IF FOUND: decide and state whether the 'classical-monocyte lineage' count includes only CD14+ classical monocytes or all monocytes; keep DCs out; report the count under both definitions so the difference is visible. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5775029/ ; https://www.cell.com/immunity/fulltext/S1074-7613(19)30334-6 ; https://azimuth.hubmapconsortium.org/references/human_pbmc/

label: Pitfall: contrast direction, reference level, unused categories
text: PITFALL: Wrong contrast, reference level or leftover categorical levels. Factor reference levels default to alphabetical order ('IFN-beta' sorts before 'PBS', so an unspecified contrast returns PBS vs IFN-beta), and after subsetting, the obs categoricals still carry 91 cytokine and 12 donor levels; unused levels or dropped donors can give a rank-deficient design or a wrong coefficient. In a '~donor + condition' fit it is also easy to pull a donor coefficient instead of the condition coefficient. Some PyDESeq2 versions rewrite underscores in factor levels to hyphens and the deprecated ref_level argument is ignored. CHECK: call remove_unused_categories() on donor and cytokine after subsetting; request the contrast explicitly as ['cytokine','IFN-beta','PBS'] (numerator IFN-beta, denominator PBS); sanity-check sign on canonical interferon-stimulated genes (ISG15, IFIT1, IFIT3, MX1, IFI44L, OAS1 must have large positive LFC and tiny padj); verify the design matrix is full rank with n_donors + 1 columns. IF FOUND: fix the contrast/levels and re-run; the DEG count itself is symmetric in sign, but a wrong coefficient or rank-deficient design gives a completely different count. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html (Note on factor levels; Model matrix not full rank) ; https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.dds.DeseqDataSet.html ; https://github.com/scverse/PyDESeq2/blob/main/src/pydeseq2/dds.py

label: PITFALL which matrix each metric is computed on
text: PITFALL: The three requested numbers can be computed on different matrices, and habitual extra QC shifts all of them. The gene filter (<10 cells) is stated as a step before HVG selection; median UMIs per cell and the percent of non-zero entries equal to 1 are described as dataset-level statistics. Computing them after gene filtering removes rare-gene entries (which are disproportionately counts of 1) and lowers cell totals; tutorial-style cell filtering (e.g. filter_cells min_genes=200, mito or MAD filters, doublet removal) is not requested and would drop cells in shallow data, changing the median, the percentage and every gene's detection count. CHECK: compute the median UMIs/cell and pct-equal-1 both on the unfiltered matrix and after the gene filter, and see whether they differ at the reported precision; assert n_obs is unchanged (11693) at the end. IF FOUND (they differ): report the unfiltered-matrix value for the two dataset-level statistics as primary, note the post-filter value, and apply no cell filtering. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/488

label: Pitfall: NB false positives with many donors, permutation control
text: PITFALL: Negative-binomial methods (DESeq2, edgeR) have been reported to exceed nominal FDR in human population samples with many replicates per group, mostly because of outlier counts; with up to 12 donors per arm and small noisy pseudobulks the DEG list may contain outlier-driven calls. The original report is contested (later papers attribute much of it to outliers fixable by winsorization and to flawed permutation of library size), so treat this as a diagnostic, not a reason to abandon DESeq2. CHECK: negative control by permutation: within each donor randomly swap the IFN-beta/PBS labels (or flip a random half of donors), re-run the identical pipeline several times, and expect ~0 DEGs at padj<0.05 & |LFC|>1; also check that top DEGs are supported by most donors (same sign of within-donor log ratio in the large majority of donors) rather than one extreme pseudobulk; optionally compare with a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank on log-CPM per donor. IF FOUND (permutations yield many DEGs, or many DEGs are single-donor driven): keep Cook's filtering on, report the outlier-driven fraction, and flag the headline count as an upper bound. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-022-02648-4 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-024-03230-w ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-024-03231-9

label: PITFALL low-density neutrophils in PBMC
text: PITFALL: PBMC preparations from cancer patients, especially during chemotherapy, often contain low-density neutrophils/granulocytes (PMN-MDSC) that co-purify in the mononuclear layer. They share S100A9/S100A12 with classical monocytes and can be absorbed into the monocyte cluster, inflating the count. CHECK: in S100A9/S100A12-high cells, test for neutrophil genes that are in the panel: CXCR2, CXCR1, MME, VNN2, CMTM2, AQP9, MMP9, ARG1, and immature granule genes ELANE, AZU1, DEFA3, DEFA4, BPI, CTSG, CD24; neutrophils are also CD14-low, HLA-DRA/CD74-low and have few detected genes. Also check eosinophil/basophil genes CLC, EPX, CPA3, and whether such cells differ by treatment timepoint. IF FOUND: label granulocytes as a separate lineage and exclude them from the classical-monocyte count; do not let a low-gene QC cutoff silently decide this, state whether they were removed by QC or kept and labelled. SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.684119/full ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/immunology/articles/10.3389/fimmu.2021.703846/full ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41590-026-02671-8

label: Pitfall: ambient RNA and cell-type label shift under stimulation
text: PITFALL: Strong perturbations create condition-specific ambient RNA and can shift cell-type labels: highly induced transcripts from other cell types bleed into monocyte profiles, and IFN-stimulated monocytes may be annotated differently (e.g. CD14 Mono vs CD16 Mono) so that the 'CD14 Mono' set is not the same population in both arms. Either can add DEGs that are not monocyte-intrinsic responses. CHECK: compare the fraction and number of cells labelled CD14 Mono (and CD16 Mono) per donor between IFN-beta and PBS; look in the DEG list for marker genes of other lineages (T/NK: CD3E, NKG7, GNLY; B: MS4A1, CD79A; platelets: PPBP, PF4; erythroid: HBB, HBA1) and for mitochondrial/ribosomal genes. IF FOUND: this does not change the required method or the reported count (the task fixes the cell_type column), but report the label-shift size and how many DEGs are other-lineage markers as a caveat on interpretation. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.multisample/ambient-problems.html ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12864-023-09822-3 ; https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/introduction-to-ambient-rna-correction

label: PITFALL explicit zeros inflate nnz
text: PITFALL: Counting non-zero entries with sparse .nnz / getnnz counts STORED values including explicit zeros (and un-summed duplicates), so both the denominator of 'percent of non-zero entries equal to 1' and per-gene detection counts can be inflated. CHECK: on X run (X.data == 0).sum(), X.has_canonical_format, and (X.data < 0).sum(); compare X.nnz with X.count_nonzero(). IF FOUND (any explicit zeros or duplicates): call X.sum_duplicates() and X.eliminate_zeros() first, and define the percentage as 100 * (X.data == 1).sum() / (X.data != 0).sum() and detection as (X > 0) per gene. Report as a percentage (0-100), not a fraction. SOURCE: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.getnnz.html

label: PITFALL per-cell gating vs cluster annotation
text: PITFALL: Counting a lineage by per-cell gating on one marker (e.g. CD14>0) undercounts badly because of dropout, while cluster-level labels depend on clustering resolution, neighbour number and mixed clusters; either can move the monocyte count by a large fraction. CHECK: annotate at cluster level from several markers per lineage, then (1) repeat at 2-3 Leiden resolutions and neighbour settings and see how the monocyte count moves, (2) inspect each cluster for mixed marker expression and sub-cluster mixed ones, (3) compare with a per-cell multi-gene score (e.g. sc.tl.score_genes on CD14, S100A9, S100A12, FCN1) to find monocyte-like cells stranded in other clusters. IF FOUND: use cluster-level labels refined by sub-clustering of the myeloid compartment, and report the range of counts across reasonable settings instead of a single unexamined number. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/annotation.html ; https://doi.org/10.31219/osf.io/ndafw ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10189648/

label: PITFALL joint clustering and over-integration
text: PITFALL: Clustering blood and tumour cells together, or batch-correcting across them, can distort the blood annotation: tumour macrophages (C1QA, C1QB, CD163, VSIG4, SPP1, LIPA high) pull the myeloid cluster definition away from blood monocytes, and integration methods over-correct when cell-type composition differs between batches, merging distinct types. Tissue and batch may be partly confounded here (sample names suggest one cartridge holds PBMC+tissue tags and the other only PBMC tags). CHECK: cross-tabulate batch x source x sample; cluster PBMC cells alone and compare the monocyte count with the count from joint clustering; after any Harmony/BBKNN step confirm lineage markers remain cluster-specific and that monocytes and DCs or NK and T did not merge. IF FOUND: subset to PBMC before normalisation/PCA/clustering for the blood characterisation, and use batch correction only if the same lineage visibly splits by batch; prefer the uncorrected PBMC-only result when the two disagree. SOURCE: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2021.11.15.468733v2 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8098019/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12067276/

label: PITFALL min_cells threshold and filter order
text: PITFALL: Gene-filter threshold semantics are easy to get wrong by one or by kind. 'Filter genes detected in fewer than 10 cells' means keep genes with n_cells >= 10; sc.pp.filter_genes(min_cells=10) keeps genes 'expressed in at least min_cells cells' (inclusive), whereas min_counts=10 thresholds total UMIs instead and a strict '> 10' drops genes detected in exactly 10 cells. The filter must run BEFORE HVG selection because the seurat_v3 loess mean-variance trend and the dispersion bins are fitted over all genes present, so the gene universe changes the ranking. CHECK: after filtering, assert min over genes of (X > 0).sum(axis=0) equals >= 10 and count how many genes sit exactly at 10; compute HVG prevalence from the raw count matrix (cells with count > 0), not from normalised or scaled values, and not from a stale var['n_cells'] column computed before any later subsetting. IF FOUND (mismatch): redo the filter with min_cells=10 on raw counts and recompute HVGs. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.filter_genes.html ; https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/488

label: PITFALL HVG and normalisation on small panel
text: PITFALL (lower confidence, reasoned from panel design rather than a dedicated source): whole-transcriptome preprocessing defaults misbehave on a 386-gene pre-selected immune panel. Selecting 2000 HVGs is meaningless and selecting a few hundred discards lineage markers that the panel was built around; normalising to target_sum=1e4 when cells have only tens to hundreds of molecules inflates low-count cells; and library-size normalisation is compositional on a panel dominated by a few highly expressed genes (e.g. HLA-DRA, CD74, FTH1, GAPDH, IGKC), which differ strongly between lineages. CHECK: confirm how many genes enter PCA; check which genes take the largest share of counts per lineage; confirm canonical markers (CD3E, MS4A1, CD14, NKG7) survived feature selection. IF FOUND: keep all panel genes (or drop only never-detected genes), normalise to the median library size, log1p, and use a modest number of PCs; check that lineage calls are stable to this choice. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11229035/

label: PITFALL seurat_v3 loess dependency and failures
text: PITFALL: seurat_v3 HVG selection can fail or be silently swapped. It needs the optional scikit-misc package (loess); and the loess fit can raise 'reciprocal condition number' or 'There are other near singularities' errors, attributed to an excess of all-zero genes in a (sub)set of cells, most often when batch_key is used. A common bad reaction is to fall back to the default dispersion flavor or change span without saying so, which changes the HVG set. CHECK: try 'import skmisc' before the run; make sure the min_cells gene filter was applied first; if the fit errors, check for genes with zero counts in the cells being fitted. IF FOUND: install scikit-misc (pip install scikit-misc) rather than changing flavor; remove all-zero genes for the failing subset rather than altering span; if a different flavor or span is unavoidable, say so and report it as a deviation. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2669 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1504 ; https://github.com/chanzuckerberg/cellxgene-census/blob/40b42116/api/python/cellxgene_census/src/cellxgene_census/experimental/pp/_highly_variable_genes.py

label: PITFALL exactly 2000 HVGs and median rounding
text: PITFALL: The HVG set may not contain exactly 2,000 genes, and the final integers hide rounding choices. With dispersion-based flavors, a mean-expression bin holding a single gene has its normalised dispersion artificially set to 1 and NaN dispersions can occur; with n_top_genes set, all mean/dispersion cutoffs are ignored. The median of 2,000 prevalence values is the mean of the two middle values and can end in .5, while the answer must be an int. CHECK: assert adata.var['highly_variable'].sum() == 2000; check for NaN in the ranking statistic; compute the median prevalence as a float and see whether it is fractional; confirm the median UMI is taken over per-cell row sums of raw counts (axis=1). IF FOUND: fix the selection so exactly 2000 genes are flagged; if the median is x.5, state the rounding rule used. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html

label: sc10 data layout from headers
text: FILE STRUCTURE (headers only, values not inspected): 157798551.node is an AnnData h5ad with 6420 cells x 19918 genes; X is a DENSE float32 matrix; layers['raw_counts'] is a dense int64 matrix; var has columns 'mean' and 'std' (exactly what sc.pp.scale writes, so X is probably z-scored/scaled log-normalized data - verify); uns['log1p'] exists but is an EMPTY dict (no 'base' key); obs has 'sample' (one category, '4T1_viable', mouse) and 'n_genes' (so filter_cells was already run); there is no .raw. Gene names are mouse symbols mixed with clone IDs like 'RP23-317L18.4'. The two matrices are ~0.5 GB and ~1 GB in memory; load raw_counts and convert to sparse CSR to save memory.

label: HVG on scaled X is invalid
text: PITFALL: adata.X in this file is very likely already scaled (z-scored; var has 'mean'/'std' from sc.pp.scale), and running sc.pp.highly_variable_genes on scaled data is wrong - every gene has variance ~1 and mean ~0, the 'seurat' flavor applies expm1 to z-scores, and it may either crash (NaN bins, 'Bin edges must be unique', KeyError) or SILENTLY return a meaningless 2000-gene list. CHECK: X.min() < 0, per-gene mean of X ~0 and std ~1, and whether X.max() is exactly 10 (max_value clipping); compare with layers['raw_counts'] being non-negative integers. IF FOUND: do not use X; rebuild the input from layers['raw_counts'] (normalize_total + log1p for flavor 'seurat'/'cell_ranger', or pass layer='raw_counts' for 'seurat_v3'). SOURCE: https://nbisweden.github.io/workshop-archive/workshop-scRNAseq/2023-01-30/labs/compiled/scanpy/scanpy_03_integration.html ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.scale.html ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/scanpy-pp-highly-variable-genes-and-raise-keyerror/578

label: HVG flavor vs input matrix mismatch
text: PITFALL: each scanpy HVG flavor expects a different input and scanpy does not stop you if you give the wrong one: flavor='seurat' (the default) and 'cell_ranger' expect LOG-normalized data; 'seurat_v3'/'seurat_v3_paper' expect RAW integer counts and only emit a UserWarning ('expects raw count data, but non-integers were found') if given something else. Feeding counts to 'seurat' or log/scaled data to 'seurat_v3' runs and gives a wrong list. CHECK: before each call, assert the matrix state - counts: non-negative integers; log-normalized: non-negative, non-integer, max roughly < 15, expm1 row sums constant; and treat the seurat_v3 non-integer warning as an error. IF FOUND: for seurat_v3 use sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, flavor='seurat_v3', n_top_genes=2000, layer='raw_counts'); for seurat/cell_ranger first set X = raw_counts, then normalize_total and log1p exactly once. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2242 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/how-to-handle-data-lognormalization-when-using-highly-variable-genes-with-flavor-seurat-v3/1076

label: HVG method choice dominates the answer
text: PITFALL: the choice of HVG method changes the gene list far more than any cleaning step - published comparisons report low overlap between methods (mean pairwise overlap ~24% across methods in one benchmark; 138 of 500 genes shared between Seurat and scanpy flavor='seurat' in a scanpy issue), so 'the 2000 HVGs' is not method-independent and a list from the wrong flavor will score poorly against a reference made with another. CHECK: compute the 2000-gene lists for flavor='seurat' on log-normalized data, flavor='seurat_v3' on layer='raw_counts' (and optionally 'cell_ranger') and report the pairwise overlaps. IF FOUND (overlap well below 100%): state explicitly which flavor is the primary answer and why; the scanpy default call sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=2000) means flavor='seurat' on log-normalized data, and seurat_v3 on counts is the main alternative; always pass flavor explicitly rather than relying on the default, and do not mix in R Seurat's FindVariableFeatures, which does not reproduce scanpy's lists. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.64898/2025.12.02.691907 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2780 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3542 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-025-03887-x

label: Normalization scale factor changes dispersion HVGs
text: PITFALL: for the dispersion flavors ('seurat', 'cell_ranger') the result depends on how the log-normalized matrix was made (target_sum=1e4 vs the scanpy default target_sum=None = median library size, exclude_highly_expressed, log base), because the size of the scale factor relative to the +1 pseudocount shifts means and dispersions; seurat_v3 on raw counts is unaffected. CHECK: var['mean'] in this file holds the per-gene mean of the matrix that was scaled; recompute normalize_total(target_sum=1e4)+log1p and normalize_total(target_sum=None)+log1p from layers['raw_counts'] and see which per-gene means (and ddof=1 stds vs var['std']) reproduce var['mean']/var['std']; alternatively de-scale X*std+mean (only valid where X was not clipped at max_value). IF FOUND: use the normalization that reproduces var['mean'], because that is the log-normalized matrix the original pipeline had when HVGs would have been called; if neither matches, say so and report sensitivity of the HVG list to target_sum. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.normalize_total.html ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.scale.html ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/more-norm.html

label: Empty uns log1p dict after h5ad read
text: PITFALL: after reading an h5ad, adata.uns['log1p'] is an empty dict (the 'base': None entry is lost on write) - this file has exactly that - and scanpy versions before 1.9.4 crash with KeyError: 'base' in highly_variable_genes(flavor='seurat') and rank_genes_groups; also, because uns['log1p'] exists, sc.pp.log1p on freshly normalized counts prints 'adata.X seems to be already log-transformed', which tempts analysts to skip the log (HVG then runs on un-logged data) or to log twice. CHECK: print adata.uns['log1p'] and the scanpy version; after preparing X confirm it was logged exactly once (max value roughly 5-10 for CP10k data, not thousands and not <3). IF FOUND: build a fresh AnnData from raw_counts (or del adata.uns['log1p']) before normalize_total+log1p, or set adata.uns['log1p']['base'] = None; do not wrap the call in try/except to hide the KeyError. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2239 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2181 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/pull/2546 ; https://github.com/scverse/anndata/issues/865

label: sc12 data layout: Tapestri multi-sample protein h5
text: DATA LAYOUT (from HDF5 headers only, no values analysed): GSE276492_combined.h5 is a Mission Bio Tapestri DNA+protein file (pipeline 2.0.1) holding 5 samples as top-level groups (GSM8499463_S7 ... GSM8499467_S15). Per sample, called cells are at <sample>/assays/protein_read_counts/layers/read_counts (int64, cells x 48 antibodies; 2518, 5988, 6912, 4826 and 3714 cells), antibody names at .../ca/id, barcodes at .../ra/barcode; a much larger unfiltered table sits at <sample>/all_barcodes/protein_read_counts (e.g. 641343 barcodes). The 48-antibody TotalSeq-D heme panel includes three isotype controls named IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b. Counts are reads, not UMIs. No normalized layer is stored in the file.

label: n_top_genes semantics and exact count
text: PITFALL: with n_top_genes set, scanpy ignores min_mean/max_mean/min_disp/max_disp entirely and ranks by normalized dispersion within mean-expression bins (n_bins=20; a bin with a single gene gets normalized dispersion artificially set to 1; genes with zero dispersion become NaN); calling highly_variable_genes WITHOUT n_top_genes instead returns a cutoff-based set of arbitrary size that is not 'the top 2000', and truncating that set is not equivalent. In the dispersion flavors the cut is 'dispersions_norm >= value of the 2000th gene', so ties can return slightly more than 2000. CHECK: adata.var['highly_variable'].sum() == 2000 exactly, the returned names are unique, and no selected gene has NaN dispersions_norm/variances_norm. IF FOUND (not 2000): pass n_top_genes=2000 explicitly with default cutoffs; if ties give >2000, break them deterministically by dispersions_norm then gene order and say so; never pad the list with arbitrary genes. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2230 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/main/src/scanpy/preprocessing/_highly_variable_genes.py

label: PITFALL log of zero makes non-finite CLR values
text: PITFALL: A textbook centred log-ratio (log(x) minus mean log(x), no pseudocount) or any plain log on antibody read counts returns -Inf/NaN wherever a count is zero, so the fraction of finite normalized values drops below 1 purely because of the formula chosen; muon documents that its flavor='standard' CLR 'may yield infinite values if the input contains zeros'. CHECK: count zeros in read_counts before normalizing; after normalizing compute np.isfinite(dense_matrix).sum() / dense_matrix.size on the full cells x antibodies matrix that is actually stored (not on sparse .data only, and not after np.nan_to_num). IF FOUND: use a zero-safe variant (log1p-based 'seurat' CLR, CLR on counts+1 as in the original CITE-seq paper, or asinh) rather than patching non-finite values afterwards, and report the fraction measured on the final stored layer. SOURCE: https://muon.scverse.org/stable/generated/muon.prot.pp.clr.html ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/1377

label: seurat_v3 loess failure and span
text: PITFALL: flavor='seurat_v3' fits a loess of log10(variance) on log10(mean) of raw counts and fails with ValueError 'reciprocal condition number' / 'There are other near singularities' (or even segfaults in old scikit-misc) when the matrix contains all-zero or near-constant genes; the common 'fix' of raising span (0.3 -> 0.5/1) changes the fitted trend and therefore the gene ranking. It also needs the scikit-misc package. CHECK: count genes with zero total in layers['raw_counts'] (and zero variance) before calling; confirm skmisc imports. IF FOUND: exclude only the all-zero genes from the HVG computation (they can never be HVGs) and keep span at the default 0.3; if you must change span, report it as a deviation and compare the list with the default-span attempt. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1504 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2669 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/pull/3980

label: PITFALL zero-read cells and zero-variance antibodies give NaN
text: PITFALL: Tapestri cells are called from the DNA library, not from protein, so a called cell can have zero or very few antibody reads; dividing by a per-cell total, size factor or geometric mean that is zero gives NaN/Inf for that whole row, and z-scoring an antibody column with zero variance gives NaN for that whole column. CHECK: per-cell total protein reads (minimum, number of cells with total == 0, number of antibodies detected per cell) and per-antibody variance within each sample. IF FOUND: use a normalization that is defined at zero (pseudocount CLR / asinh), do not add a z-score step without guarding zero-variance columns, and state explicitly whether such cells were kept or dropped because dropping them changes the denominator of any 'fraction finite' check. SOURCE: https://support.missionbio.com/hc/en-us/articles/360053187154-File-report-html ; https://muon.scverse.org/stable/generated/muon.prot.pp.clr.html

label: PITFALL use called cells not all_barcodes
text: PITFALL: Normalizing the wrong table. Each sample holds both an unfiltered all_barcodes/protein_read_counts table (hundreds of thousands of barcodes, mostly empty droplets) and the called-cell table assays/protein_read_counts; Mission Bio's own loader is used with raw=False so only cell-associated barcodes are analysed. Normalizing all_barcodes makes the matrix dominated by empty, near-zero rows. CHECK: confirm the matrix normalized has one row per called cell (rows equal to the assays/.../ra/barcode length per sample, 48 columns) and that orientation is cells x antibodies. IF FOUND: normalize the assays (called-cell) matrix; use all_barcodes only as a background reference if a background-based method is chosen. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/curated_notebooks/dna-protein-multisample.html

label: Do not re-filter before HVG
text: PITFALL: extra cell or gene filtering before HVG selection (filter_genes min_cells, QC re-filtering, dropping mitochondrial 'mt-' / ribosomal 'Rps'/'Rpl' genes, subsetting cells) changes the gene universe, the mean-expression bins and the loess trend, so the 2000-gene list shifts; HVG methods are known to over-select mito/ribo genes and analysts often remove them out of habit, but the task asks for the HVGs of the given object. The object already carries obs['n_genes'], i.e. it was QC-filtered upstream. CHECK: confirm you are using all 6420 cells and all 19918 genes, and count how many selected HVGs are mt-/Rps/Rpl genes. IF FOUND: keep the object as given (only all-zero genes may be masked for the loess); report mito/ribo HVGs as a note rather than deleting them and back-filling, unless the task explicitly asks for exclusion. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.02.12.430764 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/ ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1504

label: PITFALL merged multi-sample file: normalize per sample
text: PITFALL: The file is a merged multi-sample h5 (5 samples), and treating it as one sample or reading only the first group silently normalizes a fifth of the data; methods that estimate anything across cells (per-antibody CLR, NSP, dsb, z-scoring) also mix sample-specific depth and staining differences if run on the pooled matrix, and cell barcodes can repeat across samples. Mission Bio's multisample workflow loops 'for sample in group' and handles protein per sample. CHECK: every sample group has a normalized layer of the same shape as its counts; antibody id order is identical across samples; barcodes are unique after prefixing with the sample name. IF FOUND: normalize each sample separately, prefix barcodes, then concatenate; compute any whole-dataset summary (such as fraction finite) as pooled finite count over pooled size, not as an unweighted mean of per-sample fractions. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/curated_notebooks/dna-protein-multisample.html ; https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dsb/vignettes/additional_topics.html

label: No batch_key for single-sample data
text: PITFALL: batch-aware HVG selection (batch_key) uses different ranking rules (number of batches a gene is HVG in, median rank; 'seurat_v3' and 'seurat_v3_paper' order these differently) and silently filters unexpressed genes, so adding batch_key changes the list; it is only meaningful with several batches. CHECK: obs['sample'] here has a single category, so there is nothing to stratify by. IF FOUND (single batch): call highly_variable_genes with batch_key=None; with batch_key=None 'seurat_v3' and 'seurat_v3_paper' give the same result. label: PITFALL CLR axis ambiguity (per cell vs per antibody)
text: PITFALL: 'CLR' means two different things and tools default differently: within each cell across antibodies (original CITE-seq, Mosaic, Seurat margin=2, muon axis=1) versus per antibody across cells (Seurat default margin=1, muon default axis=0, Mission Bio R 'clr_by_feature'). Per-cell CLR assumes total antibody signal is comparable across cells and fails when cell types lack markers in the panel; per-antibody CLR fails when sequencing depth per cell varies a lot. A transposed matrix silently swaps the two. CHECK: confirm matrix orientation (n_cells x 48) and which axis the function centres on; for an unshifted per-cell CLR the row means of the output are about 0. IF FOUND: choose the axis deliberately (per-cell corrects depth, which matters when per-cell protein totals vary widely) and record axis and pseudocount in the output. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/871 ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/3605 ; https://muon.scverse.org/stable/generated/muon.prot.pp.clr.html

label: PITFALL total-count normalization is biased for antibody panels
text: PITFALL: Applying the RNA recipe (scale each cell to a common total, then log1p) to antibody counts. With only a few dozen pre-selected antibodies the counts are strongly compositional: one or two abundant markers dominate the per-cell total, so total-count scaling makes every other marker depend on them; OSCA says library-size factors for ADTs introduce composition bias and recommends geometric-mean/median-based or isotype-control-based size factors. CHECK: per cell, the share of protein reads taken by the top 1-3 antibodies, and whether per-cell totals differ systematically between cell populations. IF FOUND: prefer a ratio-based method (CLR with pseudocount, Mosaic NSP/asinh, or control/median-based size factors) over normalize_total+log1p. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/integrating-with-protein-abundance.html ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/surface-protein/normalization/

The required output key is 'top_marker_genes' even though the content is the HVG list, and it must hold all 2000 names. CHECK: adata.var_names.is_unique; every reported name is in the original var index; len(list) == 2000 and len(set(list)) == 2000; eval_answer.json parses as JSON with that single key. label: PITFALL isotype control columns in the protein panel
text: PITFALL: Three of the 48 columns (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b) are isotype controls, not biology. CLR across antibodies ignores the information they carry and, if left in, they enter the per-cell geometric mean; treating them as markers also pollutes clustering. Removing them changes the matrix size, so results depend on whether they were kept. CHECK: locate the three IgG columns; look at how isotype counts scale with each cell's total protein reads (a strong relationship indicates depth/non-specific binding noise). IF FOUND: keep the choice explicit; either use the controls for noise correction (dsb step II, control-based size factors) or keep them in the stored normalized matrix but exclude them from downstream features, and say which. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11568108/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/integrating-with-protein-abundance.html

label: PITFALL dsb preconditions on Tapestri data
text: PITFALL: dsb looks applicable (unfiltered barcodes and isotype controls exist) but has preconditions: it standardizes each antibody by the mean and standard deviation of background droplets, so an antibody with zero spread in the chosen background gives a division by zero (this follows from the documented formula), a badly chosen background (including real cells, or only near-zero barcodes) distorts every value, and here the all_barcodes barcode strings are stored with a different width than the called-cell barcodes so cells cannot be excluded from the background without first reconciling the formats. sc-best-practices says that without both empty droplets and isotype controls you should fall back to CLR. CHECK: background barcodes exclude called cells after matching barcode formats; every antibody has non-zero SD in the background; result is finite. IF FOUND: fall back to pseudocount CLR, or dsb's ModelNegativeADTnorm which needs no empty droplets. SOURCE: https://search.r-project.org/CRAN/refmans/dsb/html/DSBNormalizeProtein.html ; https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dsb/vignettes/no_empty_drops.html ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/surface_protein/normalization.html

label: PITFALL integer dtype and random jitter in normalization
text: PITFALL: Implementation traps that corrupt the normalized layer without an error: the counts are int64, so in-place division or assignment into the integer array truncates values; Mosaic's asinh/NSP methods add random Gaussian jitter (sd 0.5) to the counts, which makes output non-reproducible unless random_state is set and makes some jittered counts negative, so any hand-written log applied after jitter yields NaN; NSP additionally rescales reads and resets its scale to 1 if more than 5% of cells would end with zero reads. CHECK: cast counts to float64 before normalizing; the normalized layer is float, has exactly the same shape as the counts, and is stored as a named layer alongside the untouched raw counts; fix the random seed. IF FOUND: redo the normalization on a float copy with a fixed seed and keep raw counts unchanged. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.normalize_reads.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/missionbio.demultiplex.protein.nsp.NSP.html

label: PITFALL trajectory is method-dependent; test stability
text: PITFALL: Trajectory methods always return an ordering, even when the data are discrete clusters or when 'dominant' is ambiguous; pseudotime is a hypothesis, and results from non-linear embeddings (UMAP/t-SNE-based orderings) are especially sensitive to preprocessing. Different analysts will get different terminal groups purely from choices of HVG number, n_pcs, n_neighbors and method. CHECK: derive the axis three ways on the same preprocessed data (PC1 of HVGs, diffusion component 1, DPT/PAGA path) and confirm they agree (|Spearman| above about 0.8); repeat over a small grid (e.g. 1000/2000/4000 HVGs, 15/30/50 PCs, k=15/30) and measure Jaccard overlap of terminal-group membership and of the top-N marker list; inspect cell density along the axis to see whether it is a continuum or two/three separated clusters. IF FOUND: if the ends are discrete clusters, define terminal groups as the Leiden clusters at the two extremes (ordered by mean axis value or PAGA path) rather than arbitrary pseudotime quantiles; if methods disagree, prefer the axis that is stable across the grid and compute pseudotime in PCA/diffusion space, never on UMAP coordinates; report only markers that recur across settings. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11844634/ ; https://journals.biologists.com/dev/article/146/12/dev170506/19458/Concepts-and-limitations-for-learning ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9527995/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/trajectory-analysis.html

label: PITFALL outliers and root define the endpoints
text: PITFALL: The ends of a diffusion component, DPT ordering or cluster-MST are easily captured by a handful of outlier cells or one tiny, distant cluster (doublets, low-quality cells, a rare contaminant), and DPT also depends on the arbitrary root cell; terminal groups then contain a few odd cells and markers are unrepresentative. CHECK: look at the distribution of DC1/PC1 (a long tail from under about 2 percent of cells signals outliers); count cells in each terminal group (each should be a substantial population, not a few dozen cells); rerun DPT rooted at each extreme and confirm the ordering is simply reversed; check the terminal clusters are connected to the main body in PAGA rather than isolated. IF FOUND: remove or set aside the outlier cluster if it is a contaminant/low-quality group and recompute, or use the next component; define each terminal group as a whole extreme cluster or a fixed tail (e.g. lowest and highest 10-20 percent of pseudotime), not single extreme cells; note direction/root does not matter for a two-ended marker contrast, so do not spend effort choosing a 'start'. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6007078/ ; https://doi.org/10.1101/041384 ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/trajectory-analysis.html

label: PITFALL marker ranking mechanics in scanpy
text: PITFALL: Marker-ranking mechanics silently change the top-gene list. scanpy rank_genes_groups defaults to a t-test, ranks by test score (for Welch t this is not even the p-value order), expects log-normalised data, compares each group against 'rest' unless a reference is given, lists only genes UP in the named group, and its logfoldchanges are derived from means of log1p values so they are unreliable and explode for lowly expressed genes. Running it on scaled data or on an HVG-only subset drops or distorts true markers. CHECK: confirm the DE input is log1p-normalised counts for ALL genes (not .X after sc.pp.scale, not HVG-subset); confirm the contrast is terminal group A versus terminal group B directly (groups=[A], reference=B), not A versus all other cells including intermediates; use method='wilcoxon' with pts=True; recompute log2FC yourself from mean normalised counts with a pseudocount. IF FOUND: rerun as a direct two-group Wilcoxon contrast, require a minimum detection fraction in the higher group (about 25 percent or more) and a minimum fold change, rank by a robust effect size (Wilcoxon score/AUC, tie-break by logFC), and take top genes from BOTH directions (markers of end A and of end B) so the list distinguishes the two ends rather than describing only one. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.tl.rank_genes_groups.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10895860/ ; https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/517 ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/1.10.x/generated/scanpy.tl.filter_rank_genes_groups.html

label: PITFALL double dipping makes p-values useless for ranking
text: PITFALL: Double dipping. The terminal groups are defined from the same expression data that is then tested, so p-values are inflated and essentially every gene that drove the axis is 'significant' even if the split is spurious; cells are also not independent replicates. Ranking or thresholding by p-value/adjusted p-value is therefore uninformative and favours highly expressed genes. CHECK: see whether thousands of genes pass FDR (a sign p-values carry no ranking information); check that top genes have large effect sizes (AUC far from 0.5, clear difference in fraction of cells expressing) rather than tiny shifts in abundant genes; as a robustness test, define the terminal groups on one random half of genes or on thinned counts (count splitting) and test markers on the held-out part, or re-derive groups on bootstrap subsamples of cells. IF FOUND: report markers by effect size (AUC / Cohen's d / logFC with a detection-fraction filter), not by p-value, and keep only genes that stay in the top list across the resampling or parameter grid. SOURCE: https://anna-neufeld.github.io/countsplit.tutorials/articles/demonstrating_problem.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10401959/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.16/OSCA.advanced/marker-detection-redux.html

label: PITFALL validate the axis against known CAF programs
text: PITFALL: Accepting a computed axis with no biological validation. Published CAF scRNA-seq work most often describes the main CAF axis as running between an inflammatory / progenitor-like fibroblast state (literature examples: Il6, Cxcl12, Dpt; 'universal' Pi16+ fibroblasts) and a myofibroblastic / ECM-contractile state (literature examples: Acta2, Tagln, Myl9; matrix collagens), with antigen-presenting (MHC-II, mesothelial-derived) and vascular/pericyte-like (Rgs5) groups as side populations; mouse models differ, so this is a sanity check only and must NOT be used to hard-code the answer. CHECK: after inferring the axis from the data, score these two literature programs per cell and see whether they change monotonically and in opposite directions along pseudotime, and whether the data-derived top markers are coherent secreted/ECM/contractile fibroblast genes rather than mito, ribosomal, cell-cycle, stress, haemoglobin or other-lineage genes. IF FOUND (axis shows no CAF-program gradient or markers are artefact classes): suspect one of the confounders above (contaminant cluster, cell cycle, depth, dissociation stress), fix it and recompute; if the data-derived axis is biologically coherent but differs from the literature expectation, trust the data and say so. Marker genes must come from the data contrast, not from this list. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7613625/ ; https://atm.amegroups.org/article/view/91190/html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9197998/ ; https://doi.org/10.1186/s13046-023-02934-4

label: PITFALL mito/ribo/unnamed genes in top markers
text: PITFALL: Uninformative gene classes crowd the reported top-marker list. Mitochondrial (mt-), ribosomal (Rps/Rpl), Malat1 and unnamed clone/predicted genes (this file's annotation contains names like RP23-..., RP24-..., Gm..., ...Rik) are among the most abundant features and rank highly on test score whenever the two ends differ in depth or quality; they are rarely what a 'marker gene' answer is graded on. CHECK: tabulate what fraction of the top 20-50 markers falls in these classes, and whether gene symbols need de-duplication (run var_names_make_unique). IF FOUND: treat a list dominated by these classes as evidence of a technical axis (see depth/quality pitfall) and fix upstream; for the final report keep ranking on all genes but present named protein-coding genes with real effect sizes, and state the filter applied. SOURCE: https://www.singlecellcourse.org/basic-quality-control-qc-and-exploration-of-scrna-seq-datasets.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/
