The 48 antibodies are 45 CD/HLA markers plus 3 isotype controls IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b. 'AOC' = antibody-oligo conjugate. The three methods named in the task (CLR, NSP, asinh) are exactly the options of Mosaic's Protein.normalize_reads, but neither the missionbio.mosaic package nor a diptest package is installed and pip has no network, so NSP and the dip test must be implemented by hand. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.normalize_reads.html

label: PITFALL 1: NSP must be re-implemented; ranking may hinge on it
text: PITFALL: NSP (Noise corrected and Scaled Protein) is a proprietary Mission Bio Mosaic algorithm whose source is not public and whose package is not installed, so a home-made 'NSP' can differ enough from the real one to decide the A/B/C ranking. What the docs do specify: Gaussian jitter (sd 0.5, mean 0) is added to the raw read counts, an arcsinh is applied, per-cell background and signal are each assumed to depend linearly on the cell's total protein reads, a linear model is fitted to background and to signal and that depth dependence is removed; optionally reads are first divided by a scale factor for over-sequenced runs (reset to 1 if it would leave >5% of cells with 0 reads); normalization is run per sample; a correct run shows signal and background as distinct and both flat versus read depth. CHECK: confirm 'import missionbio.mosaic' fails; after your NSP, plot/regress per-cell background level and signal level against log total reads (slope should be ~0 after correction, clearly non-zero before) and rerun with 3+ jitter seeds and at least one alternative reasonable background definition (e.g. isotype controls vs lowest-expressed antibodies per cell). IF FOUND (i.e. the NSP bimodal-marker count moves across seeds/variants by as much as the gap between methods): say the ranking is implementation-sensitive, report the range, and base the answer on the variant that follows the documented steps most literally rather than on whichever variant wins. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/missionbio.demultiplex.protein.nsp.NSP.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.demultiplex.protein.nsp.NSP.plot.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.demultiplex.protein.nsp.NSP.scaling_factor.html

label: PITFALL 2: dip test must be hand-implemented and validated; Monte Carlo p-values at matching n
text: PITFALL: No dip-test package is available (python diptest/unidip missing, no R, no pip network), and hand-written dip code is error-prone (the original published Fortran had a bug giving asymmetric, near-1 results), while p-values depend strongly on n and are not a closed form: the reference implementation interpolates a table in sqrt(n)*D, or simulates P = mean(D_obs <= dip(runif(n))) with B=2000 uniform samples of the SAME n. CHECK: validate your dip function before using it: (a) dip is unchanged by x -> a*x+b and by x -> -x; (b) uniform samples give p roughly uniform (about 5% below 0.05); (c) N(0,1) samples of n~5000 give p near 1; (d) a 50/50 mixture of N(0,1) and N(4,1) gives p near 0; (e) minimum possible dip is 1/(2n). Build the null by simulating dip of uniform samples at each sample's actual n (B>=2000; sqrt(n)*D is nearly n-free at large n so one null per n can be reused for all markers and methods). IF FOUND (any validation fails, or p-values were taken from a table for the wrong n): fix the implementation first; use one identical null, seed, cell set and marker set for all three normalizations so differences come only from the normalization. SOURCE: https://github.com/cran/diptest/blob/master/R/dipTest.R ; https://www.stat.math.ethz.ch/CRAN/web/packages/diptest/refman/diptest.html

label: PITFALL 3: discrete counts/ties make the dip test falsely significant; jitter handling differs by method
text: PITFALL: Hartigan's dip test assumes continuous data ('a unimodal F may have an atom only at a unique mode'); integer AOC counts create several atoms (0,1,2,3...) that any per-marker monotone transform (asinh, or CLR computed per marker) preserves, so low-count antibodies get spuriously significant dips; even 11 tied values at 3 levels give p=0.044. Mosaic handles this by adding N(0, sd=0.5) jitter to the counts for asinh and NSP only (not CLR), and its docs note that small jitter leaves peaks at 0,1,2,3. A per-cell CLR breaks ties implicitly through each cell's own geometric mean, so the three methods are not compared like-for-like unless ties are handled deliberately. CHECK: per antibody, the fraction of cells with raw count <= 3 and the number of distinct normalized values; run the dip test with and without the sd-0.5 jitter on the counts; look at whether the isotype controls (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b) become 'bimodal'. IF FOUND (markers significant only without jitter, or low-count/isotype markers significant): treat those as discreteness artefacts, use jittered counts for asinh and NSP as the tool specifies, state what was done for CLR, and report how the per-method counts change with/without jitter. SOURCE: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/203556/hartigans-dip-test-significant-for-bimodality-with-clearly-unimodal-data ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.demultiplex.protein.nsp.NSP.scaling_factor.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.normalize_reads.html

label: PITFALL 4: large-n oversensitivity of dip test, saturation/ties, multiple testing
text: PITFALL: The dip test's critical value shrinks with n, so with thousands of cells per sample (2.5k-6.9k, ~24k pooled) it rejects unimodality for nearly-unimodal distributions (small shoulders); p<0.05 can then be met by most of the 48 antibodies under every normalization, making the 'number of bimodal markers' saturate or tie, and raw dip values are not comparable across different n. Also 48 markers x 3 methods (x 5 samples) at alpha 0.05 is uncorrected multiple testing. CHECK: count significant markers per method; if counts are close to 48 or within 1-3 of each other, also compare the dip statistic itself, repeat on equal-size random subsamples (e.g. 1000-2000 cells, several seeds) and with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, and see whether the method ranking is stable. IF FOUND (ranking changes with n, seed or BH): keep the task's stated criterion (dip p<0.05) as the primary count but report that the margin is fragile and which method wins under each variant; do not quietly switch criteria to break a tie. SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2511.01705v1

label: PITFALL 5: pooled vs per-sample normalization and testing
text: PITFALL: The file holds 5 separate patient samples. Pooling cells from all samples into one distribution per antibody manufactures multimodality from between-sample shifts in staining, sequencing depth and cell composition, which is not a positive/negative population split, and it inflates n. Mosaic normalizes protein reads per sample (for sample in group: sample.protein.normalize_reads(...)) and NSP's linear fit and scale factor are sample-specific; a published Tapestri analysis states NSP was run on a per-sample basis. CHECK: after each normalization compare per-sample medians/quantiles of every antibody; run the dip test both per sample and pooled. IF FOUND (pooled is significant where individual samples are not, or sample medians differ): normalize and test per sample, and fix in advance one rule for turning 5 per-sample results into a single marker count per method (e.g. total significant marker-sample pairs, or markers significant in a majority of samples); report whether the winning method is the same per sample, under that rule, and pooled. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/curated_notebooks/dna-protein-multisample.html ; https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11529336/v1

label: PITFALL 6: use called cells (assays/), not all_barcodes
text: PITFALL: Each sample has two protein matrices: all_barcodes/protein_read_counts (425k-1.28M barcodes, overwhelmingly empty/non-cell barcodes) and assays/protein_read_counts (2.5k-6.9k called cells). Running normalization or the dip test on all_barcodes makes every antibody look bimodal (empty barcodes vs cells) or zero-dominated, and makes CLR/NSP parameters describe background rather than cells; Mosaic loads only cell-associated barcodes (raw=False) and its notebook subsets protein to the DNA assay's barcodes before normalizing. CHECK: matrix shape before normalizing (thousands of rows, not hundreds of thousands); that protein barcodes equal the barcodes of the same sample's assays/dna_read_counts; distribution of total protein reads per cell for a low-count clump. IF FOUND: use assays/protein_read_counts restricted to DNA-called barcodes for all three methods; all_barcodes may be used only as an optional background reference, never as the tested population; apply any cell filter identically before all three normalizations. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/curated_notebooks/dna-protein-multisample.html

label: PITFALL 7: CLR axis and formula ambiguity
text: PITFALL: 'CLR' names several different transforms that give different marker distributions: (i) per cell across antibodies (original CITE-seq; compositional; what a Tapestri/Mosaic-style CLR does, log counts centred on the cell's own mean log count), (ii) per antibody across cells (Seurat default margin; just log1p(x/constant) per marker, i.e. no cell-depth correction at all), and formula variants log((x+1)/mean-or-geomean(x+1)) versus Seurat's log1p(x / exp(sum(log1p(x[x>0]))/length(x))), which floors negatives at 0 and is non-linear near zero. Seurat's margin help text is also widely misread (margin=1 is per feature, margin=2 is within a cell). The dip test is invariant only to affine maps, so these variants can yield different bimodal-marker counts. CHECK: compute the CLR count under per-cell and per-antibody versions and both formula variants, with all 48 antibodies (isotypes included) in the per-cell geometric mean. IF FOUND (count differs across variants): use the per-cell, across-antibody log-ratio with a +1 pseudocount as the primary definition (the standard meaning and the one consistent with the tool the task's method list comes from), state it explicitly, and report the alternative counts as sensitivity. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29356-8 ; https://divingintogeneticsandgenomics.com/post/details-in-centered-log-ratio-clr-normalization-for-cite-seq-protein-count-data/ ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/3605

label: PITFALL 8: CLR compositional artefacts; isotype controls as negative controls
text: PITFALL: Per-cell CLR is compositional: every antibody's value is divided by the cell's geometric mean over the whole panel, so a few abundant, strongly bimodal lineage antibodies shift the denominator in one cell type and imprint a mirror-image split on unrelated or non-expressed antibodies, including the isotype controls; ADT counts also carry large protein-specific background that CLR does not remove and the negative population is not centred at zero. This can inflate CLR's count of 'bimodal' markers with artefacts rather than true positive/negative populations. CHECK: use the 3 isotype controls (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b) as negative controls: they should be unimodal under every method; for each CLR-significant marker, test whether the two modes simply track the cell's geometric mean (correlation with the per-cell mean log count) or another marker's positive/negative status; compare with the same marker under asinh/NSP. IF FOUND (isotypes or clearly non-expressed markers bimodal under a method): report the count both with and without isotype controls, flag those calls as normalization artefacts, and say whether excluding them changes which method has the most bimodal markers. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29356-8 ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/surface-protein/normalization/

label: PITFALL 9: asinh cofactor/jitter choice and uncorrected sequencing depth
text: PITFALL: asinh has a hidden parameter and no depth correction. asinh(x/c) is linear below ~c and logarithmic above; c=1 on raw integer counts leaves separate spikes at 0,1,2 (false modes), a large c (5 for CyTOF, ~150+ for flow) compresses or linearizes the negative population and can merge or split peaks; the Mosaic asinh option exposes only a jitter (sd 0.5), i.e. plain arcsinh of jittered counts. Unlike CLR (per-cell geometric mean) and NSP (regression on total reads), asinh does not remove per-cell total-read differences (cell size, capture, sequencing depth), so any structure in total reads per cell (low-quality cells, doublets, cell-size classes) is copied into every antibody. CHECK: dip test and histogram of log total protein reads per cell per sample; correlation of each asinh-normalized antibody with log total reads; rerun asinh with cofactor 1 and 5, with and without jitter. IF FOUND (asinh count changes with cofactor, or markers are bimodal only because total reads are): use plain arcsinh of sd-0.5-jittered counts as the primary asinh definition, report the cofactor sensitivity, and note which asinh calls are depth-driven rather than marker-specific. SOURCE: https://immunedynamics.io/Spectre/articles/data_transformation.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.normalize_reads.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29356-8

label: PITFALL 10: dip significance is not the same as clear positive/negative bimodality
text: PITFALL: A significant dip test means 'not unimodal' (at least bimodal), not 'two clean positive/negative populations': tri-modal markers, a small outlier clump or a shoulder also reject, while a rare positive population (a few % of cells) or overlapping modes look like a skewed tail and are missed because the test is conservative (uniform null) and needs well-separated subpopulations. So the dip count can both over- and under-state 'clear bimodal separation', and differently per normalization. CHECK: for every marker called significant, inspect the density/ridge plot and fit a 2-component Gaussian mixture: record minor-component fraction and separation (e.g. Ashman's D > 2); list markers that are significant but have >2 KDE peaks or a minor fraction <~2%, and markers with an obvious rare positive tail that are not significant. IF FOUND: keep dip p<0.05 as the task's stated counting rule, but report the stricter count (dip significant AND 2-component separation) alongside it and whether the winning method is the same under both; if they disagree, say so explicitly instead of picking silently. SOURCE: https://www.stat.math.ethz.ch/CRAN/web/packages/diptest/refman/diptest.html ; https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-9868.00141

label: Tapestri: germline SNPs mistaken for somatic drivers
text: PITFALL: The 181-variant panel has no matched normal and mixes germline SNPs with somatic mutations; a germline variant in a driver gene (for example the common TP53 P72R polymorphism, hg19 chr17:7579472 G>C, or intronic/synonymous SNPs in DNMT3A/TET2/ASXL1) can falsely satisfy 'co-occurring DNMT3A and TP53' and, if used as a clone feature, puts nearly every cell into one giant 'mutant' clone. CHECK: Within each sample separately, compute for every variant the percentage of genotyped cells (NGT 0/1/2, excluding 3) that are mutated (NGT 1 or 2) and the split between het and hom. A germline het shows as mutated in roughly 80-95% of cells with the remainder split between NGT=0 and NGT=2 at about half the allele-dropout rate each (ADO metadata here is 14-19%); a germline hom shows ~100% NGT=2. Also check whether the same variant is near-clonal in several of the five unrelated patients (SNP) and whether it is coding/nonsynonymous at all. IF FOUND: Exclude such variants from the driver set and from the DNMT3A+TP53 sample screen; keep only variants that are clearly subclonal in the sample (a distinct WT population well above what ADO explains) and that are nonsynonymous/truncating changes in a myeloid driver gene. Only keep a near-clonal variant if it is a canonical hotspot and justify it explicitly. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10273159/ ; https://www.jmdjournal.org/article/S1525-1578(17)30313-6/fulltext.

label: Tapestri: het/hom zygosity split by allelic dropout fragments clones
text: PITFALL: Allelic dropout (ADO) converts a true heterozygous call into NGT=2 (ref allele dropped) or NGT=0 (mutant allele dropped); the file's own metadata reports ADO rates of 14-19% for these five samples (published Tapestri runs report ~5-12%), so defining clones on the three-state genotype 0/1/2 splits one real het clone into a main clone plus 'hom' and 'WT/single-mutant' satellites, while a binary mutated/not-mutated definition merges them; the two definitions give different sizes for the largest mutant clone. CHECK: Build the clone table both ways (three-state NGT 0/1/2 and binary NGT in {1,2} vs 0) on the same complete-genotype cells. For each driver, compare the number of NGT=2 cells with the number of NGT=1 cells: a hom share of roughly ADO/2 (about 5-10% of mutated cells) with similar AF/DP/GQ profile is the dropout signature; a large, discrete NGT=2 population (AF ~100, good depth) is real LOH or hemizygosity (X-linked genes such as BCOR/STAG2/ZRSR2/PHF6 in males are expected to be NGT=2). IF FOUND: If the hom calls look like dropout, do not count them as a separate biological clone: collapse het+hom to 'mutated' for clone assignment (or equivalently fold the satellite back into its parent). If there is a genuine large hom population, keep zygosity. In either case state which definition was used and report the largest-mutant-clone percentage under both so the director can see the sensitivity. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2020006996 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12776156/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-19119-8.

label: Tapestri: NGT=3 is missing, not WT; denominator is complete-genotype cells
text: PITFALL: In Mosaic h5 files NGT is 0=WT, 1=het, 2=hom, 3=missing; treating 3 as WT inflates the WT clone and deflates every mutant clone, and using all cells of the sample (or all 23,958 cells of the merged file) as denominator gives a different percentage than the standard 'cells with complete genotype at every driver locus'. CHECK: For the chosen sample and each selected driver variant, tabulate the counts of NGT 0/1/2/3; report how many cells remain after requiring NGT != 3 at all driver loci and how that number changes as each locus is added (GC-rich amplicons in TP53, SRSF2, GATA2, RUNX1 are known to have many no-calls). IF FOUND: Drop cells with any NGT=3 at a driver locus (the published Miles/Bowman workflow: 'remove remaining cells with any unknown genotypes'), then compute clone percentages over the remaining cells including the all-WT clone in the denominator. If one marginal variant removes a large share of cells, report the result with and without it rather than silently shrinking the denominator. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html ; https://bowmanr.github.io/scDNA_myeloid/post-processing.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-19119-8.

label: Tapestri: merged multi-sample h5 must be analysed per sample
text: PITFALL: The h5 is a merged file of five patients (row attribute sample_name; 2518/5988/6917/4826/3714 cells) whose 181 variants are the union across samples (each sample has only 75-92 pipeline-passing variants); a variant that is germline or somatic in one patient may be all-missing, all-WT or sporadic noise in another, and pooled statistics across patients are meaningless for clone calling. CHECK: Subset rows by assays/dna_variants/ra/sample_name before anything else. Per sample and per variant compute percentage missing (NGT=3) and percentage mutated. Confirm how variants absent from a sample were filled (all 3 with DP=0, or all 0). IF FOUND: Run the DNMT3A/TP53 screen, the full-panel driver scan, and the clone table strictly within one sample. Never require complete genotypes at a locus that is entirely uncalled in that sample (it would delete every cell) and never call a variant 'absent' in a sample where it is merely missing. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/manual/data_structure.html.

label: Tapestri: raw NGT vs quality-masked genotypes
text: PITFALL: The NGT layer holds raw genotype calls; standard practice (Mosaic filter_variants, Tapestri Insights) masks a cell-variant call as missing when DP<10, GQ<30, or the allele fraction is inconsistent with the genotype (het AF below 20-30%, ref AF above 5%, hom AF below 95%), producing NGT_FILTERED. Low-depth or low-AF 'het' calls otherwise inflate mutant clones and create spurious double-mutant cells. This file carries the pipeline defaults in metadata (af_cutoff 20, dp_cutoff 10, gq_cutoff 30) and a FILTER_MASK layer. CHECK: For each candidate driver in the chosen sample, look at the AF distribution of NGT=1 cells (should centre near 50, not 10-25), and at DP and GQ of mutated calls. Work out FILTER_MASK polarity empirically (compare it with DP<10 / GQ<30 / AF<20) before using it. Recompute the clone table with low-quality calls set to 3 and compare with the raw-NGT table. IF FOUND: Use the masked genotypes (failed calls become missing and leave the denominator) as the primary analysis and report the raw-NGT figure as a sensitivity check. If the two differ materially, say so in the answer notes. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/manual/data_structure.html.

label: Tapestri: noise variants and recurrent artifacts fragment clones
text: PITFALL: 'Scan all 181 variants for drivers' invites over-inclusion: every extra variant multiplies the number of genotype combinations and removes cells that are missing at that locus, so adding a sequencing artifact (classic example: ASXL1 G646Wfs*12 homopolymer insertion, hg19 chr20:31022441 A>AG; other homopolymer indels; variants seen at a similar low level in all samples) or a non-driver changes the largest-clone percentage. CHECK: For each candidate require, within the sample: mutated in at least ~1% of genotyped cells and at least ~10 cells (Mosaic default min_mut_prct_cells=1; published minimum clone size 10 cells), mean AF of mutated cells near 50 or 100 rather than 15-30, good GQ, not present at a similar low frequency in all five patients, and a nonsynonymous/truncating consequence in a recognised myeloid/CH driver gene (annotate from hg19 coordinates: the file has no gene or protein annotation). IF FOUND: Exclude the variant from clone definition and list it with the reason. Report the final driver list explicitly, and re-run the clone table after exclusion; published workflows drop blacklisted recurrent artifacts, synonymous/non-coding variants and variants mutated in fewer than 2 cells before clone assignment. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10273159/ ; https://bowmanr.github.io/scDNA_myeloid/post-processing.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html.

label: Tapestri: small satellite clones are ADO/doublet artifacts
text: PITFALL: With ADO near 15%, about 7% of the cells of a true double-mutant clone lose the mutant allele at each locus and appear as single-mutant clones, and droplet doublets (COMPASS assumes 8% by default) merge two cells so that two separate single-mutant clones produce an apparent double-mutant clone and WT+mutant doublets look like low-AF hets; this matters when deciding whether DNMT3A and TP53 mutations are in the same cells or in separate clones, and which clone is 'largest'. CHECK: For every non-dominant clone compare its size with (a) ADO/2 times the size of the parent clone that differs by one locus and (b) doublet rate times 2 times fA times fB for clones A and B. Inspect per-clone AF: doublet-derived mutant calls sit near 25% rather than 50%. Optionally bootstrap cells (resample with replacement) and keep clones whose lower 95% bound is at least 10 cells. IF FOUND: Do not report artifact-sized clones as distinct populations; keep them in the denominator but identify the largest mutant clone only among clones that exceed the ADO/doublet expectation. Note that this filter should not change the size of a dominant clone, only the interpretation of minor ones. SOURCE: https://bowmanr.github.io/scDNA_myeloid/assessing-clonal-abundance.html ; https://github.com/missionbio/compass ; https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2020006996.

label: Tapestri: 'mutant fraction' is cell fraction, not bulk VAF
text: PITFALL: In single-cell data a het somatic clone present in 10% of cells has a pseudo-bulk VAF of about 5%; bulk CHIP/CCUS criteria are stated in VAF (>=2%), whereas single-cell tools report percentage of mutated cells, so the sample that passes 'DNMT3A somatic clone exceeds 10%' can depend on which quantity is used and on whether missing cells are in the denominator. CHECK: For each DNMT3A and TP53 candidate in each of the five samples compute both (i) mutated cells / genotyped cells and (ii) mean AF over genotyped cells; list which samples pass the DNMT3A >10% and TP53-present criteria under each definition. IF FOUND: If exactly one sample qualifies under both definitions, proceed. If the definitions disagree, prefer percentage of mutated cells among genotyped cells (the natural single-cell meaning of mutant fraction) and flag the ambiguity and the alternative sample to the director. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4624443/ ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html.

label: Tapestri: clone = full multi-variant genotype; WT excluded only from the ranking
text: PITFALL: Clonal haematopoiesis samples often carry several independent mutations (including more than one DNMT3A variant in different clones); defining clones per gene, or only on DNMT3A and TP53, merges distinct clones and overstates the largest one, while dropping WT cells from the denominator overstates every mutant clone. In CCUS the all-WT genotype is frequently the largest group, and the question asks for the largest clone carrying at least one mutation. CHECK: Assign each complete-genotype cell the concatenated genotype across all retained driver variants (one column per variant, not per gene), count each distinct pattern, and confirm the percentages sum to 100 including the all-WT pattern. Compare the result with the two-variant (DNMT3A+TP53 only) table to see how much the extra drivers change it. IF FOUND: Rank only patterns with at least one mutated locus, but divide by all complete-genotype cells (WT included). Report the genotype pattern of the winning clone, its cell count and the denominator. SOURCE: https://bowmanr.github.io/scDNA_myeloid/assessing-clonal-abundance.html ; https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.2020006996.

label: Tapestri task: file layout and encoding
text: DATA CONTEXT for the Tapestri task: /workspace/data/GSE276492_combined.h5 is a Mosaic-style merged h5 (hg19, panel CO89_Custom-Myeloid, pipeline 2.0.2, V2 chemistry) with five samples (n_cells 2518, 5988, 6917, 4826, 3714; per-sample ADO rate in metadata 0.15, 0.19, 0.14, 0.19, 0.19). Paths: assays/dna_variants/layers/{NGT,AF,DP,GQ,FILTER_MASK,AF_MISSING,RGQ} (cells x 181 variants), assays/dna_variants/ca/{id,CHROM,POS,REF,ALT,amplicon,filtered,ado_rate,ado_gt_cells}, assays/dna_variants/ra/{barcode,sample_name,filtered}, assays/protein_read_counts/layers/read_counts (cells x 48 antibodies, raw counts). label: CAVEAT: unverified assumptions in library pitfall notes
text: CAVEAT on the library's pitfall notes: three statements are NOT verified from a retrieved source and should be treated as assumptions. (1) The exact Mosaic CLR formula (believed to be log1p of reads minus the per-cell mean of log1p over all antibodies) could not be retrieved because Mosaic's source pages are not public; only 'CLR = Centered Log Ratio, per-sample' is documented. (2) The internal steps of NSP beyond the documented summary (jitter sd 0.5 on counts, arcsinh, linear fit of background and of signal versus total reads, optional scale-down factor, max 5% zero-read cells) are unknown, including how background versus signal antibodies are chosen per cell. (3) 'mosaic, diptest, unidip and R are not installed and pip has no network' was observed in the library agent's sandbox; an analyst should re-check with 'import diptest' / 'import missionbio.mosaic' in their own environment and prefer the real packages if they are present. label: PITFALL strict > vs scanpy inclusive >=
text: PITFALL: scanpy sc.pp.filter_cells(min_genes=N) keeps cells with n_genes >= N (source: cell_subset = number_per_cell >= min_number), but the task demands strict n_genes > 1000, so min_genes=1000 wrongly keeps nuclei with exactly 1000 genes. CHECK: count nuclei with n_genes == 1000 exactly; if that count is non-zero the two conventions give different answers. IF FOUND: use an explicit mask n_genes > 1000 (equivalently min_genes=1001), never min_genes=1000. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/1.11.1/src/scanpy/preprocessing/_simple.py

label: PITFALL explicit zeros inflate nnz-based n_genes
text: PITFALL: In a sparse matrix, X.getnnz(axis=1), X.nnz and np.diff(indptr) count STORED entries including explicitly stored zeros, so they can overcount genes detected per nucleus; only count_nonzero or (X > 0).sum(axis=1) count true non-zeros. CHECK: compare (X.data == 0).sum() to 0, and compare np.diff(X.indptr) against np.asarray((X > 0).sum(axis=1)).ravel() for equality. IF FOUND: call X.eliminate_zeros() first or compute n_genes as (X > 0).sum(axis=1) directly; do not use indptr differences. SOURCE: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.getnnz.html and https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/488

label: PITFALL non-canonical CSR duplicates
text: PITFALL: A CSR matrix read from disk may be non-canonical (duplicate column indices within a row, unsorted indices); duplicates are logically summed, so stored-entry counts and even (X > 0).sum(axis=1) on the un-deduplicated matrix can count one gene twice. CHECK: X.has_canonical_format (or after X.sum_duplicates() verify X.nnz is unchanged). IF FOUND: run X.sum_duplicates() then X.eliminate_zeros() before counting genes per nucleus. SOURCE: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.count_nonzero.html and https://github.com/scipy/scipy/issues/5807

label: PITFALL verify X is raw integer counts
text: PITFALL: A float-typed .X is not proof of raw counts; h5ad files often hold normalized/log1p or ambient-corrected values in X, and here X is float32 with no .raw and no layers. CHECK: on X.data verify all values are integer-valued (np.all(X.data == np.round(X.data))), minimum >= 0, and maximum is a plausible UMI count (not ~<15 as in log1p data); also check row sums of X equal obs total_counts. IF FOUND non-integer: X is not the raw matrix and the count cannot be computed as specified from X alone - report that rather than thresholding transformed values; if integer-valued, float32 dtype is harmless (exact up to 2^24). SOURCE: https://discourse.scverse.org/t/how-could-adata-raw-x-contain-non-integer-values/3708 and https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3224

label: PITFALL stale obs n_genes columns
text: PITFALL: Pre-existing obs columns named n_genes are often stale: scanpy writes obs n_genes only when filter_cells ran, possibly on a different matrix, gene set or processing stage; this file has both obs n_genes and obs n_genes_raw, which may disagree with each other and with X. CHECK: recompute n_genes from X as (X > 0).sum(axis=1) and compare elementwise with obs n_genes and obs n_genes_raw; report how many nuclei differ and how many pass > 1000 under each. IF FOUND mismatched: the task defines n_genes from the raw count matrix, so the recomputed value from X is authoritative; use the obs columns only as a cross-check and note the discrepancy. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/488 and https://discourse.scverse.org/t/difference-between-n-genes-and-n-genes-by-counts/632

label: PITFALL gene filtering before counting n_genes
text: PITFALL: Any step that removes or alters genes or counts before computing n_genes changes how many nuclei clear a fixed threshold: sc.pp.filter_genes(min_cells=...), HVG subsetting, dropping mitochondrial/ribosomal genes, var_names_make_unique-style merging, normalization, or ambient-RNA correction. Tutorial pipelines do several of these by reflex. CHECK: confirm adata.shape is still 966768 x 32227 at the moment n_genes is computed and that no gene filter, cell-calling, doublet or mito filter ran first. IF FOUND: recompute n_genes on the untouched matrix with all genes; apply only the single n_genes > 1000 filter the task asks for. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html and https://bioconductor.org/books/3.19/OSCA.advanced/single-nuclei-rna-seq-processing.html

label: PITFALL >0 vs !=0 definitions
text: PITFALL: 'count > 0' and 'non-zero' are different definitions if any value is negative: scanpy calculate_qc_metrics n_genes_by_counts counts stored non-zero entries after eliminate_zeros (i.e. != 0), whereas filter_cells uses X > 0. CHECK: X.data.min() >= 0. IF FOUND negatives: the matrix is not raw counts (see raw-count pitfall); if you must proceed, use strictly (X > 0).sum(axis=1) as the task states and flag it. If no negatives and no explicit zeros, the two methods agree and can be used to cross-validate each other. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/1.12.1/src/scanpy/preprocessing/_qc.py

label: PITFALL categorical group counts dropping cells
text: PITFALL: Per-group counts from a pandas categorical can silently lose cells: value_counts drops NaN by default, groupby drops NaN keys and (observed=False) lists unused categories, and labels may vary in case/whitespace, so Adult + Aged may not equal total. CHECK: adata.obs['age_group'].isna().sum() == 0, the categories are exactly 'Adult' and 'Aged', and after filtering assert Adult + Aged == total; use value_counts(dropna=False). Also cross-tab sample x age_group (3 samples) to confirm each sample maps to one age group. IF FOUND: report total as all nuclei passing the filter and state how unlabelled nuclei were handled rather than letting them vanish. SOURCE: https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/whatsnew/v1.5.1.html and https://github.com/pydata/pandas/issues/9443

label: PITFALL densifying a 967k-nucleus matrix
text: PITFALL: With ~967k barcodes x 32k genes, any densifying operation (X.toarray(), np.asarray(X), X.A, pandas conversion) needs ~125 GB and will crash or tempt subsampling, which makes the count non-deterministic or wrong; anndata backed='r' row-by-row iteration is also reported to leak memory. CHECK: the sparse matrix has ~172M stored entries (~2 GB in memory), so load it sparse and keep every operation sparse. IF FOUND memory pressure: read X/data, X/indices, X/indptr with h5py in row chunks and count data > 0 per row via indptr, over ALL rows - never subsample. The ~967k barcode count means the object is largely unfiltered droplets, so expect only a small fraction to pass; that is not an error. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/anndata/issues/1597 and https://github.com/chanzuckerberg/single-cell-curation/issues/399

label: sc20 data layout
text: DATA FACT (headers only, no analysis): 156291668.node is an AnnData .h5ad file with 11693 cells x 22790 genes. obs has only two columns: popv_prediction (categorical, 18 cell types, the only cell-type label) and sample (4 samples). obsm has X_pca (50d), X_scvi_popv (20d), X_scanvi_popv (20d), X_umap_scvi_popv, X_umap_scanvi_popv. uns and obsp are empty, so there is NO precomputed neighbour graph and NO existing cluster column: the analyst must build the kNN graph and cluster themselves.

label: pitfall: wrong use_rep
text: PITFALL: The kNN graph gets built on the wrong representation. scanpy sc.pp.neighbors with use_rep=None silently uses X_pca when it exists (it does in this file), and X_scanvi_popv / the UMAP coordinates are different embeddings (scANVI is label-supervised, so clusters on it look purer). CHECK: after neighbors, assert adata.uns['neighbors']['params']['use_rep'] == 'X_scvi_popv' and that the embedding used has shape (11693, 20). IF FOUND: rerun sc.pp.neighbors(adata, use_rep='X_scvi_popv') and recluster; do not pass n_pcs (it is ignored for non-PCA reps) and do not cluster on the 2-D UMAP. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pp.neighbors.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1281 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/clustering-with-scvi-latent-space/1467

label: pitfall: purity depends on resolution
text: PITFALL: Purity rises mechanically with the number of clusters (it reaches 100% when every cell is its own cluster), so the answer depends on the unstated clustering resolution, and tuning resolution to raise purity is invalid. CHECK: compute the purity at Leiden resolutions e.g. 0.25, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 and record n_clusters and purity for each; see how much the value moves. IF FOUND (value moves by more than about 1-2 points): do not pick the best-looking one; report the value at the tool defaults that the standard scvi-tools/scanpy workflow uses when nothing is specified (sc.pp.neighbors n_neighbors=15, sc.tl.leiden resolution=1.0) as the primary answer and state the sensitivity range next to it. SOURCE: https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/evaluation-of-clustering-1.html ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.tl.leiden.html ; https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/1.2.2/tutorials/notebooks/quick_start/api_overview.html

label: pitfall: macro vs weighted purity
text: PITFALL: Two different aggregates are both called purity. The textbook overall purity is cell-weighted (sum over clusters of the majority-type count, divided by total cells); the task instead asks for the AVERAGE of per-cluster purities, i.e. an unweighted mean over clusters where each cluster counts once regardless of size. They give different numbers whenever cluster sizes are unequal. CHECK: compute both, macro = mean over clusters of (max type count / cluster size) and micro = sum of max type counts / n_cells, and compare. IF FOUND (they differ): answer with the unweighted per-cluster mean as the task defines it, and mention the weighted value only as a side note. SOURCE: https://www.cs.rpi.edu/~zaki/DMML/slides/pdf/ychap17.pdf ; https://inferensys.com/glossary/enterprise-knowledge-graphs/knowledge-graph-quality-assessment/cluster-purity

label: pitfall: leiden backend and seed
text: PITFALL: Leiden output is not stable across backend, version and seed. scanpy's legacy default is flavor='leidenalg', n_iterations=-1, directed graph, random_state=0; newer scanpy warns that the default moves to flavor='igraph' (n_iterations=2, undirected) and to an unseeded rng in 2.0, and results differ between scanpy 1.9 and 1.10 even with the same call. Cluster count and therefore average purity can shift. CHECK: print scanpy/leidenalg/igraph versions; run Leiden with both flavors and with several seeds (e.g. 0, 1, 42) at the same resolution and tabulate n_clusters and purity. IF FOUND (purity varies across runs): fix random_state=0 explicitly, use the plain default call sc.tl.leiden(adata) settings as the primary result, and report the spread across flavors/seeds as the uncertainty rather than a single unexplained number. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3422 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2865 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.tl.leiden.html

label: pitfall: tiny clusters inflate macro purity
text: PITFALL: Tiny or singleton clusters distort an unweighted average of per-cluster purity: a cluster of 1-20 cells is almost always near 100% pure and counts as much as a cluster of 2000 cells, so a few fragments (from high resolution, a disconnected kNN graph, or outlier cells) push the average up. CHECK: print the cluster size table with per-cluster purity; flag clusters with fewer than about 20 cells and recompute the mean with and without them. IF FOUND: keep all clusters in the reported number (the task definition has no size filter) but do not raise resolution or shrink n_neighbors in ways that create fragments, and note how much the tiny clusters contribute. SOURCE: https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/evaluation-of-clustering-1.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7852188/

label: pitfall: wrong purity definition
text: PITFALL: 'Cluster purity' means something else in several single-cell tools: bluster neighborPurity (fraction of a cell's neighbours in the same cluster), ROGUE (entropy-based), or silhouette-like scores. None of these use cell-type labels and they are not what is asked. CHECK: confirm the code is a cluster-by-cell-type contingency table (pd.crosstab(clusters, adata.obs['popv_prediction'])) with row max divided by row sum. IF FOUND (another purity function was used): replace it with the label-majority fraction per cluster, then average over clusters and multiply by 100. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/3.14/OSCA.advanced/clustering-redux.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-16904-3

label: pitfall: percent scale and denominators
text: PITFALL: The answer is returned on the wrong scale or from a bad denominator. The task wants a percentage (0-100); value_counts(normalize=True) and crosstab(normalize='index') return proportions (0-1). Also, popv_prediction is a pandas categorical: missing labels (NaN) are dropped by crosstab/value_counts, which changes the per-cluster denominator, and groupby on categoricals with observed=False can add empty rows. CHECK: assert adata.obs['popv_prediction'].isna().sum() == 0, that the contingency table sums to 11693, that every cluster row sum equals its cluster size, and that the final value lies between 100/18 and 100 and is not below 1. IF FOUND: multiply by 100 once (not twice), and divide the majority count by the full cluster size including any unlabeled cells, stating that choice. SOURCE: https://permetrics.readthedocs.io/latest/pages/clustering/PuS.html

label: pitfall: do not preprocess the embedding
text: PITFALL: The embedding or the cell set is altered before clustering. X_scvi_popv is a finished 20-d scVI latent space; scaling it, running PCA on it, retraining scVI, re-normalising X, filtering cells/genes, or clustering each of the 4 samples separately all change the kNN graph and the cell denominator. The 'sample' column is a batch variable that scVI has already corrected, not a grouping for the purity. CHECK: confirm the clustering uses all 11693 cells, the stored obsm['X_scvi_popv'] unchanged, euclidean kNN (scanpy default), and one clustering for the whole dataset. IF FOUND: remove the extra preprocessing/QC filtering and cluster the stored embedding directly with sc.pp.neighbors(use_rep='X_scvi_popv') then Leiden. SOURCE: https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/1.2.2/tutorials/notebooks/quick_start/api_overview.html ; https://scib.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide.html

label: pitfall: clustering algorithm choice
text: PITFALL: The clustering algorithm itself is unspecified, and k-means, Louvain and Leiden on the same embedding give different cluster counts and purities; k-means also needs a hand-picked k, which directly sets the purity. For single-cell embeddings the standard is graph-based Leiden on a kNN graph of the embedding (scanpy/scvi-tools tutorials, sc-best-practices). CHECK: confirm the primary result is Leiden on the X_scvi_popv kNN graph; if another algorithm was used, rerun with Leiden defaults and compare. IF FOUND (a different algorithm or a hand-chosen k such as k=18 to match the number of cell types was used): switch the primary answer to default Leiden and report the other only as a sensitivity check. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/clustering.html ; https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/1.2.2/tutorials/notebooks/quick_start/api_overview.html

label: caveat: popV label circularity and granularity
text: CAVEAT for interpretation (does not change the computation): popv_prediction is a PopV consensus label, and one of PopV's voting methods is a kNN classifier on the same X_scvi_popv embedding, so purity of scVI-embedding clusters against these labels is somewhat circular and optimistic. Labels are also fine-grained (several CD4/CD8 naive/memory T subtypes), so default-resolution clusters that merge adjacent T subtypes will have purity well below 100% for a legitimate reason; do not treat low purity in T-cell clusters as a bug or raise resolution to fix it. SOURCE: https://github.com/YosefLab/popV/blob/main/popv/algorithms/_scvi.py ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-024-01993-3

label: Data state: X already scaled, counts in layers
text: PITFALL: The .X of the provided h5ad (6420 cells x 19918 genes, one sample) is ALREADY processed: it is dense float32 with ~90% negative values and a max of exactly 10 (i.e. log-normalised, z-scored, clipped at 10), var has mean/std/highly_variable (2000 HVGs, seurat_v3-style columns) and varm['PCs'], but obsm is empty (no X_pca) and integer counts sit in layers['raw_counts']. Running normalize_total/log1p on .X would double-transform (log of negatives gives NaN) and silently wreck the PCA. CHECK: print adata.X.min()/max(), fraction of integers, and confirm layers['raw_counts'] is non-negative integer with max >> 50; never trust the uns['log1p'] flag alone. IF FOUND: either (a) restart from layers['raw_counts'] -> normalize_total(1e4) -> log1p -> HVG -> scale(max_value=10) -> PCA, or (b) treat .X as the finished scaled matrix and go straight to PCA on the HVGs; do not mix the two, and say which was used. Ideally run both and confirm the final ratio agrees. SOURCE: https://discourse.scverse.org/t/how-could-adata-raw-x-contain-non-integer-values/3708 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

label: PCA gene mask and HVG flavor are implicit and version-dependent
text: PITFALL: Which genes enter the PCA is version-dependent in scanpy. Up to ~1.11, sc.pp.pca silently restricts to var['highly_variable'] when that column exists; newer releases removed use_highly_variable and renamed mask_var to mask, so the same call may use all 19918 genes instead of the 2000 HVGs and give a different kNN graph. Also HVG flavor matters: flavor='seurat_v3' expects raw counts (pass layer='raw_counts'), flavor='seurat' expects log-normalised data; HVG selection cannot be run on z-scored data. CHECK: after PCA, verify how many genes have non-zero loadings in varm['PCs'] (should equal the HVG count you intended), and print scanpy.__version__. IF FOUND: pass the gene mask explicitly (mask_var='highly_variable' or subset adata[:, hvg]) and state n_top_genes=2000, n_comps=50 as the standard defaults; do not rely on implicit behaviour. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.pca.html ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/release-notes/index.html

label: connectivities is not the kNN graph; edge direction matters
text: PITFALL: scanpy's obsp['connectivities'] is NOT the kNN graph: it is the UMAP fuzzy-union, symmetrised and weighted, with far more than k neighbours per cell (one report: up to 91 neighbours at k=10). Counting its non-zeros or summing its weights as 'kNN edges' gives different cell-type fractions than the true directed kNN stored in obsp['distances'] (exactly k-1 non-zeros per row). Direction matters too: edges going OUT of pericytes (their own k nearest neighbours) differ from edges coming IN from other cells, because abundant types/hubs pull in many incoming edges. CHECK: for the pericyte rows compare (a) binary neighbours from obsp['distances'] (or sklearn NearestNeighbors indices) against (b) connectivities>0 and (c) connectivities weights; check row nnz equals k-1 in (a). IF FOUND: use the directed, unweighted kNN neighbour lists of pericyte cells as the primary definition ('fraction of kNN edges from pericyte cells'); report the symmetrised/weighted variant only as a sensitivity check and flag if the ratio changes materially. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1984 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3014

label: Self-neighbour off-by-one in k
text: PITFALL: Off-by-one in k from self-neighbours. scanpy's n_neighbors=15 counts the cell itself, so each cell gets 14 real neighbours; sklearn NearestNeighbors.kneighbors(X) with the training data passed as X returns each cell as its own first neighbour, whereas kneighbors() with no argument excludes self. A self-edge counted as a pericyte-pericyte edge inflates the pericyte share of the denominator, and k vs k-1 real neighbours shifts the cross-type counts. CHECK: assert no neighbour index equals the query index, and print the number of real neighbours per pericyte cell. IF FOUND: drop self, state the k actually used (default 15 in scanpy = 14 others), and note that the requested ratio CAF_fraction / max(other_fraction) is unchanged by whether pericyte-pericyte or self edges stay in the denominator (both fractions share the same denominator) - so the ratio depends only on the cross-type edge COUNTS, which do change with k. SOURCE: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.neighbors.NearestNeighbors.html ; https://github.com/scverse/rapids-singlecell/issues/80

label: Ratio of small edge counts is sensitive to k and n_pcs
text: PITFALL: The ratio is a quotient of two small edge counts and can be unstable or undefined. Pericytes are usually a tight, small cluster, so most of their kNN edges stay within pericytes and only a handful go to other types; the denominator (largest non-CAF, non-pericyte type) may rest on a few edges or be zero, making the ratio swing widely or blow up with small changes in k, number of PCs or HVGs. CHECK: print the pericyte cell count, the raw edge COUNTS (not just fractions) to every one of the 10 other labels, and recompute the ratio over a small grid (k = 10,15,20,30; n_pcs = 30,50; scaled vs unscaled) to see whether the conclusion (CAF is top neighbour by a factor of X) is stable. IF FOUND: report the value from the canonical defaults (scanpy: 2000 HVGs, scale max_value=10, 50 PCs, n_neighbors=15, euclidean) as the answer, and state the range seen; if the denominator is zero say so explicitly rather than returning inf silently. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6918801/ ; https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-10587521/v1

label: Comparison set: exclude CAFs and pericytes from the max; exact labels; raw fractions
text: PITFALL: Mis-specifying the comparison set. The dataset has 11 labels: B cells, CAFs, Endothelial cells, Epithelial/Cancer cells, M2-like Macrophages, Macrophages, Monocyte-derived cells, Neutrophils, Pericytes, Proliferating myeloid cells, T/NK cells. The denominator is the max over non-pericyte types OTHER than CAFs (9 labels); including CAFs in the max caps the ratio at 1, and substring matching ('Macrophages' also matches 'M2-like Macrophages'; 'CAF' vs 'CAFs') or merging myeloid labels changes the max. Raw adjacency fractions are also not abundance-corrected: an abundant type gets more edges by chance, which is why neighbourhood-enrichment tools use permutation z-scores - but the task asks for the raw fraction ratio, so do not swap in an enrichment score. CHECK: use exact label equality on obs['cell_type'], print value_counts, and confirm the max is taken over exactly 9 labels. IF FOUND: keep the raw-fraction definition for the answer; optionally mention the abundance-normalised view (edges per target cell) as context only. SOURCE: https://squidpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/squidpy.gr.nhood_enrichment.html ; https://arxiv.org/html/2506.18692

label: Build kNN on all cells in X_pca, not a subset or UMAP
text: PITFALL: The kNN graph must be built on ALL cells in PCA space, with PCA fitted on all cells. Subsetting to pericytes (or pericytes+CAFs) before PCA/kNN, building the graph on UMAP coordinates, or building it on the 19918-gene matrix instead of the PCA embedding changes neighbours entirely. With no obsm['X_pca'] in the file, sc.pp.neighbors will silently compute its own PCA with defaults if you have not; and n_pcs=None uses all stored PCs. CHECK: assert the embedding passed to the neighbour search has shape (6420, n_pcs) and is obsm['X_pca'] that you computed; assert neighbour indices range over all 6420 cells. IF FOUND: rebuild on the full dataset with use_rep='X_pca' and state n_pcs. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pp.neighbors.html

label: PCA solver and approximate kNN non-determinism
text: PITFALL: Non-determinism in PCA and neighbour search. sklearn randomized PCA is not exactly reproducible across platforms and even arpack has reported run-to-run/thread-count differences; scanpy uses exact brute-force kNN only for small data (per source: euclidean metric and n_obs < 8192, or n_obs < 4096 otherwise) and approximate PyNNDescent beyond that or for other metrics such as cosine - with 6420 cells, euclidean is exact but cosine is approximate. Small neighbour changes matter when only a few cross-type edges exist. CHECK: rerun the pipeline twice and compare the pericyte edge-count table; cross-check scanpy's neighbours against exact sklearn NearestNeighbors(algorithm='brute') on the same X_pca. IF FOUND: fix svd_solver='arpack' and random_state=0, use exact kNN (transformer='sklearn' or sklearn directly), keep euclidean metric as the default. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1187 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1749 ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/how-to/knn-transformers.html

label: Scaling, hubness and doublets can drive cross-type edges
text: PITFALL: Gene scaling and high-dimensional hubness change who is a neighbour of whom. There is no consensus on z-scoring genes before PCA (it up-weights lowly expressed noisy genes), and in many PCs a few 'hub' cells appear in very many cells' kNN lists, which can make one abundant type (e.g. cancer cells or macrophages) the apparent top neighbour of a rare type. Heterotypic doublets and ambient RNA (pericyte+endothelial doublets are a common example) also sit between clusters and create spurious cross-type edges. CHECK: compare the pericyte neighbour table with and without sc.pp.scale and at 30 vs 50 PCs; look at in-degree of the non-pericyte cells receiving pericyte edges (are a few cells receiving most of them?); check whether pericytes adjacent to endothelial cells have unusually high n_genes/total counts. IF FOUND: keep the standard pipeline (scale, 50 PCs) for the reported number since the task says 'standard preprocessing', do not delete cells on your own authority, but flag that the non-CAF maximum is driven by hubs/doublets if that is the case. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btab795 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6625319/ ; http://www.royfrancis.com/seqhub/chapters/sc/index.html

label: sc15 data structure from headers
text: DATA FACTS (from file headers only, no analysis done): 159763751.node is an AnnData h5ad with 100,000 cells x 40,352 genes; X is a CSR matrix whose first stored values are small integers, so it looks like raw counts (verify before normalising); layers and obsp are empty, so no neighbour graph is supplied. obs has cell_type (18 categories: B Intermediate/Memory, B Naive, CD4 Memory, CD4 Naive, CD8 Memory, CD8 Naive, CD14 Mono, CD16 Mono, HSPC, ILC, MAIT, NK, NK CD56bright, NKT, Plasmablast, Treg, cDC, pDC), donor (12), cytokine (91 categories), treatment (PBS vs cytokine), sample (1092 = donor x cytokine), plus split-pool barcode wells and QC columns. obsm holds X_pca (50 PCs) and X_umap; uns/pca_info says method 'sample-based PCA', variance_explained 0.346, and lists only 100 hvg_genes that appear to be in var order (the list may be truncated or the PCA may really rest on few genes), so the supplied X_pca should be tested rather than trusted.

label: PITFALL purity rises with cluster count
text: PITFALL: Purity is trivially inflated by making more clusters (every cell its own cluster gives 100%), and the task's 'average purity' is an unweighted mean over clusters, so many tiny pure clusters raise it while hiding large mixed clusters; a resolution picked only to maximise purity is over-clustered and not a meaningful result. CHECK: over a resolution sweep, tabulate n_clusters, types captured, unweighted mean purity, cell-weighted purity, minimum cluster size and the purity of the 5 largest clusters; see whether purity gains come only from cluster count. Also verify the metric code: purity on a 0-100 scale, captured = number of DISTINCT dominant types (not number of clusters), total_clusters counts exactly the clusters used for purity, no empty/unused categories or NaN labels in the crosstab. IF FOUND: report the solution with the fewest clusters that reaches >=17 captured types with stable purity, state the cluster count and weighted purity next to it, and never feed cell_type labels into the clustering itself (labels may only score or choose among unsupervised partitions, and that tuning must be disclosed). SOURCE: https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/html/htmledition/evaluation-of-clustering-1.html ; https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1606.05596

label: PITFALL resolution limit hides rare types
text: PITFALL: Modularity-based Leiden/Louvain has a resolution limit: communities smaller than a scale set by the total graph size get merged into neighbours, so in a 100,000-cell graph at default resolution (~1.0) rare PBMC types (HSPC, ILC, pDC, Plasmablast, cDC, NK CD56bright) are absorbed and never become the plurality of any cluster; raising global resolution instead shatters the big populations (multiresolution modularity merges small and splits large at once). CHECK: build an 18-row table per run: type size, the cluster holding most of that type, share of the type in it, and whether the type is dominant in any cluster; run it across resolutions (e.g. 0.5 to 5) and note which types are still uncaptured. IF FOUND: sub-cluster only the parent cluster(s) containing the missing type (scanpy sc.tl.leiden restrict_to, or re-run HVG+PCA+neighbours on that subset) instead of cranking global resolution; CPM quality function is an alternative that lacks the limit. SOURCE: https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.0605965104 ; https://journals.aps.org/pre/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevE.84.066122 ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/clustering.html

label: PITFALL supplied PCA and few HVGs
text: PITFALL: Clustering on a supplied embedding built from too few or poorly chosen genes cannot separate similar cell types. For abundant, very different types feature choice barely matters, but for subtle differences (naive vs memory T, Treg, MAIT, NKT, NK CD56bright) both the number of features and the selection method strongly change the clusters. The file's X_pca reports only 100 hvg_genes and a 'sample-based PCA' with 34.6% variance explained. CHECK: cluster once on the supplied obsm['X_pca'] and once on a recomputed pipeline from raw counts (normalize_total, log1p, 2000-4000 HVGs, PCA 50) at a matched number of clusters, and compare types captured and purity; also check whether known subset markers (e.g. FOXP3, SLC4A10, CCR7, NCAM1, KLRB1) are in the HVG set. IF FOUND: use the recomputed embedding; do not assume the precomputed PCA/UMAP is fit for fine-grained typing, and never cluster on the 2-D UMAP. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-025-06240-y ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-025-02624-3

label: PITFALL donor and cytokine effects drive clusters
text: PITFALL: In multi-donor, stimulated-vs-control PBMC data, stimulation (e.g. interferon-type cytokines change hundreds of genes in every cell, monocytes most strongly) and donor identity can drive PCs, so cells group by condition or donor rather than by type; this dataset has 12 donors x 91 cytokine conditions. Splitting one type by state only adds clusters, but a shared response programme can also pull different types together and lower purity or lose a capture. CHECK: for each cluster compute the largest donor share and largest cytokine share (and PBS vs cytokine share) and compare with the global shares; correlate top PCs with donor and treatment; flag mixed-type clusters dominated by one cytokine or donor. IF FOUND: select HVGs batch-aware (batch_key=donor or sample) and integrate the PCs with Harmony on donor (optionally also cytokine), then re-cluster and compare the 18-row capture table against the unintegrated run; keep whichever captures more types at equal cluster count. SOURCE: https://satijalab.org/seurat/archive/v3.2/immune_alignment.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6964114/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12840603/

label: PITFALL integration overcorrection erases rare types
text: PITFALL: Batch integration can over-correct: Harmony's objective is biased toward major cell types, so small populations can be blended into large neighbours, and methods such as MNN, scVI and LIGER can alter the data considerably; integrating by default may lose exactly the rare types needed to reach 17 of 18. CHECK: compare, before vs after integration and at the same number of clusters, the per-type capture table and the purity of the clusters dominated by rare types (HSPC, ILC, pDC, Plasmablast, cDC, NK CD56bright); a rare type that was dominant somewhere before and nowhere after is over-correction. IF FOUND: use the uncorrected PCA, or integrate on donor only with a weaker setting, and treat integration as an option to be justified by the capture table rather than a required step. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9982060/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12315870/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8748196/

label: PITFALL T/NK subsets not discrete in RNA
text: PITFALL: Fine T/NK subsets do not form discrete RNA clusters. T-cell states vary continuously; CD4 and CD8 are imperfectly resolved by RNA (low CD4 transcript), and in a ~500K T-cell atlas unsupervised clusters mixed CD4 and CD8 regardless of feature selection or PCA/Harmony, being driven by metabolism, TCR, immunoglobulin and HLA transcripts instead of subset markers. Labels like CD4/CD8 Naive vs Memory, Treg, MAIT, NKT, ILC were probably assigned by reference mapping or protein, so one global clustering will leave several of them never dominant and will hold most of the impure clusters. CHECK: print the type-by-cluster confusion matrix restricted to T/NK clusters; list which T/NK types lack a cluster where they are the plurality and which clusters fall below ~60% purity. IF FOUND: subset the T/NK compartment, re-select HVGs inside the subset (consider dropping TR*V/IG*/HLA/ribosomal/mitochondrial genes from the HVG list), recompute PCA and neighbours, and cluster that subset at higher resolution; expect purity in this compartment to stay well below the myeloid/B clusters and say so. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.immuno.2025.100063 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12446064/ ; https://www.cell.com/cell-reports-methods/fulltext/S2667-2375(24)00328-X

label: PITFALL kNN k too large merges rare types
text: PITFALL: The kNN graph is fixed before Leiden runs and matters as much as resolution: a larger n_neighbors gives a more global view and merges small populations into neighbours (k=15 to 50 usually changes the cluster count more than a resolution change), and graph type/quality function strongly affect results when k and resolution are not ideal. A population with fewer cells than a few multiples of k cannot hold its own neighbourhood. CHECK: note the smallest cell-type size and compare it with k; rebuild neighbours at k=10, 15, 30 (same PCs) and compare the 18-row capture table at a matched number of clusters. IF FOUND: use the smaller k (10-15) for the global graph or for the sub-clustering step that targets the rare type, and record k, number of PCs and metric alongside resolution. SOURCE: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.08.20.671270v2 ; https://casrai.org/guides/leiden-clustering-single-cell ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/clustering.html

label: PITFALL cycling cells form a mixed cluster
text: PITFALL: Proliferating cells from different lineages (activated T, NK, B) share a cell-cycle programme stronger than their type markers and form one cycling cluster; cytokine-stimulated PBMC are likely to contain such cells, and the 18 labels have no 'proliferating' class, so that cluster would be a low-purity mix. CHECK: score S and G2M phases (sc.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle) or look at MKI67/TOP2A per cluster, and inspect the label composition of any cluster with high cycling scores. IF FOUND: sub-cluster that cluster on an HVG set with cell-cycle genes removed (or regress S/G2M scores before PCA) so it splits by lineage, and compare the result; do not regress cell cycle blindly, since regression can remove other biology. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12446064/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.20/OSCA.advanced/cell-cycle-assignment.html ; https://github.com/serjisa/cycling_T

label: PITFALL normalisation and PC count drop rare signal
text: PITFALL: Preprocessing choices silently drop rare-type signal: clustering raw or doubly log-transformed counts, or keeping too few PCs, removes it, because PCs that separate rare populations explain little total variance and fall below an elbow-plot cut-off. Log-normalisation and Pearson residuals perform similarly overall, but Pearson residuals give marker genes of small populations high variance (residual clipping matters when very few cells carry a strong marker). CHECK: confirm X is integer counts (X.data equals its rounded self, max value) before normalising and that it is not already logged; compare 30 vs 50 PCs and log1p-CP10k vs analytic Pearson residuals (scanpy.experimental.pp) on the 18-row capture table. IF FOUND: normalise from raw counts exactly once, keep about 50 PCs instead of cutting at the elbow, and switch to Pearson-residual HVG/PCA if it captures a rare type that log-normalisation misses. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-021-02451-7 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10172138/ ; https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.11.19.390542v1.full.pdf

label: PITFALL seed instability of capture count
text: PITFALL: Leiden is stochastic and has no null model: a different random seed changes the partition, so a result of 17 or 18 captured types that rests on one small borderline cluster can flip between runs, and the reported cluster count and purity move with it. CHECK: re-run the chosen configuration with 3-5 random_state values (and, if cheap, on a 80% subsample) and record captured types, n_clusters and mean purity each time. IF FOUND: prefer a configuration whose capture count is the same across seeds, fix and report random_state, and report the range across seeds rather than the best seed. SOURCE: https://casrai.org/guides/leiden-clustering-single-cell ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7852188/

text: DATA LAYOUT (headers only, no analysis done): GSE276492_combined.h5 is a Mission Bio Tapestri multi-assay HDF5 (pipeline 2.0.2, sdk 3.1.2, panel CO89_Custom-Myeloid, hg19, 279 amplicons) holding 5 samples as separate top-level groups (GSM8499463_S7, GSM8499464_S8, GSM8499465_S10, GSM8499466_S13, GSM8499467_S15). Per-cell genotypes are at <sample>/assays/dna_variants/layers/{NGT,GQ,DP,AF,FILTER_MASK,RGQ} with shape cells x variants (2518x75267, 5988x89607, 6912x99071, 4826x78181, 3714x81592); variant annotations in ca/{id,filtered,CHROM,POS,REF,ALT,QUAL,amplicon,ado_rate}, cell annotations in ra/{barcode,filtered,sample_name}. Stored pipeline QC cutoffs in dna_variants/metadata are identical in all samples: gq_cutoff 30, dp_cutoff 10, af_cutoff 20, missing_cells_cutoff 50, missing_variants_cutoff 50, mutated_cells_cutoff 1; metadata n_passing_variants = 82, 88, 92, 75, 82 and n_passing_cells = 2518, 5983, 6898, 4826, 3714 (sample order as above).

label: PITFALL filtered flag polarity (1 = removed)
text: PITFALL: The 'filtered' flag has inverted polarity relative to intuition: in Tapestri h5 files ca/filtered == 1 means the variant was filtered OUT by the pipeline QC, so the QC-passed set is filtered == 0 (same for ra/filtered on cells). Taking filtered == 1 as 'passed' swaps a set of ~80 variants per sample for ~75,000-99,000 failing ones and changes both the median and the count completely. CHECK: for each sample count ca/filtered == 0 and ca/filtered == 1 and compare with dna_variants/metadata/n_passing_variants (82, 88, 92, 75, 82); likewise count ra/filtered == 0 against n_passing_cells. IF FOUND: use whichever polarity reproduces n_passing_variants exactly and state it; if neither reproduces it, report that rather than guessing. SOURCE: https://github.com/joeymays/karyotapR/blob/v1.0.2/R/createTapestriExperiment.R ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/manual/data_structure.html

label: PITFALL NGT missing code is 3
text: PITFALL: Missing genotypes in the Tapestri NGT layer are coded as the integer 3 (0 = wildtype/ref, 1 = heterozygous, 2 = homozygous alt, 3 = missing), not NaN, -1 or 0. Using isnan, != -1, > 0 or != 0 as 'non-missing' gives a call rate of 1.0 everywhere or silently turns it into a mutation rate. CHECK: list the unique values of NGT on the passing variants (expect exactly a subset of {0,1,2,3}); confirm that NGT == 3 cells have DP == 0 or very low DP. IF FOUND: call rate per variant = mean over cells of (NGT in {0,1,2}) = 1 - mean(NGT == 3); wildtype (0) counts as called. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html ; https://rdrr.io/github/northNomad/tapestri.tools/src/R/read.R

label: PITFALL raw NGT vs quality-masked genotype
text: PITFALL: There are two defensible definitions of 'non-missing genotype' and they give different call rates. (a) Raw: stored NGT != 3. (b) Quality-masked: genotype also has GQ >= 30, DP >= 10 and, for mutated calls only, AF >= 20 (the stored cutoffs); this is what the pipeline's FILTER_MASK layer / mosaic's NGT_FILTERED encode by setting failing genotypes to 3, and it is the definition the pipeline used when it selected the QC-passed variants (>= 50 percent of cells genotyped). Raw call rates are higher than masked ones, so the median and the count >= 0.8 both shift. CHECK: compute both on the passing variants; verify FILTER_MASK polarity by cross-tabulating FILTER_MASK against (GQ < 30 or DP < 10 or NGT == 3) rather than assuming 1 = failing; under the masked definition every passing variant should have call rate about >= 0.5, which is a sanity check that you have the right mask. IF FOUND (the two differ): do not silently pick one. The task wording 'non-missing genotype' on the stored genotypes most literally means NGT != 3 on the NGT layer as shipped; report that as primary unless your lead decides otherwise, and record the masked-definition numbers as a sensitivity result so the director can see the gap. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html ; https://rdrr.io/github/MissionBio/tapestriR/src/R/filter_variants.R ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/manual/data_structure.html

label: PITFALL multi-sample: per-sample vs union variant set
text: PITFALL: The file is five samples with five different variant lists and five different QC-passed sets, not one merged cells x variants matrix, so 'the final QC-passed variant set' and 'fraction of cells' are not defined until you choose a combination rule, and the rules give different answers: (1) per-sample: one call rate per (sample, passing variant) pair, about 419 values pooled, a variant passing in several samples counted several times; (2) union of passing variant ids, call rate over all 23,958 cells pooled, pulling each variant's column from every sample's full matrix (mosaic's multisample workflow subsets every sample to the union of per-sample passing variants); (3) intersection of passing ids only. In rule 2 a variant that is absent from a sample's variant list has no genotype there. CHECK: decode ca/id bytes and compute the overlap of passing ids across samples (size of union, intersection, and how many union ids are missing entirely from some sample's full id list); compute the answer under rules 1 and 2. IF FOUND (rules disagree): state the rule explicitly; for rule 2 treat cells of a sample lacking the variant as missing (not dropped from the denominator) and say so; never report a median of per-sample medians as if it were the pooled per-variant median. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/curated_notebooks/dna-multisample.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/functions/missionbio.mosaic.io.load.html

label: PITFALL do not re-derive the variant filter
text: PITFALL: Re-deriving the QC-passed variant set with a tool default instead of using the stored flag gives a different set. The stored ca/filtered flag comes from the pipeline cascade (mask genotypes with GQ < 30, DP < 10, mutated AF < 20; drop variants genotyped in < 50 percent of cells; drop cells with < 50 percent of kept variants genotyped; drop variants mutated in < 1 percent of remaining cells). mosaic's Dna.filter_variants() defaults differ (vaf_ref 5, vaf_het 30, vaf_hom 95, and min_prct_cells is a completeness-weighted percentage over 10 iterations, not a plain fraction), tapestriR warns its filter 'will not return identical results to Tapestri Insights', and Tapestri Insights uses a different denominator (genotyped cells) from mosaic (all cells). CHECK: if you recompute a filter, compare its variant count per sample with metadata n_passing_variants (82, 88, 92, 75, 82) and with ca/filtered == 0. IF FOUND (counts differ): use the stored ca/filtered flag as the 'final QC-passed variant set' and do not add extra variant filters (no QUAL, germline, blacklist or min-call-rate filter of your own) unless you report them as a deviation. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html ; https://rdrr.io/github/MissionBio/tapestriR/src/R/filter_variants.R ; https://bbglab.github.io/bbgwiki/Methods/Sequencing/singleCell/Mosaic/

label: PITFALL cell denominator: assay cells, not all_barcodes or metadata n_cells
text: PITFALL: Wrong cell denominator. The call-rate denominator should be the called cells, i.e. the rows of <sample>/assays/dna_variants (2518, 5988, 6912, 4826, 3714), not the <sample>/all_barcodes group (about 1.3 million raw barcodes, mostly empty droplets, and it has read counts only). Two further traps: the pipeline also flags a few cells as failing (ra/filtered; metadata n_passing_cells 5983 of 5988 in S8 and 6898 in S10), and S10's metadata n_cells says 6917 while the NGT matrix has 6912 rows, so metadata counts must not be used as the denominator. CHECK: denominator == NGT.shape[0] for the cells you kept; compute call rates with all assay cells and again with only ra/filtered-passing cells and see whether the median or the >= 0.8 count moves. IF FOUND (they differ): 'fraction of cells' most literally means all cells in the assay matrix; use that as primary, and report the passing-cells-only variant as a sensitivity result. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/functions/missionbio.mosaic.io.load.html ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/manual/data_structure.html

label: PITFALL call rate is truncated by the QC selection
text: PITFALL: The QC-passed variants were selected on their own call rate (pipeline keeps variants genotyped in >= 50 percent of cells after quality masking), so the call-rate distribution on the final set is truncated from below and is not comparable to call rates over all ~75k-99k variants; a median or >= 0.8 count computed over all variants, or over variants passing only in some other sample, will be far lower. Missingness is also amplicon-driven: variants on the same amplicon share dropout, so the passing variants are not independent draws. CHECK: confirm the number of variants entering the median equals the QC-passed count (per sample 82, 88, 92, 75, 82, or the union size if pooling) and that the minimum quality-masked call rate is about 0.5; look at ca/amplicon to see how many distinct amplicons the passing variants cover. IF FOUND (variant count is in the tens of thousands, or min masked call rate is near 0): you are summarising the unfiltered set or mixing variant sets across samples; fix the subsetting before reporting. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/manual/data_structure.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9218383/

label: PITFALL axis, units and >= 0.8 boundary
text: PITFALL: Summary arithmetic errors at the threshold. Layers are cells x variants, so per-variant call rate is a mean down axis 0 (one value per variant); averaging along axis 1 gives per-cell completeness instead, whose count is bounded by the number of cells, not variants. Call rate must stay a fraction in [0,1] (pipeline metadata cutoffs are percentages, e.g. 50, so mixing units makes '>= 0.8' meaningless), the threshold is inclusive (>=), and rounding call rates before thresholding or float error at exactly 0.8 can move variants across the cut-off. CHECK: length of the call-rate vector equals the number of passing variants; all values in [0,1]; count variants within 1e-9 of 0.8 and decide them with integer arithmetic (5 * n_called >= 4 * n_cells). IF FOUND: compute the count from integer called/total counts, report the median unrounded (numpy median of an even-length vector averages the two middle values), and return the count as an integer.
