label: Leiden backend/objective/n_iterations change cluster count
text: PITFALL: 'Leiden, resolution=0.6, seed=0' is not one algorithm; the backend, objective and iteration count change the number of clusters. In the installed scanpy 1.10.4, sc.tl.leiden defaults to flavor='leidenalg', RBConfigurationVertexPartition (modularity with resolution), n_iterations=-1 (run to convergence), directed=True, use_weights=True; flavor='igraph' with n_iterations=2 gives different labels, and calling igraph's community_leiden directly defaults to objective_function='CPM', where resolution 0.6 means something entirely different and yields a wildly different cluster count. leidenalg.find_partition itself defaults to n_iterations=2, not -1. CHECK: write down flavor, objective, n_iterations, weights and directedness explicitly; run the modularity-type objective (RBConfiguration, resolution_parameter=0.6, seed=0) and compare n_clusters between n_iterations=-1 and 2 and between leidenalg and igraph(objective_function='modularity'). IF FOUND (counts differ): never use CPM; report the result of the conventional scanpy default call (leidenalg, RBConfiguration, n_iterations=-1, random_state=0) as the primary answer and state the variants' counts as sensitivity. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.tl.leiden.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2865 ; https://leidenalg.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference.html ; https://r.igraph.org/reference/cluster_leiden.html

label: kNN is approximate above 8192 cells in scanpy
text: PITFALL: the kNN search silently becomes approximate. In scanpy 1.10.4 sc.pp.neighbors uses exact brute-force search only when n_obs < 8192 (Euclidean) and otherwise switches to PyNNDescent approximate search, whose result depends on random_state, cell order and thread count; small neighbour differences snowball into different Leiden partitions. The DRG file has 19,259 nuclei before filtering, so this is likely to apply. CHECK: count nuclei after the n_genes > 1000 filter; build the k=20 graph both with scanpy's default and with an exact search (sc.pp.neighbors(..., transformer='sklearn') or sklearn NearestNeighbors(algorithm='brute')) and compare neighbour sets and resulting n_clusters. IF FOUND (n_obs >= 8192 or the two disagree): treat the exact kNN as the deterministic reference, always pass random_state=0, and report whether n_clusters is the same under both; if it is not, say so rather than hiding it. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/1.11.x/src/scanpy/neighbors/__init__.py ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/how-to/knn-transformers.html ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/changing-the-order-of-the-anndata-objects-in-anndata-concat-changes-the-leiden-clustering/3802

label: k semantics, weighting and symmetrisation of kNN graph
text: PITFALL: 'k=20, symmetric graph' has several incompatible readings that change Leiden output. (a) scanpy's n_neighbors counts the cell itself, so n_neighbors=20 gives 19 other neighbours per row of obsp['distances'], whereas sklearn kneighbors_graph(n_neighbors=20, include_self=False) gives 20 others. (b) scanpy clusters on obsp['connectivities'], a UMAP fuzzy-union WEIGHTED graph whose rows have variable numbers of nonzeros, not a binary kNN graph; a hand-built graph may be binary union (A or A.T), mutual (A and A.T), or SNN/Jaccard. Mutual kNN drops many edges and inflates the cluster count; resolutions do not carry over between graph types. (c) scanpy's leidenalg path treats the symmetric matrix as a directed graph with both edge directions, which is equivalent in effect but differs from passing each undirected edge once with summed weights. CHECK: print per-row nonzero counts of the graph, whether it equals its transpose, and whether weights are all 1; compute n_clusters for scanpy connectivities vs binary union kNN. IF FOUND (they differ): use a union-symmetrised graph (never mutual-only), prefer the standard scanpy sc.pp.neighbors(n_neighbors=20, n_pcs=30, metric='euclidean') connectivities as primary, and report the binary-union count as sensitivity. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2587 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1984 ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pp.neighbors.html ; https://sunjh22.github.io/knowledge/bioinformatics/algorithms/k-nearest-neighbor-graphs.html

label: No clipping, explicit target_sum, strict >1000, no extra steps
text: PITFALL: tutorial habits add steps the task does not ask for. sc.pp.scale(adata, max_value=10) and Seurat ScaleData(scale.max=10) CLIP scaled values, which changes PCA (clipped genes are no longer mean 0) and can change clusters; sc.pp.normalize_total defaults to the MEDIAN total count unless target_sum=1e4 is passed; sc.pp.filter_cells(min_genes=1000) keeps nuclei with n_genes >= 1000 whereas the task says strictly > 1000; adding mito/doublet/min_cells gene filters, regress_out, or batch integration across the 3 samples (3M, 21M1, 21M2) all change the graph. pct_mito is to be computed only, not filtered on. By contrast, ddof=1 (scanpy) vs ddof=0 (sklearn StandardScaler) in scaling only rescales all genes by one constant and does not change neighbours. CHECK: confirm no clipping (max abs scaled value may exceed 10), target_sum=1e4, count nuclei with n_genes exactly 1000 and confirm they are dropped, and confirm the gene and cell sets were not otherwise reduced. IF FOUND: remove the extra step and rerun; the task's listed steps are the whole pipeline. label: PCA solver, dtype and n_pcs determinism
text: PITFALL: PCA is a hidden source of non-determinism that propagates to the cluster count. sklearn's randomized solver is not reproducible across platforms; even svd_solver='arpack' has given different coordinates across CPU counts/architectures and on float32 input, and tiny coordinate differences change approximate-kNN ties and then Leiden. Also 'PCA with 50 PCs, graph on PCs 1..30' means fit 50 components and take the first 30 columns (sc.pp.neighbors(n_pcs=30)), not all 50 and not a separately fitted 30-component randomized PCA. Component sign flips do not matter for Euclidean distances. CHECK: run PCA on the dense scaled HVG matrix in float64 with svd_solver='arpack' (random_state=0) and with a full SVD; compare the first 30 PCs up to sign and compare n_clusters; confirm the neighbour step used exactly 30 columns. IF FOUND (results differ by solver/dtype): use float64 with arpack or full SVD, fix the thread count, and report n_clusters under both solvers. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1187 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/325 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3628 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/changing-the-order-of-the-anndata-objects-in-anndata-concat-changes-the-leiden-clustering/3802

label: PITFALL wrong DE background
text: PITFALL: The 'rest' in the marker test is the wrong background. The task asks for the contractile subcluster versus all other CAF subclusters, but running rank_genes_groups on the full object (or with macrophages, epithelial cells etc. in the reference) returns generic fibroblast genes (collagens, Dcn) instead of contractile-specific ones; separately, a pooled 'rest' is dominated by the largest CAF subcluster, so a gene can rank high while not being up against every other subcluster. CHECK: confirm the DE object contains exactly the 536 CAF-labelled cells, groups=[contractile cluster], reference='rest'; then for the top 50 compute mean log-normalized expression per subcluster and confirm each gene is higher in the contractile cluster than in most or all of the other 5. IF FOUND: restrict the test to the CAF subset; keep one-vs-rest as the primary answer (it is what the task states) but flag genes that are only up against the largest subcluster. SOURCE: https://ouyanglab.com/singlecell/clust.html ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-024-03183-0 ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.22/OSCA.advanced/marker-detection-redux.html

label: PITFALL marker ranking criterion
text: PITFALL: 'Top 50 markers' depends on how genes are ranked. Scanpy ranks by the test score (z-statistic), Seurat by p-value then fold change; ranking by log fold change alone selects very lowly expressed genes with huge unstable logFC; ranking by p-value gives ties at 0; rankby_abs=True lets down-regulated genes into the list; scanpy Wilcoxon has tie_correct=False by default although sparse counts are heavily tied; and p-values are inflated anyway because the clusters were defined from the same data (and there is one sample, so no pseudobulk is possible). CHECK: with pts=True confirm all 50 genes have positive score and positive logFC, are expressed in a reasonable fraction of the contractile cluster (e.g. >=10-25%), and compare the top-50 from Wilcoxon (tie_correct=True) with the t-test top-50. IF FOUND to differ: use up-regulated genes only, ranked by Wilcoxon score on log-normalized data (the benchmark-supported default: Wilcoxon, t-test and logistic regression perform best), not by logFC or raw p-value, and report the overlap between methods rather than treating p-values as evidence. SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-024-03183-0 ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38409056/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.22/OSCA.advanced/marker-detection-redux.html

label: PITFALL gene set scoring
text: PITFALL: Gene-set scores (scanpy score_genes / Seurat AddModuleScore) can mis-rank clusters: the score subtracts randomly sampled control genes binned by mean expression, so it depends on which matrix is used (clipped z-scores vs log-normalized), on the cell population it is computed in, on the random seed, and it is noisy for short gene lists; genes missing from var_names (e.g. human upper-case symbols in a mouse dataset) are dropped, sometimes silently. IF FOUND that the methods disagree on the top cluster, trust the control-free per-gene comparison and confirm afterwards that canonical contractile genes (Acta2, Tagln, Myl9, Tpm2) appear high in that cluster's DE ranking. text: DATA STRUCTURE (headers only, no analysis done): the h5ad at /scbench-data/158542059.node has 100,000 cells x 40,352 genes (var index = gene symbols), X is a sparse matrix of raw integer counts (first values 1-80, no layers, no uns), obs columns include donor (Donor1..Donor12), cytokine (91 levels including 'IFN-beta' and 'PBS'), treatment (only 'PBS' vs 'cytokine'), cell_type (18 levels including 'CD14 Mono') and sample (1092 levels = donor_cytokine). With ~92 cells per donor x cytokine across all 18 cell types, CD14 Mono pseudobulks will be small (tens of cells or fewer) and some donor x condition groups may fall under the 10-cell threshold; nobody has counted them yet.

label: PITFALL LFC ranking favors low-count genes
text: PITFALL: Ranking significant genes by the raw (maximum-likelihood) log2FoldChange puts low-count genes at the top, because ratios are noisiest when counts are low; a gene with zeros in every PBS pseudobulk and a handful of reads in IFN-beta gets a huge LFC and can still pass FDR<0.05 across ~12 donor pairs, pushing well-expressed induced genes out of the top 20. CHECK: for the top 20, print baseMean and the raw pseudobulk counts per sample in PBS and IFN-beta; count how many have near-zero PBS counts or baseMean below ~10; re-rank with apeglm-shrunken LFC (lfcShrink / PyDESeq2 lfc_shrink) and with a pre-fit expression filter, and report the overlap of the three top-20 lists. IF FOUND: apply an explicit gene expression filter before fitting (e.g. >=10 counts in at least as many samples as the smaller group, or edgeR filterByExpr / decoupler filter_by_expr) and state whether the ranking uses MLE or shrunken LFC; shrinkage changes only the LFC, not the Wald p-values/padj, so the FDR<0.05 set is the same and only the order changes. The task wording ('log2FoldChange', FDR) follows DESeq2 column names, so keep the MLE-ranked list available as well as the shrunken one and say which one is reported. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4302049/ ; https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/102052/ ; https://doi.org/10.17615/j2ds-ak73

label: PITFALL fit two conditions not all 91
text: PITFALL: Fitting the DE model on all 91 cytokine conditions (up to 1092 pseudobulks) instead of only IFN-beta and PBS changes the answer: DESeq2 estimates one dispersion per gene across every sample in the model and size factors across every sample, so unrelated cytokines with different variability move the IFN-beta vs PBS p-values (a Bioconductor user reports only ~60% overlap of significant genes between the two approaches), and with ~1000 sparse pseudobulks almost no gene is non-zero in all samples, which breaks median-of-ratios size factors. The DESeq2 vignette FAQ recommends fitting groups together in general but splitting when within-group variability differs between groups. CHECK: state how many pseudobulks and which cytokine levels enter the model; if all conditions are fitted, compare the top 20 against a fit restricted to IFN-beta + PBS samples. IF FOUND: for this two-condition question with up to 12 donor pairs, fit only the IFN-beta and PBS CD14 Mono pseudobulks with design ~ donor + condition; do not use the obs column 'treatment' as the condition, because it lumps all 90 cytokines against PBS. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html#if-i-have-multiple-groups-should-i-run-all-together-or-split-into-pairs-of-groups ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/102149/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/p132527/

label: PITFALL unpaired donors in paired design
text: PITFALL: With design ~ donor + condition, a donor that has only one of the two conditions left after the >=10-cell filter adds nothing to the IFN-beta vs PBS estimate (negative-binomial GLMs effectively drop unpaired samples), yet it still enters size-factor estimation, dispersion estimation and the baseMean used for independent filtering; and dropping the donor term altogether throws away most of the power when donors differ. CHECK: after filtering pseudobulks to >=10 CD14 Mono cells, tabulate donor x condition (IFN-beta, PBS) with cell counts and total counts per pseudobulk; confirm how many donors have both; confirm the design matrix is full rank. IF FOUND: keep only donors that have both an IFN-beta and a PBS pseudobulk, keep donor as a fixed blocking factor (~ donor + condition), and report the number of pairs used; do not switch to an unpaired design to rescue unpaired donors. SOURCE: https://support.bioconductor.org/p/96432/ ; https://www.biostars.org/p/9592605/ ; https://pseudocount.com/posts/paired-samples-rna-seq-design/

label: PITFALL Cook's outlier filter drops induced genes
text: PITFALL: DESeq2/PyDESeq2 Cook's-distance outlier handling can remove genuinely induced genes. PyDESeq2 defaults are refit_cooks=True with min_replicates=7 and cooks_filter=True: with >=7 replicates per condition an 'outlier' count is replaced by a trimmed mean, with fewer the gene's p-value is set to NA. In small pseudobulks a strongly induced gene whose response is uneven across donors looks like an outlier, and DESeq2's author acknowledges the filter is not ideal for genes with a clear group difference plus one deviant sample. Such genes then vanish from an FDR<0.05 list or get a shrunken fold change. CHECK: count genes with NaN pvalue (distinct from NaN padj) and genes with replaced counts; list those with large positive LFC; rerun with refit_cooks=False and cooks_filter=False (R: minReplicatesForReplace=Inf, cooksCutoff=FALSE) and compare the top 20. IF FOUND: inspect the per-sample counts of the affected genes; if the gene is consistently higher in IFN-beta across donors, treat the flag as a false alarm and report results with outlier handling disabled, saying so. SOURCE: https://support.bioconductor.org/p/110719/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/75103/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/129088/ ; https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.dds.DeseqDataSet.html

label: PITFALL size factors on sparse pseudobulks
text: PITFALL: Median-of-ratios size factors (DESeq2 default, PyDESeq2 size_factors_fit_type='ratio') use only genes with a non-zero count in every sample; pseudobulks built from 10-30 cells are sparse, so the size factors may rest on a few dozen very highly expressed genes (or fail with 'every gene contains at least one zero'), and if those genes are themselves interferon-responsive the normalization absorbs part of the treatment effect and biases every LFC. CHECK: count genes with all-positive counts across the pseudobulks in the model; compare size factors against total counts per pseudobulk (they should be roughly proportional) and against number of cells; look for a pseudobulk with a size factor far from the rest. IF FOUND: remove low-count genes first, then use the 'poscounts' estimator or supply library-size/TMM-type size factors; never add a pseudocount of 1 to the count matrix to get around the error; consider dropping a pseudobulk whose library is an order of magnitude smaller than the others. SOURCE: https://support.bioconductor.org/p/76548/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9160016/ ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/134077/

label: PITFALL independent filtering and NaN padj
text: PITFALL: Independent filtering and gene pre-filtering change which genes can be called at FDR<0.05. DESeq2 results set padj to NA for genes below an automatically chosen mean-count threshold (PyDESeq2 independent_filter=True, alpha=0.05 by default; R default alpha is 0.1), and a comparison like padj<0.05 silently drops NaN rows; pre-filtering genes changes the multiple-testing universe; a mismatch between the alpha used for filtering and the 0.05 cut-off gives a slightly different set. CHECK: report counts of genes tested, with NaN padj, and with padj<0.05 and LFC>0; confirm alpha=0.05 was used in the results call; confirm NaN padj genes are excluded on purpose rather than treated as significant or as zero; vary the pre-filter (none, >=10 counts in >=n samples, filter_by_expr) and see if the top 20 moves. IF FOUND: fix alpha=0.05, filter genes once per cell type before fitting (single-cell best practices advise removing lowly expressed genes per cell type), and report the filter used alongside the list. SOURCE: https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/DESeq2/inst/doc/DESeq2.html ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/70941/ ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/conditions/differential-gene-expression/ ; https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.ds.DeseqStats.html

label: PITFALL contrast direction and reference level
text: PITFALL: The contrast can come out with the wrong sign or the wrong groups. Python/R pick the reference level alphabetically, and 'IFN-beta' sorts before 'PBS', so a default coefficient is PBS vs IFN-beta and 'upregulated' genes are really the repressed ones; PyDESeq2 needs contrast=['variable','tested_level','ref_level'], and the lfc_shrink coefficient name (format like 'condition[T.IFN-beta]' in recent versions) must match the fitted coefficient, which only exists if PBS is the reference. Hyphens, spaces and underscores in level or column names may be rewritten by the tool. CHECK: print the design matrix columns / dds.varm['LFC'] column names and the results header line stating the comparison ('IFN-beta vs PBS'); confirm that a few canonical interferon-stimulated genes have positive LFC and that normalized counts of the top genes are higher in IFN-beta samples in every donor. IF FOUND: set PBS as reference explicitly (ordered categorical or ref_level) and pass the contrast explicitly as [factor, 'IFN-beta', 'PBS']; rename levels to plain alphanumerics (e.g. IFNb, PBS) before fitting if the tool complains. SOURCE: https://inmoose.readthedocs.io/en/stable/deseq.html ; https://pydeseq2.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/docstrings/pydeseq2.ds.DeseqStats.html ; https://github.com/mims-harvard/tooluniverse/blob/HEAD/plugin/skills/tooluniverse-rnaseq-deseq2/references/troubleshooting.md

label: PITFALL sum raw counts, donors as replicates
text: PITFALL: Pseudobulk built the wrong way gives wrong statistics: averaging or summing normalized/log-transformed values instead of summing raw integer counts breaks the negative-binomial model, and testing cells as replicates (Wilcoxon/t-test on cells, or donor as a covariate in a cell-level model) is pseudoreplication with heavily inflated false positives, so almost every gene passes FDR and the top 20 by LFC becomes a list of rare genes. CHECK: confirm the matrix aggregated is integer-valued raw counts (here X is raw counts and there are no layers); confirm one profile per donor x cytokine within CD14 Mono only, with the >=10-cell rule applied to CD14 Mono cells in that donor x cytokine (not to all cell types in the sample); confirm the number of rows in the DE input equals the number of pseudobulks, not cells; confirm pseudobulk sums are integers. IF FOUND: rebuild by summing raw counts per donor x cytokine and run a bulk count model (DESeq2/PyDESeq2 or edgeR) with the donor as the replicate unit. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-25960-2 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-21038-1 ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/conditions/differential-gene-expression/ ; https://atlas-protocol.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notebooks/06_differential_expression.html

label: PITFALL very small pseudobulks
text: PITFALL: Pseudobulks of 10-30 cells are far below what practitioners consider reliable (workflow guides recommend about 50 cells per sample; analysts report 'wonky' results from pseudobulks of very few cells), and cell numbers and library sizes vary several-fold between donor x condition groups, so a few tiny pseudobulks can drive both the dispersion estimates and the largest fold changes. Interferon treatment may also change how many cells are labelled CD14 Mono, making IFN-beta pseudobulks systematically smaller than PBS ones. CHECK: tabulate cells and total counts per pseudobulk for IFN-beta and PBS by donor; plot or list the first principal components of the normalized pseudobulks to see whether a sample separates by size rather than by condition; repeat the DE with a stricter threshold (e.g. >=20 cells) and compare top-20 overlap. IF FOUND: keep the task's >=10-cell rule for the reported answer, but apply a firm gene-expression filter, flag genes whose rank depends on one small pseudobulk, and report how stable the top 20 is to the cell threshold. SOURCE: https://bcbio.github.io/singlecell-reports/03_differential_expression/scRNA_pseudobulk.html ; https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9143599/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-35519-4

label: PITFALL scale max_value clipping (None vs 10)
text: PITFALL: z-score clipping silently changes the reported value. scanpy sc.pp.scale defaults to max_value=None (no clipping), but the legacy scanpy tutorial uses sc.pp.scale(adata, max_value=10) and Seurat ScaleData clips at scale.max=10 by default; the cell with the highest raw count of a marker gene is exactly the kind of outlier whose z-score can exceed 10, in which case a clipped pipeline returns exactly 10.0 instead of the true z. CHECK: compute the unclipped z for the target cell/gene and see whether |z| > 10; an answer of exactly 10.0 is the signature of clipping. IF FOUND: the two conventions give different answers, so choose deliberately: the task text says only 'z-score scale' and names no clip, so the literal reading is plain sc.pp.scale(adata) with defaults (no max_value); report the unclipped value and note the clipped alternative in your notes. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.scale.html ; https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/scaledata ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/1166

label: PITFALL normalize_total target_sum (median default vs 1e4)
text: PITFALL: wrong size-factor target in 'global scale log normalization'. scanpy sc.pp.normalize_total defaults to target_sum=None, which rescales every cell to the MEDIAN library size, whereas 'global-scaling normalization' (Seurat LogNormalize wording) means divide each cell by its total counts, multiply by a fixed scale factor of 10,000, then natural log1p. Because log1p is non-linear, the downstream z-score is NOT invariant to target_sum, so median-vs-1e4 gives different final values. CHECK: compute the final value with target_sum=1e4 and with target_sum=None and see how far apart they are; also confirm exclude_highly_expressed stays False (True changes every cell's size factor). IF FOUND: use sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4) then sc.pp.log1p(adata) as the standard global-scaling log normalization; do not rely on the default target_sum. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.normalize_total.html ; https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/pbmc3k_tutorial ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/3630

label: PITFALL select cell on raw counts before normalization; check ties
text: PITFALL: picking the wrong cell. The task asks for the cell with the highest RAW count of the gene; after depth normalization the cell with the highest normalized or scaled value is often a different (shallower) cell, so taking argmax after normalize_total/log1p/scale selects the wrong cell. Ties are a second trap: raw counts are small integers, several cells can share the maximum, and tied cells have different library sizes and therefore different final values. CHECK: take argmax on the untouched integer matrix BEFORE any normalization and store the obs_name; count how many cells equal the max ((col == col.max()).sum()); compare with the argmax of the normalized column. IF FOUND: always index the final matrix by the stored raw-argmax cell; if there are ties, np.argmax's first occurrence is the conventional pick, but report the tie and the values for all tied cells in your notes. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.normalize_total.html

label: PITFALL in-place normalization aliases the raw counts
text: PITFALL: 'raw' counts that are no longer raw because scanpy works in place. normalize_total, log1p and scale all overwrite adata.X; a 'saved' reference such as counts = adata.X, adata.layers['counts'] = adata.X, or adata.raw = adata made without .copy() can alias the same array and get normalized too (scanpy issue 3073), so a later 'raw argmax' is silently computed on normalized values. This file has no layers and no .raw; X is a dense int64 array (6420 cells x 19918 genes). CHECK: before normalizing assert X is non-negative integers (dtype int64, X.min() >= 0) and extract the gene's raw column with .copy(); after normalizing assert that saved column is still integer-valued. IF FOUND: reload the file, compute and store the raw-argmax cell name first (or keep adata.X.copy()), then normalize; never normalize twice (scanpy warns 'adata.X seems to be already log-transformed'). SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3073 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/does-processing-the-data-always-overwrite-the-raw-counts/1094

label: PITFALL no filtering/HVG subsetting before scaling
text: PITFALL: z-scores depend on which cells and genes are in the matrix. Each gene's mean and sd are computed over the cells present when scaling, and each cell's size factor is its total over the genes present when normalizing; so any extra filter_cells/filter_genes, QC removal, highly-variable-gene subsetting or regress_out inserted from a 'standard pipeline' template changes the final value, and HVG subsetting can drop the gene of interest entirely (Seurat ScaleData scales only variable features by default; 'you should re-scale after subsetting as the mean and sd will change'). CHECK: confirm adata.shape is unchanged (6420 x 19918) from load to final value and that the gene is still in var_names after scaling. IF FOUND: the task says only normalize + scale 'the given .h5ad', so apply normalize_total -> log1p -> scale to all cells and all genes with no filtering, no HVG subset, no regress_out (obs already has n_genes, suggesting cell filtering was done upstream). SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/2365 ; https://satijalab.org/seurat/reference/scaledata

label: PITFALL target_sum=None median differs dense vs sparse (scanpy <1.12.4)
text: PITFALL: default target_sum is computed differently for dense and sparse input in some scanpy versions. With target_sum=None, scanpy 1.11.2-1.12.3 uses the median over NON-ZERO-count cells for dense arrays but the plain median for CSR matrices (fixed in 1.12.4), and zero-count cells produce divide-by-zero in manual size-factor code. This file's X is a DENSE int64 array, so converting it to sparse first could change a median-based result. CHECK: (adata.X.sum(axis=1) == 0).sum() — are there zero-count cells; print scanpy.__version__. IF FOUND: this only bites the median default; passing an explicit target_sum=1e4 removes the version/array-type dependence. With zero-count cells, do not drop them silently (that changes gene means/sds) — note it. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/release-notes/index.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/1.12.x/src/scanpy/preprocessing/_normalization.py

label: PITFALL ddof=1 vs ddof=0 and float32; use manual cross-check
text: PITFALL: hand-rolled z-score uses a different sd convention or dtype than scanpy. sc.pp.scale uses the sample variance (ddof=1) and sets sd=1 for zero-variance genes; np.std and sklearn StandardScaler use ddof=0; normalize_total casts integer X to float32, a manual numpy pipeline runs in float64. With 6420 cells ddof changes z by a factor sqrt(6420/6419) (about 8e-5 relative) and float32 adds ~1e-6 relative error, so these are small but they are the expected size of disagreement between a correct manual check and scanpy. CHECK: recompute the single gene by hand in float64: x = log1p(raw_col / totals * 1e4); z = (x[cell] - x.mean()) / x.std(ddof=1); compare to the scanpy value. IF FOUND: agreement to ~1e-4 relative confirms the pipeline; a larger gap means a real method difference (target_sum, clipping, filtering, wrong cell), not rounding — find it before reporting. Report the scanpy (ddof=1) value. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.scale.html ; https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/23758

label: PITFALL gene symbol lookup: exact, unique var_name
text: PITFALL: gene looked up by the wrong or an ambiguous name. Gene symbols are case-sensitive (mouse 'Mrc1' vs human 'MRC1'), var_names can be non-unique (duplicates make adata[:, 'Mrc1'] ambiguous, and var_names_make_unique renames later copies to 'Mrc1-1'), and some files index by Ensembl ID with symbols in a var column. In this file var has only an index and no extra columns. CHECK: (adata.var_names == 'Mrc1').sum() must equal 1 and adata.var_names.is_unique should be True; extract the column with adata.var_names.get_loc('Mrc1') and confirm it is a single integer. IF FOUND: if duplicated, do not sum or pick silently — report it; if absent, look for a case variant or symbol column before concluding anything. SOURCE: https://anndata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generated/anndata.AnnData.var_names_make_unique.html

label: What the final z-score is and is not sensitive to
text: FACT (method note, not a pitfall): the final z-score is invariant to the log base (log2/log10/ln of 1+x differ by a constant factor that cancels in (x-mean)/sd), so do not spend effort on the base; natural log (sc.pp.log1p default, Seurat LogNormalize) is standard. The z-score is NOT invariant to the scale factor (1e4 vs median vs 1e6), to the pseudocount, to clipping (max_value), or to the set of cells included. Standard order is normalize_total -> log1p -> scale; scaling must be done on the log-normalized matrix, not on raw counts. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/3630 ; https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering-2017.html

label: PITFALL batch-key: DataFrame.sample method shadows column test
text: PITFALL: Testing for the obs column with attribute access gives a wrong, always-true answer, because pandas DataFrame has a built-in method called .sample; hasattr(adata.obs, 'sample') and getattr(adata.obs, 'sample', None) are True/non-None whether or not a column named sample exists. CHECK: test membership only with 'sample' in adata.obs.columns (or 'sample' in adata.obs) and print list(adata.obs.columns) next to the boolean so the decision is visible. IF FOUND: replace any hasattr/dot-access test with the explicit .columns membership test and use bracket access adata.obs['sample'] afterwards. SOURCE: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/5904 ; https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24870306/how-to-check-if-a-column-exists-in-pandas

label: PITFALL batch-key: .node file is h5ad, sc.read extension dispatch fails
text: PITFALL: The data file 159007346.node is an AnnData HDF5 (h5ad-format) file with a non-standard .node extension; scanpy.read()/sc.read dispatches on file extension and will fail or mis-parse it, which tempts analysts to guess the obs columns instead of reading them. CHECK: open it with anndata.read_h5ad('159007346.node') (optionally backed='r' to avoid loading the ~435 MB matrix; it does not care about the extension) and confirm adata.obs is a DataFrame with age_group present. IF FOUND: never use sc.read with extension inference for this file; use read_h5ad or pass ext='h5ad', and base the batch-key decision only on the columns actually read. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/blob/main/src/scanpy/readwrite.py ; https://anndata.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/anndata.io.read_h5ad.html

label: PITFALL batch-key: obs columns vs index vs other slots
text: PITFALL: Confusing the obs index, obs values or other slots with obs columns. In pandas 'x' in df tests column labels but 'x' in df['col'] tests the Series index, not values; in h5ad the obs index is stored as its own dataset (named by the _index attribute) inside the obs group and real columns are listed in the column-order attribute, so a raw h5py listing of obs keys mixes the index with the columns; var, uns and raw are not obs. CHECK: decide from adata.obs.columns after anndata.read_h5ad; if inspecting with h5py, use f['obs'].attrs['column-order'] and ignore the entry named by f['obs'].attrs['_index']; also print adata.obs.index.name. IF FOUND: a name that appears only as the index name, only in var/uns/raw, or only as a value inside another column does not count as an obs column named sample. SOURCE: https://anndata.readthedocs.io/en/stable/fileformat-prose.html ; https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78499163/why-the-difference-in-checking-for-value-of-pd-dataframe-vs-pd-series-if-value-i

label: PITFALL batch-key: exact name match, no fuzzy matching or overriding the rule
text: PITFALL: Fuzzy or judgement-based matching changes a deterministic rule. The rule is exact: a column literally named 'sample' (case-sensitive, no extra whitespace) selects sample, otherwise age_group. Near-miss names such as Sample, sample_id, orig.ident, batch, donor or library do not satisfy rule 1, and conversely an existing sample column must be used even if it looks unsuitable (few levels, nested inside age_group, non-categorical dtype). CHECK: print repr() of every obs column name and evaluate the exact string equality; do not use str.contains, lower() or startswith. IF FOUND: apply the rule literally and mention the near-miss or data-quality observation only as a note, not as a reason to pick the other key. SOURCE: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24870306/how-to-check-if-a-column-exists-in-pandas ; https://www.zerve.ai/data-science-problems/pandas/keyerror-column-not-found-fix

label: PITFALL batch-key: do not override rule with confounding arguments; condition-as-batch removes biology
text: PITFALL: Second-guessing the stated rule with integration theory. Best practice says the batch covariate sets which variation is removed; the per-sample level is the usual batch key, and using the biological condition itself (Adult vs Aged age_group) as batch key regresses out the biology of interest, while samples are fully nested within age group so the two can never be separated by design. An analyst who reasons 'sample is confounded with age, so I will use age_group' (or the reverse) departs from the deterministic instruction. CHECK: pd.crosstab(adata.obs[<sample col>], adata.obs['age_group']) if a sample column exists, purely to document nesting; confirm age_group has only the levels Adult and Aged. IF FOUND: still report the key chosen by the rule; note that age_group as batch key is only the stated fallback and would remove age signal if used for correction downstream. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular-structure/integration/ ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/scvi-integration-using-two-batch-keys/1758 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/failure-to-remove-a-batch-key-effect-of-number-of-lvs/1973

label: PITFALL batch-key: tiny/NaN/non-categorical batches break HVG batch_key but do not change the choice
text: PITFALL: A batch key that exists can still break downstream batch-aware steps: scanpy highly_variable_genes(batch_key=...) raises ZeroDivisionError when any batch has a single cell, old versions raise TypeError on non-categorical keys, NaN or unused categories create phantom batches, and n_top_genes is applied per batch then combined. CHECK: adata.obs[batch_key].value_counts(dropna=False), dtype, and number of unused categories. IF FOUND: this does not change which key the rule selects; cast to str/category, drop unused categories or tiny batches only for the downstream computation, and report the key name unchanged. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/3103 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2236 ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/758

label: PITFALL batch-key: answer must be the letter; silent fallback to else-branch on swallowed errors
text: PITFALL: Reporting the key name instead of the option letter, or wrapping the answer wrongly. The required answer is a JSON object with field answer holding a single letter, where A means sample and B means age_group; writing 'sample' or 'age_group' as the value, or adding extra fields or prose to eval_answer.json, fails an exact-match grader. CHECK: after deciding batch_key, map it with {'sample': 'A', 'age_group': 'B'}[batch_key], write eval_answer.json, then re-read it with json.load and assert the value is in {'A','B'} and consistent with the printed column list. label: PITFALL double log-normalization
text: PITFALL: The file header suggests X is already normalized and log1p-transformed (float32 X, uns['log1p'] present, raw integers in layers['counts']), so running normalize_total + log1p on X again double-transforms the data, which compresses high-expression genes and changes both HVG ranking and PC loadings. CHECK: print X.max(), whether X values are integers, whether np.expm1(X).sum(1) is constant across cells (e.g. 1e4), and whether layers['counts'] holds non-negative integers. IF FOUND: do not normalize/log X again; either use X as the log-normalized matrix or rebuild it once from layers['counts'] (normalize_total target_sum=1e4, log1p) and confirm the two agree. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1333 ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/differences-between-x-raw-x-and-raw-in-anndata-object/1192

label: PITFALL HVG flavor input mismatch
text: PITFALL: HVG flavors need different inputs: flavor='seurat' and 'cell_ranger' expect log-normalized data, while flavor='seurat_v3' expects raw integer counts, and feeding the wrong matrix silently gives a different gene set (seurat_v3 only warns 'expects raw count data, but non-integers were found'). CHECK: confirm which matrix each HVG call sees; for seurat_v3 pass layer='counts'; for seurat use log X. Note uns['log1p'] in this file is an empty dict with no 'base' key, which in some scanpy versions raises KeyError 'base' in highly_variable_genes(flavor='seurat') (this last point is from background knowledge, not a retrieved page); if it occurs set adata.uns['log1p']['base'] = None. IF FOUND: fix the input, then compute HVGs with n_top_genes about 2000 and compare the PC1 top-20 across flavors. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html ; https://discourse.scverse.org/t/how-to-handle-data-lognormalization-when-using-highly-variable-genes-with-flavor-seurat-v3/1076

label: PITFALL loadings extraction
text: PITFALL: Reading PC1 loadings from the wrong place or misaligned: scanpy stores loadings in adata.varm['PCs'] (rows = var_names, column 0 = PC1), and sc.pp.pca by default restricts to var['highly_variable'] when it exists, so non-HVG genes have loading 0 and a matrix scaled on all genes vs HVG-subset gives different PCs. CHECK: assert adata.varm['PCs'].shape[0] == adata.n_vars, build pd.Series(adata.varm['PCs'][:,0], index=adata.var_names), sort by absolute value, and confirm the top 20 are all HVGs with non-zero loadings; confirm PC1 is the component with the largest uns['pca']['variance_ratio']. IF FOUND: subset to HVGs (or keep the mask), scale, rerun PCA, and re-extract. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.pca.html ; https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/836

label: PITFALL PC sign and both poles
text: PITFALL: A principal component is a contrast with arbitrary sign, so a top-20-by-absolute-loading list may come entirely from one pole and hide what sits at the other end; naming the axis from one pole alone mislabels it (e.g. seeing only genes of one cell class and calling it a 'program'). CHECK: report the sign of each of the top 20 genes, and separately list the top ~20 positive and top ~20 negative loading genes; then see which cells sit at each end of obsm['X_pca'][:,0]. IF FOUND (one-sided top 20): interpret PC1 using both poles and the cells at each extreme, not the gene list alone. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pl.pca_loadings.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4543476/

label: sc23 data layout and antibody panel
text: DATA FACT (from file headers only, no analysis): GSE276492_combined.h5 holds 5 samples as top-level groups (GSM8499463_S7, GSM8499464_S8, GSM8499465_S10, GSM8499466_S13, GSM8499467_S15), each with assays/protein_read_counts/layers/read_counts (called cells x 48 antibodies; 2518, 5988, 6912, 4826 and 3714 cells = 23,958 in total) and a separate all_barcodes/protein_read_counts (hundreds of thousands of raw, mostly non-cell barcodes). Only raw read_counts exist, no normalized layer. Antibody names are in ca/id: CD10, CD117, CD11b, CD11c, CD123, CD13, CD138, CD14, CD141, CD16, CD163, CD19, CD1c, CD2, CD22, CD25, CD3, CD30, CD303, CD304, CD33, CD34, CD366, CD38, CD4, CD44, CD45, CD45RA, CD45RO, CD49d, CD5, CD56, CD62L, CD62P, CD64, CD69, CD7, CD70, CD71, CD8, CD83, CD90, CD99, FcεRIα (stored HTML-escaped as 'FcεRIα'), HLA-DR, plus three isotype controls IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b. Panel is TotalSeq-D Heme Oncology + CD70; the DNA panel is a custom myeloid panel, so expect patient samples from a myeloid malignancy with blasts, not healthy PBMC. There is no CD20, CD15 or CD66b.

label: PITFALL gene-family names vs what PC separates
text: PITFALL: Gene-family names in a loadings list do not by themselves identify the axis: ribosomal protein (RPL/RPS) genes differ strongly between hematopoietic cell types, so their presence can mark cell-type identity rather than a translation/ribosome-biogenesis program; likewise a few immediate-early genes (FOS, JUN, DUSP1) or a few cycle genes do not make a stress or proliferation axis. CHECK: count how many of the top 20 fall in each class (RPL/RPS, lineage/surface markers, IEG/heat-shock, cell-cycle such as MKI67/TOP2A), then test what PC1 actually separates: group PC1 scores by obs['popv_prediction'] and compute between-cell-type vs within-cell-type variance (eta-squared / one-way ANOVA R2). IF FOUND (PC1 variance mostly between annotated cell types): name the axis by which cell types sit at each pole; if mostly within cell types, a program-type axis (translation, stress, cycle) is supported. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-016-1104-z ; https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.basic/dimensionality-reduction.html

label: Denominator must be all called protein cells
text: PITFALL: Using the wrong cell set or denominator changes every percentage against the 1.0% cut-off: all_barcodes/protein_read_counts contains raw non-cell barcodes, and dropping QC-failed or unassignable cells shrinks the denominator and inflates rare labels. CHECK: confirm the cell count used equals the sum of the five assays/protein_read_counts matrices (23,958) and that the label counts, including Other/Unassigned, sum to it; also tabulate each label's fraction per sample to see whether a pooled >=1% call comes from a single sample. IF FOUND: use only the called cells under assays/, pool all five samples as the denominator, and put low-quality or ambiguous cells into Other/Unassigned instead of deleting them. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/curated_notebooks/dna-protein-multisample.html (raw=False loads cell-associated barcodes only) and the file headers.

label: PITFALL PC1 vs depth
text: PITFALL: The log-normalize + HVG + PCA pipeline can put technical variation (sequencing depth, number of detected genes, fraction of zeros) into leading PCs; Townes et al. 2019 state that log-CPM normalization and HVG selection 'produce false variability in dimension reduction'. No QC columns exist in this file, so nothing guards against it. CHECK: compute total_counts and n_genes_by_counts from layers['counts'] (plus pct MT- and pct RPL/RPS) and take Spearman correlation with PC1 score, both overall and within each popv_prediction cell type. IF FOUND (strong correlation within cell types): PC1 is partly technical, so interpret via cell-type separation and confirm the top-20 gene class is unchanged across variants rather than adding non-standard steps; if the correlation is only between cell types it is likely confounded with cell identity (cell types differ in RNA content) and not a reason to relabel the axis. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-019-1861-6 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6582955/

label: CLR is compositional and biases marker gating
text: PITFALL: CLR normalization (the Mosaic default, per-cell centred log ratio across the antibody panel) is compositional: with a small hand-picked panel, a cell that is bright for many markers (myeloid cells, blasts) gets a large geometric mean, pushing its other markers down, while lymphocytes with few bright markers have background pushed up; the CLR negative peak is not at zero and sits at different values in different cell types. CHECK: plot each lineage marker (CD3, CD19, CD14, CD56, CD123, CD11c) under CLR versus asinh or log of library-scaled counts and see whether the negative peak location differs between cell groups; re-run the labelling under a second normalization (asinh or NSP-style total-count-corrected) and compare label fractions. IF FOUND: do not gate on a single global CLR cut-off; use per-marker thresholds placed in the valley between negative and positive peaks, and treat any label whose >=1% status flips between normalizations as unresolved and settle it with explicit multi-marker gating. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61023-6 ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/surface-protein/normalization/ ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.normalize_reads.html

label: PITFALL scaling and outlier populations
text: PITFALL: Scaling every HVG to unit variance up-weights low-expressed and rare-population genes, and without clipping a handful of extreme cells (the labels include rare platelets, plasma cells, pDC and stem cells) can pull a leading PC toward a tiny population instead of the main axis. CHECK: use sc.pp.scale(adata, max_value=10) as in the standard scanpy workflow, look at the distribution of PC1 scores (is the variance carried by under ~2 percent of cells?), and rerun without max_value to see whether the PC1 top 20 changes. IF FOUND (PC1 driven by a few outlier cells or changes with clipping): report the clipped (max_value=10) result as the standard one and state the sensitivity. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html ; https://github.com/alterlab-ieu/alterlab-academic-skills/blob/main/skills/bioinformatics/alterlab-scanpy/references/standard_workflow.md

label: Background is not zero: per-marker thresholds and isotypes
text: PITFALL: Antibody-tag counts have a non-zero background peak (ambient/unbound antibody plus non-specific binding) for every marker, so 'count > 0', 'CLR > 0' or one cut-off shared by all markers calls background as positive and inflates rare labels such as pDC and cDC. CHECK: for each gating marker and each sample, look at the density of log or asinh counts for a negative and a positive mode, and compare with the three isotype controls (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b), which give the noise floor. IF FOUND: set a separate threshold per marker (valley or two-component Gaussian mixture on the log scale, background mean subtracted), require specific markers to clearly exceed isotype level, never use the isotype controls as clustering features, and do not rely on isotypes alone to place a gate since they mark the noise floor, not the positive boundary. SOURCE: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dsb/vignettes/no_empty_drops.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29356-8 ; https://www.bio-rad-antibodies.com/flow-cytometry-guide-isotype-controls.html

label: PITFALL stress signature vs cell type
text: PITFALL: A handling/stress signature can be real yet not be PC1 of the whole dataset: in PBMC scRNA-seq, sampling-time stress correlated with PC1 only when PCA was run within each cell subtype, while across all PBMC cell type was the greatest driver of variance and sampling time came after it. CHECK: if immediate-early or stress genes appear in the top 20, check whether they load on the same pole as lineage markers of one cell class and whether PC1 scores still separate annotated cell types (popv_prediction). IF FOUND: do not call PC1 a stress axis unless PC1 varies mainly within cell types and the top loadings are dominated by IEG/heat-shock genes on one pole with no lineage markers. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7212672/

label: Per-sample staining batch effects
text: PITFALL: The five samples were stained and sequenced separately, so negative and positive peaks of the same marker sit at different values per sample; normalizing or thresholding the pooled matrix lets one sample's background look like another sample's positive population, and Mosaic's NSP normalization fits its background/signal model to total reads within a run. CHECK: overlay per-sample densities of CD3, CD19, CD14, CD4, CD8, CD56, CD123 and of total antibody reads per cell; look for shifted peaks or very different sequencing depth. IF FOUND: normalize and set thresholds per sample (or align negative/positive peaks across samples) before pooling labels, and check that clusters are not simply samples. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-61023-6 ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/missionbio.demultiplex.protein.nsp.NSP.html

label: PITFALL robustness to HVG and scaling choices
text: PITFALL: The PC1 top-20 list depends on arbitrary choices (HVG flavor and number, clipping, solver, gene pre-filtering), and Townes et al. note HVG selection is 'somewhat arbitrary' because observed variability depends on the pseudocount; a single run can give an unrepresentative list. CHECK: run at least three variants (e.g. seurat on log X with n_top_genes=2000; seurat_v3 on layers['counts'] with 2000; scanpy default mean/dispersion thresholds), each with scale(max_value=10) and svd_solver='arpack', after sc.pp.filter_genes(min_cells=3), and compare the gene classes in the top 20 and the correlation of PC1 scores between variants (use absolute correlation, sign is arbitrary). IF FOUND (variants disagree on the axis): report the disagreement and prefer the plain scanpy-tutorial pipeline as 'standard'; if they agree, the answer is robust. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-019-1861-6 ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html

label: Sticky cells, Fc binding and doublets fake co-expression
text: PITFALL: Some cells carry a cell-wide technical signal (antibody aggregates, dead or sticky cells, Fc-receptor binding on monocytes and other myeloid cells, doublets) and look positive for everything, including mutually exclusive lineage markers; they get mis-gated into T, B, NK or DC labels. CHECK: per cell, compare summed isotype-control counts (IgG1+IgG2a+IgG2b) and total antibody counts with the rest of the sample; count cells positive for exclusive pairs (CD3 with CD19, CD3 with CD14, CD19 with CD14) and see whether they are the high-isotype or high-total cells; check whether isotype signal is higher in CD14/CD64-positive cells. IF FOUND: require a marker to exceed the cell's own isotype/background level (the dsb idea of removing the per-cell technical component), label cross-lineage and high-isotype cells Other/Unassigned, and keep them in the denominator. SOURCE: https://github.com/niaid/dsb ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29356-8 ; https://zsa.med.uni-rostock.de/fileadmin/Institute/zsa/documents/CF_ZSA/S_02_Perfekte_Kontrolle__07.03.2023.pdf

label: Leukemic blasts contaminate mature lineage gates
text: PITFALL: These are likely myeloid-malignancy samples (custom myeloid DNA panel, heme-oncology antibody panel), so a large share of cells may be immature blasts (CD34 and/or CD117 positive, CD33/CD13 positive, CD45 dim) that fit none of the mature labels cleanly and can aberrantly carry CD7, CD56, CD4, CD123 or CD11c; a healthy-PBMC gating scheme will scatter them across NK, CD4_T, pDC and cDC. CHECK: measure the fraction of cells positive for CD34 or CD117, and how many cells currently labelled NK, CD4_T, pDC or cDC are also CD34/CD117/CD33/CD13 positive; also look for CD71-bright erythroid and CD138-bright plasma cells. IF FOUND: gate immature/blast, erythroid and plasma cells out first, decide explicitly and state whether CD34/CD117-positive myeloid cells go to Myelomonocytic or to Other/Unassigned, and report whether the final present-label set is the same under both conventions. SOURCE: https://www.cytometry.org/web/modules/Module_30.pdf ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13748365/ ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-020-19119-8

label: pDC needs CD123 + HLA-DR + CD303/CD304, not CD123 alone
text: PITFALL: Calling pDC from CD123 alone over-counts: basophils are CD123-bright but HLA-DR-negative and FcεRIα-positive, monocytes can be CD123/HLA-DR bright, and myeloid or monocytic blasts were CD123-bright in about 14% of AML cases; pDCs are also CD4-positive and CD3-negative, so a CD4 gate without CD3 puts them (and monocytes) into CD4_T. Normal pDCs are well under 1% of leukocytes, and pDC expansion of 2% or more occurs in only about 4-5% of AML, so the 1% decision for pDC sits right at the edge. CHECK: among CD123-high cells, tabulate HLA-DR, CD303, CD304, FcεRIα, CD34, CD64, CD14, CD11c, CD3, CD19; count how many are HLA-DR+ with CD303 and/or CD304 and negative for CD3/CD19/CD14/CD64/CD34. IF FOUND: define pDC as CD123-high AND HLA-DR+ AND (CD303+ or CD304+) AND lineage-negative (CD3, CD19, CD14, CD64, CD11c low, CD34 negative); send CD123+ HLA-DR-negative FcεRIα+ cells (basophils) and CD123+ CD34+ cells (blasts) elsewhere; report the pDC fraction under strict and loose definitions. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13748365/ ; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/cyto.a.24269 ; https://haematologica.org/article/view/9708 ; https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/16/11/2118

label: cDC versus monocyte versus B cell overlap
text: PITFALL: cDC and monocytes share CD11c, HLA-DR, CD33 and CD4-dim, so a 'CD11c+ HLA-DR+' rule labels monocytes as cDC (or all cDC as Myelomonocytic), and the cDC fraction near 1% then depends entirely on that rule; CD1c is also found on some B cells, and FcεRIα marks both cDC2 and basophils. CHECK: within HLA-DR+ CD11c+ cells that are CD3/CD19/CD56-negative, split by CD14 and CD64 and look at CD1c, CD141 and FcεRIα; confirm that CD1c+ cells labelled cDC are CD19/CD22-negative and CD123-low. IF FOUND: define cDC as HLA-DR+ CD11c+ with CD1c+ (cDC2) or CD141-high (cDC1), CD14-negative, CD64-low, CD123-negative/dim, lineage-negative; assign CD14+ or CD64-high cells to Myelomonocytic; state the cDC fraction under this strict rule and under the looser one. SOURCE: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/cyto.a.24269 (CD1c-on-B-cells and CD141-low-on-monocytes are general immunology knowledge, not quoted from the source)

label: CD4, CD8, CD56, CD16 are not lineage-specific
text: PITFALL: No single surface marker in this panel is lineage-restricted for T subsets or NK: CD4 is dim on monocytes and present on pDC; CD8 is dim on a subset of NK cells; CD56 is on NK-like T cells, on aberrant monocytes and on some AML blasts; CD16 is on non-classical monocytes and neutrophils as well as NK (and under 5% of cytotoxic T cells). Gating CD4_T, CD8_T or NK on one marker shifts cells between labels. CHECK: cross-tabulate CD3 against CD4, CD8, CD56 and CD16; within CD3-negative CD56+ or CD16+ cells check CD7 (NK are CD7+) and CD14/CD33/CD64/CD11b (myeloid); count CD3+ cells that are CD4+CD8+ or CD4-CD8-. IF FOUND: require CD3+ for both T labels (backed by CD5/CD2/CD7), define NK as CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD14/CD64/CD33-negative with CD56+ and/or CD16+ and CD7+, send CD3+CD56+ cells to their T label, and fix a stated rule for double-positive and double-negative T cells. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1182/blood-2009-04-216374 ; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cyto.a.22245 ; https://doi.org/10.1309/q49crj030l22mhlf

label: Cluster-level labels hide or split rare populations
text: PITFALL: Labelling whole clusters (Leiden/k-means on UMAP, as in the Mosaic workflow) merges rare populations such as pDC, cDC, NK or B cells into a larger neighbour when there are too few clusters, or splits one lineage into several when there are too many, so label fractions near the 1% cut-off depend on clustering resolution; with about 24,000 cells 1% is roughly 240 cells, so sampling error is small and the uncertainty is in the method. CHECK: compute label fractions by direct per-cell marker gating and by cluster annotation at two or more resolutions; list every label whose fraction falls between about 0.5% and 2% under any of them; inspect marker heatmaps of each cluster for mixed content and sub-cluster mixed ones. IF FOUND: base the final assignment on per-cell hierarchical gating (or sub-clustered, marker-verified clusters), and for each borderline label state the fraction under each variant and which definition was used to decide presence. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s42003-019-0415-5 ; https://doi.org/10.1002/cyto.a.23030 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8453896/

label: PITFALL NGT=3 is missing, not mutant
text: PITFALL: In Tapestri/Mosaic NGT layers the code 3 means MISSING genotype (0=ref, 1=het, 2=hom-alt), so a test like NGT!=0 or NGT>0 counts every no-call as a mutation and makes nearly every cell 'mutant'. CHECK: print np.unique(NGT) per sample and count how many NK cells are 'mutant' under NGT>0 versus NGT in {1,2}. IF FOUND: define mutant strictly as NGT in {1,2}; treat 3 as not-called; decide the denominator explicitly (all NK cells, which is what Mosaic uses, versus NK cells genotyped at the site, which is what Tapestri Insights uses) and report whether the answer changes between the two. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html ; https://bbglab.github.io/bbgwiki/Methods/Sequencing/singleCell/Mosaic/

label: PITFALL unfiltered variants make every cell mutant
text: PITFALL: The h5 holds the UNFILTERED variant table (about 75,000 candidate sites per sample, most of them sequencing/PCR noise), so 'at least one non-reference call in any driver-gene site' is a union over thousands of sites and will be true for almost every cell of every lineage from random errors alone. CHECK: compute the fraction of cells with any raw NGT in {1,2} in a driver gene separately for NK, T cells and myelomonocytic cells; if it is near 100% in all classes, the raw criterion is not measuring clone membership. IF FOUND: apply Mosaic's standard per-call filters before counting (DP>=10, GQ>=30, het calls need VAF>=30% (20% is a common relaxed value), hom calls VAF>=95%, ref calls VAF<=5%; failing calls become missing) and keep only variants genotyped in >=50% of cells and mutated in >=1% of the sample's cells; report the count under raw and filtered calls because they can differ. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_variants.html

label: PITFALL germline SNPs counted as driver mutations
text: PITFALL: Germline SNPs inside driver-gene amplicons (TET2, ASXL1, TP53 etc. all carry common polymorphisms) are non-reference in every cell of the patient including NK and T cells, so they make NK 'participate' in every sample without any clonal involvement. CHECK: for each sample and each passing variant, compute the mutant fraction among genotyped cells in each immune class; a variant that is het or hom in roughly >=80-90% of genotyped cells in ALL classes (allow ~10% loss to allele dropout), with per-cell VAF near 50% or 100%, is germline. IF FOUND: exclude those variants and count only sample-specific somatic variants (clearly mutated in a subset of cells, typically enriched in myelomonocytic cells and depleted in T cells); Mosaic's filter_somatic_variants does this with gnomAD frequency >0.001 removal plus non-synonymous and non-homopolymer filters, but offline there is no annotation so lineage-ubiquity is the usable substitute. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_somatic_variants.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10613526/

label: PITFALL no variant annotation in file
text: PITFALL: The dataset's variant column attributes contain only CHROM, POS, REF, ALT, QUAL, amplicon and id, with no gene, protein-change or synonymous/non-synonymous annotation, and there is no web access to annotate, so 'non-synonymous' cannot be verified directly and intronic, synonymous and homopolymer-indel artefact sites inside driver amplicons will be counted. CHECK: list the col_attrs keys; parse the gene from the amplicon name (format like MYE_CSF3R_36932055; amplicons named AMP1..AMP44 have no gene) and confirm which panel genes are MDS drivers (the panel includes ASXL1, BCOR, CBL, DNMT3A, ETV6, EZH2, IDH1, IDH2, JAK2, KRAS, NRAS, NF1, PHF6, PTPN11, RUNX1, SETBP1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, TET2, TP53, U2AF1, WT1, ZRSR2 among others). IF FOUND: restrict to gene-named amplicons, drop the anonymous AMP amplicons, use the task's stated fallback (any non-reference call) but only on quality-filtered, non-germline, recurrent variants, and flag indels at homopolymers as likely artefacts. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_somatic_variants.html

label: PITFALL NK-myeloid doublets fake mutant NK cells
text: PITFALL: Droplet doublets of an NK cell with a mutant myeloid cell carry both the NK protein signal and the myeloid mutation, and Tapestri doublet rates of several percent are well above the 1% NK-mutant threshold, so doublets alone can push a sample over the line. CHECK: among NK-labelled cells that are called mutant, look at myeloid markers (CD33, CD14, CD64, CD11b, CD13), total protein and DNA read counts (doublets are higher), and per-cell VAF of the somatic variant (a het mutation diluted by a wild-type partner sits near 25% or lower instead of 50%). IF FOUND: remove mixed-phenotype cells before labelling (Mosaic's cluster_and_label names doublet clusters as 'A:B'/'Mixed'), require het VAF>=30%, and state how many mutant NK cells remain. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8275324/ ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.cluster_and_label.html

label: PITFALL CD56/CD16 are not NK-specific in MDS
text: PITFALL: NK cells have no single specific antibody marker: CD56 is aberrantly expressed on monocytes and myeloid progenitors in MDS and on CD56+ monocyte/DC-like cells, CD16 is on non-classical monocytes and granulocytes, CD7 is on T cells and aberrant blasts, and CD3+CD56+ NK-like T cells exist, so a 'CD56-high' or 'CD16-high' cluster mislabels mutant myeloid cells as NK. CHECK: confirm the NK-labelled cells are CD45-bright, CD3-negative, CD19-negative, CD14/CD33/CD64-negative, CD34/CD117-negative and CD7-positive with CD56 and/or CD16 positive; compare the NK mutant fraction with and without the CD7+ and CD33- requirements. IF FOUND: gate NK as CD3- CD19- CD14- CD33- CD7+ (CD56+ or CD16+) rather than by one marker or an unreviewed cluster label; coexpression of CD7 with CD56 is what separates true NK cells from CD56+ myeloid cells. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2786291/ ; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/cyto.a.22245 ; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/cyto.b.22108

label: PITFALL protein normalisation and isotype controls
text: PITFALL: Antibody-tag counts are dominated by ambient/nonspecific background and by per-cell staining depth, so thresholding raw counts or running one CLR over all five samples pooled gives sample-driven clusters and wrong positive/negative calls; the three isotype controls (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b) are not biology and distort clustering if left in as features. CHECK: after normalisation each lineage marker (CD3, CD19, CD14, CD33, CD56, CD7) should be bimodal within each sample, isotype controls should be flat near background, and clusters should not split by sample; cells high on all isotypes are 'sticky' and unreliable. IF FOUND: normalise within each sample (CLR per cell, or a background-aware method such as Mosaic NSP / dsb which uses isotypes and empty-droplet background), drop isotypes from the feature set, exclude sticky cells, and set marker gates per sample from the negative peak. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-022-29356-8 ; https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.normalize_reads.html ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41576-023-00586-w

label: PITFALL tiny NK counts versus 1% threshold
text: PITFALL: NK cells are a small population (often tens of cells out of a few thousand per Tapestri sample), so at a 1.0% threshold a single erroneous or doublet cell decides the sample, and a sample with zero NK-labelled cells has an undefined fraction. CHECK: report per sample the number of NK cells, the number of mutant NK cells, and the same fraction in T cells (negative control for false positives) and in myelomonocytic cells (positive control that the somatic variant is detectable). IF FOUND: do not call participation from one cell without scrutiny (Mosaic's somatic filter requires a minimum of 3 cells); compare the NK rate with the T-cell background rate, treat samples with no NK cells as not satisfying the criterion, and state how many samples flip if a 1-cell result is disallowed. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.dna.Dna.filter_somatic_variants.html

label: PITFALL file layout: five groups, unshared variant index
text: PITFALL: The file GSE276492_combined.h5 is five separate Tapestri runs stored as five top-level groups (GSM8499463_S7, GSM8499464_S8, GSM8499465_S10, GSM8499466_S13, GSM8499467_S15), each with 'assays' (called cells only, e.g. 2518 cells in S7) and 'all_barcodes' (over a million raw barcodes); each group has its own variant list, so variant column indices are not comparable across samples, and the DNA and protein assays must be joined on barcode. CHECK: use assays/dna_variants and assays/protein_read_counts (not all_barcodes), confirm ra/barcode order is identical between the DNA and protein assays in each group, read sample identity from ra/sample_name, and test the polarity of ra/filtered, ca/filtered and layers/FILTER_MASK by cross-tabulating against DP<10 or GQ<30 before using them. IF FOUND: process each sample independently, match variants across samples by id string (chr:pos:ref/alt) never by index, and count samples by unique ra/sample_name. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/v2.4.1/4_data_structure.html

label: PITFALL allele dropout blurs germline versus somatic
text: PITFALL: Tapestri allele dropout is roughly 5-12% per locus, so a heterozygous variant appears as wild-type or homozygous in a fraction of cells; this makes germline het SNPs look non-ubiquitous (hiding them from a strict '100% of cells' germline filter) and makes zygosity-based clone definitions unreliable. CHECK: for variants mutated in most cells, look at the mix of NGT 0/1/2 among genotyped cells; a het-dominant variant with ~5-10% ref and ~5-10% hom calls spread evenly over all immune classes is germline with dropout, not a subclone. IF FOUND: use a tolerant germline rule (mutant in >=80-90% of genotyped cells in every class) and count a cell as mutant on NGT 1 or 2 alike rather than on zygosity. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-47297-z ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8275324/

label: sc24 data layout from headers
text: DATA SHAPE (from file headers only, no analysis): 157798551.node is an AnnData h5ad, 6420 cells x 19918 genes, mouse gene symbols (e.g. Sox17, Mrpl15), one sample '4T1_viable' (4T1 mouse mammary carcinoma, viable-cell suspension). X is dense float32 and var has 'mean' and 'std' columns plus uns['log1p'], which suggests X is log-normalised then z-scored; integer counts are in layers['raw_counts']. obs has only 'sample' and 'n_genes'; there are no clusters, embeddings or neighbours stored. var contains a transgene named 'Kate2' (a fluorescent reporter) as the last gene.

label: PITFALL scaled X used for marker calls
text: PITFALL: adata.X appears to be z-scored (var has mean/std), so every gene has negative and positive values in every cell; thresholding markers with 'X > 0', computing 'fraction of cells expressing', log fold changes, or sc.tl.score_genes / rank_genes_groups on X gives wrong or sign-flipped results (scanpy rank_genes_groups 'expects logarithmized data'; logFC becomes negative/NaN on scaled data). CHECK: print X.min(), X.max(), per-gene mean and std of X (about 0 and 1 means scaled) and confirm layers['raw_counts'] holds integers. IF FOUND: rebuild a log-normalised matrix from layers['raw_counts'] (normalize_total + log1p) and use that, or the raw counts, for all marker inspection, dotplots, scoring and DE; use scaled values only for PCA/clustering. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.tl.rank_genes_groups.html ; https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/2057

label: PITFALL low-RNA neutrophils dropped or mislabelled
text: PITFALL: Neutrophils and other granulocytic myeloid cells have very low RNA content (few UMIs and few genes per cell), so standard QC (min_genes 200-500, low-count filters) or dismissing a low-count cluster as 'low quality/empty droplets' silently deletes a real Immune population; 4T1 tumours secrete G-CSF and are known for heavy granulocytic/myeloid infiltration, so this population can be large. Ptprc (CD45) is also often undetected per cell in such low-count cells. CHECK: plot total counts and n_genes per cluster; for any low-count cluster look at S100a8, S100a9, Csf3r, Cxcr2, Il1b, Retnlg, G0s2, Lcn2, Ngp alongside Ptprc using raw counts. IF FOUND: keep these cells, label them Immune, and do not apply extra cell-level QC filters before computing percentages (the denominator must stay all cells in the file). SOURCE: https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/tutorials/cr-tutorial-neutrophils ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3218014/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2517332/

label: PITFALL denominator must be all cells
text: PITFALL: The task asks for percentages of ALL cells in three compartments, so any cell removed (QC filter, doublet removal, 'unassigned'/'other' label, dropping endothelial or ambiguous clusters) changes the denominator and all three percentages. CHECK: confirm the three counts sum to adata.n_obs (6420 per the file header) and the percentages sum to 100. IF FOUND: assign every cell to exactly one of Immune, Epithelial/Cancer, CAF (ambiguous cells take the label of their cluster); if you flag doublets or junk, still count them in the compartment of their cluster and report how many cells were ambiguous so sensitivity can be judged. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12946769/ (pitfall on incomplete/biased cell capture and frequency comparisons)

label: PITFALL non-specific CAF markers vs hybrid E/M 4T1 cells
text: PITFALL: Common 'CAF/mesenchymal' markers are not fibroblast-specific: Vim, S100a4 (FSP1), Acta2, Fn1, Sparc, Thy1 and EMT signatures are also expressed by EMT-like carcinoma cells, macrophages, T cells (Thy1), pericytes and smooth muscle. 4T1 cancer cells are a hybrid epithelial/mesenchymal line: they keep E-cadherin (Cdh1), Epcam and keratins (Krt8, Krt18) while expressing vimentin, so a Vim/S100a4/EMT-based rule will move cancer cells (and myeloid cells) into CAF and inflate it. CHECK: for the putative CAF cluster(s) require a fibroblast matrix programme (Col1a1, Col1a2, Col3a1, Dcn, Lum, Pdgfra, Pdgfrb, Pdpn, Fap) AND absence of Ptprc and of Epcam/Krt8/Krt18/Cdh1 at cluster level; cross-tabulate Vim-high cells against Epcam/Krt and Ptprc. IF FOUND: define CAF by collagen/Pdgfr genes with negative selection for immune and epithelial markers, define Epithelial/Cancer by Epcam/Krt8/Krt18/Cdh1 (not by absence of Vim), and never use Vim, S100a4 or Acta2 alone. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41568-019-0238-1 ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40364-020-00245-w ; https://journals.biologists.com/dmm/article/17/9/dmm050771/361870 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8110844/

label: PITFALL per-cell thresholds vs cluster-level annotation and resolution
text: PITFALL: Calling compartments cell-by-cell from one marker (e.g. Ptprc>0 = Immune, Epcam>0 = Epithelial) fails because of dropout (a marker is missing in a large share of true-positive cells) and leaves many cells unassigned or assigned by noise; guidelines recommend annotating at cluster level with several positive and negative markers. The opposite error is under-clustering: a rare population (CAFs are usually a small minority in an unsorted tumour suspension) gets merged into a big cluster and vanishes. CHECK: cluster on log-normalised data (HVG, PCA, neighbours, Leiden) at two or three resolutions; per cluster inspect mean expression and fraction-expressing for marker panels; verify that cells positive for Col1a1/Dcn/Pdgfra form their own cluster at higher resolution and that the three percentages are stable across resolutions. IF FOUND: assign labels per cluster (sub-cluster any cluster whose markers are mixed), not per cell by threshold; if results move with resolution, use the finer one where clusters are marker-pure. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-021-00534-0 ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/annotation.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11374959/

label: PITFALL endothelial and mural cells in a three-label scheme
text: PITFALL: A whole-tumour suspension contains stromal cells that fit none of the three requested labels cleanly: endothelial cells (Pecam1, Cdh5, Kdr, Emcn) and mural cells/pericytes/smooth muscle (Rgs5, Pdgfrb, Acta2, Myh11, Des, Notch3, Mcam). Pericytes share Pdgfrb/Acta2 with CAFs and are often reported as 'vascular CAFs'; where these cells are put shifts the CAF percentage, which is small and therefore sensitive. CHECK: within Ptprc-negative, Epcam/Krt-negative clusters, look at Pecam1/Cdh5 and Rgs5/Myh11 versus Pdgfra/Dcn/Lum/Col1a1 and count each group. IF FOUND: a three-way scheme forces a choice; the usual convention is that non-immune, non-epithelial mesenchymal stroma (fibroblasts plus mural cells) goes to CAF, and endothelial cells also go with the stromal (CAF) compartment rather than Immune or Epithelial/Cancer; report the size of these groups so the effect of the choice is visible. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17740-1 ; https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/article/S1535-6108(24)00310-6/fulltext ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6279758/

label: PITFALL ambient RNA and doublets fake marker expression
text: PITFALL: Ambient RNA and heterotypic doublets make cells appear to express another lineage's markers: highly abundant transcripts (keratins and other cancer-cell genes, neutrophil S100a8/S100a9, reporter transgenes) are found at low level in every droplet, most visibly in low-UMI cells, so 'any count > 0' rules misassign cells; doublets co-express Ptprc and Epcam/Krt or Col1a1 and form small intermediate clusters with high counts. CHECK: compare cluster-level mean and fraction-expressing rather than presence/absence; look for clusters with markers of two lineages and unusually high total counts and n_genes (doublets) versus low uniform background in all clusters (ambient). IF FOUND: base labels on which marker programme is dominant per cluster; do not create an extra class and do not drop the cells (see denominator pitfall) - assign a doublet cluster to its dominant lineage and note its size. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7763177/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12946769/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10278251/

label: PITFALL Kate2 reporter used as a per-cell gate
text: PITFALL: The gene list contains a reporter transgene 'Kate2' (fluorescent protein). It is tempting to call Kate2>0 cells cancer and Kate2=0 cells non-cancer, but which cell population carries the reporter is not stated in the file, transgene detection in 3' droplet data is incomplete (many labelled cells have zero reads), and abundant reporter RNA leaks into other droplets as ambient signal. CHECK: on raw counts, tabulate Kate2 mean and fraction-positive per cluster next to Epcam/Krt8/Krt18, Ptprc and Col1a1 to see which lineage it marks and how complete it is. IF FOUND: use Kate2 only as supporting cluster-level evidence for the compartment it is enriched in; never as a per-cell positive or negative gate. label: PITFALL cycling cluster mixes lineages; MHC-II not immune-specific

IF FOUND: do not report a number from an arbitrary k without saying so; prefer the tool default for the implementation actually used (inspect the installed function signature rather than guessing), keep Louvain resolution at 1.0, and state k in the answer notes. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/v2.4.1/examples/analysis-walkthrough.html
