label: UMAP min_dist=0 is the Mosaic protein default
text: PITFALL: Mosaic's Protein.run_umap overrides UMAP defaults to n_neighbors=50, metric='cosine', min_dist=0, whereas plain umap-learn defaults to min_dist=0.1 and metric='euclidean' and scanpy's sc.tl.umap inherits the metric from sc.pp.neighbors. The task overrides n_neighbors to 20 and names cosine but says nothing of min_dist, so a re-implementation with min_dist=0.1 (or cosine set in the wrong place) yields a looser embedding and a different cluster count than the Mosaic workflow with min_dist=0. CHECK: print the actual UMAP parameters used (n_neighbors, metric, min_dist, n_components=2) and confirm cosine is applied to the 10-PC input, not to the 2-D output. IF FOUND: use umap.UMAP(n_neighbors=20, metric='cosine', min_dist=0, n_components=2) on the PCA matrix to mirror the standard workflow, and report whether min_dist=0 vs 0.1 changes n_clusters. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.protein.Protein.run_umap.html

label: CLR axis and formula: per cell across antibodies, log1p
text: PITFALL: 'CLR' is not one formula. The original CITE-seq CLR is per cell (each cell's antibody counts divided by that cell's geometric mean across antibodies); Seurat's default margin=1 instead normalises each antibody across cells, and its formula is log1p(x / exp(sum(log1p(x[x>0]))/n)) which is always >=0; muon.prot.pp.clr defaults to axis=0 with flavor='seurat'. These give different PCA spaces and different clusters. For Tapestri data the per-cell version is the relevant one (it corrects for per-cell antibody read depth); Mosaic's normalize_reads default method is 'CLR' and jitter applies only to NSP/asinh. CHECK: after normalising, verify the row (per-cell) means of the normalised matrix are ~0 if using log1p(x) minus the per-cell mean of log1p(x); confirm no NaN/inf from zero counts. IF FOUND: compute CLR per cell across the 48 antibodies with a +1 pseudocount (log1p(x) - mean over antibodies of log1p(x)); do not use a per-antibody (across-cells) CLR, and do not add jitter. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/3605

label: No scaling / isotype removal / filtering before PCA
text: PITFALL: Habitual scRNA-seq preprocessing silently added around the four named steps changes the answer: z-scoring features before PCA (sc.pp.scale), dropping isotype controls (this panel has IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b among its 48 antibodies), filtering cells, or batch-correcting samples. The Mosaic workflow runs PCA directly on the CLR 'normalized_counts' layer with all antibodies; scale_data is a separate optional method and is not part of the described pipeline. CHECK: confirm the PCA input is the unscaled CLR matrix of shape (n_cells, 48), that PCA only mean-centres (sklearn PCA default), and that the output is (n_cells, 10). IF FOUND: remove any scaling, feature selection, antibody removal or batch correction that the task did not ask for; if you believe isotype removal is warranted, report it only as a sensitivity result. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/pages/methods/missionbio.mosaic.assay._Assay.run_pca.html

label: Seed sensitivity of UMAP + Louvain
text: PITFALL: UMAP is stochastic and Louvain is too (python-louvain best_partition has random_state=None and networkx louvain_communities has seed=None by default), so n_clusters from one unseeded run is not reproducible; also UMAP 'can create false tears in clusters, resulting in a finer clustering than is necessarily present', so Louvain on a 2-D UMAP is seed-sensitive by construction. Setting random_state in umap-learn forces single-threaded, reproducible layout, but results can still differ across umap-learn/numba/pynndescent versions. CHECK: repeat the full pipeline with at least 5-10 different UMAP and Louvain seeds and tabulate n_clusters; report the mode and the range. IF FOUND: fix seeds (random_state=42 is the value Mosaic notebooks use), report the modal count, and flag in notes if the count varies by more than +-1 across seeds, since then no single integer is robust. SOURCE: https://umap-learn.readthedocs.io/en/latest/clustering.html

label: Pooling samples: barcode collisions and sample-driven clusters
text: PITFALL: Pooling 5 patient samples without thinking about depth makes clusters track sample rather than cell type, and a pooled CLR differs from per-sample CLR only if CLR is done across cells; per-cell CLR is identical whether samples are pooled before or after normalisation, but PCA, UMAP and Louvain are not. Barcodes are 18-mers that can repeat across samples, so concatenating by barcode alone can collide. CHECK: after pooling, cross-tabulate cluster label against sample group and check for duplicate barcodes across groups; verify all 5 groups have the same 48 antibody ids in the same order before stacking. IF FOUND: make barcodes unique by suffixing the sample name, stack in a fixed documented order, and do not add batch correction (the task does not ask for it) but mention sample-driven clusters in notes. SOURCE: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/notebooks/multi-sample-analysis.html

label: Environment: no mosaic/louvain package; file layout

label: Data layout of reference and query files
text: DATA LAYOUT (headers only, no analysis): 156259621.node is the labelled reference AnnData (118,685 cells x 22,927 genes, raw integer counts in X, 20 samples in obs['sample'], HIVE-platform cell names, labels in obs['manual_annotation_corrected'] with 20 types: naive/memory CD4 T, naive/memory/cytotoxic CD8 T, Treg, MAIT, gamma-delta T, naive/memory B, plasma cell, NK, cycling NK, classical/non-classical monocyte, dendritic cell, plasmacytoid DC, platelet, erythrocyte, peripheral blood stem cell). obs['manual_annotation'] is the uncorrected version and contains a duplicate spelling ('Memory CD8 Cells' vs 'Memory CD8 T Cells'), so use the corrected column. 156261218.node is the unlabelled query (11,693 cells x 27,946 genes, raw integer counts in X and layers['counts'], 4 samples, precomputed Seurat clusters at res 1 with 20 clusters, X_pca, X_umap, no cell-type column). Both use gene symbols; 22,902 genes are shared. HBB is absent from both gene lists, so it cannot be used as an erythrocyte marker.

label: Pitfall: denominator and non-target cell types
text: PITFALL: The reference contains labels outside the five requested categories (platelet, erythrocyte, peripheral blood stem cell), so the five percentages need not sum to 100; renormalising them to 100, or forcing every query cell into one of five classes, inflates every category. CHECK: after annotation, count query cells labelled platelet/erythrocyte/progenitor/unassigned (platelets: PPBP, PF4; progenitors: CD34; note HBB is not in the gene list) and state the denominator explicitly as all 11,693 query cells. IF FOUND: report each category as a share of all query cells and leave the residual as 'other'; map fine labels to the five categories only as MAIT, gamma-delta T, Treg -> T_cells; plasma cell -> B_cells; cycling NK -> NK_cells; pDC -> Dendritic_cells; platelet, erythrocyte, stem cell -> none. SOURCE: data headers plus https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/8692 (platelet clusters are routinely found in PBMC data).

label: Pitfall: forced assignment of cell types missing from the reference
text: PITFALL: Label transfer forces every query cell onto the nearest reference type, so cell types absent from the reference get a confident wrong label; the documented example is neutrophils (absent from a PBMC reference) being confidently annotated as CD14 monocytes with a high prediction score but a low mapping score. CHECK: do not rely on the prediction score alone; compute a how-well-is-this-cell-represented measure (Seurat MappingScore, or distance of each query cell to its reference neighbours in the shared embedding) and inspect markers of any query cluster with low mapping quality or very low gene counts (granulocytes: FCGR3B, CSF3R, CXCR2, S100A8 with few genes detected). IF FOUND: label such clusters 'other' rather than Monocytes or any of the five categories, and confirm every transferred label with canonical markers at cluster level. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/azimuth/issues/93 (Azimuth FAQ quoted) and https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.01.29.701618v2.full.pdf

label: Pitfall: cross-platform shift between HIVE reference and query
text: PITFALL: The reference is from the HIVE picowell platform (cell names carry HIVE ids) and the query platform is unstated; published platform comparisons report that cells cluster by technology as well as by cell type and that HIVE shows platform-specific gene signatures (higher ribosomal and mitochondrial fractions, better granulocyte retention), so a classifier or a joint PCA built without batch handling can separate reference from query instead of cell types. CHECK: compare total counts, genes detected, mito and ribo fractions between reference and query; build a joint embedding and see whether query cells mix with reference cells of the same marker-defined lineage; compare the result of two independent approaches (a classifier on normalised expression versus integration-based neighbour voting) and against reference-free marker annotation of query clusters. IF FOUND: use a transfer method that corrects for dataset and sample (reference PCA projection with anchors, Harmony or scVI/scANVI with sample as batch) on shared genes only, do not reuse the reference's stored X_pca for the query, and trust the broad lineage call only where the methods and the markers agree. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12539239/ and https://jbt.abrf.org/article/162768-multisite-assessment-of-methods-for-cell-preservation-upstream-of-single-cell-rna-sequencing

label: Pitfall: normalisation and gene-set mismatch between reference and query
text: PITFALL: Classifier-based annotation silently degrades when reference and query are not normalised identically; CellTypist, for example, stores per-gene mean and sd from training data and requires log1p of counts normalised to 10,000 per cell on all genes, and gives inaccurate predictions on scaled, SCT/Pearson-residual or highly-variable-gene-subset input. Both files here hold raw integer counts in X, and the query has 5,044 genes the reference lacks. CHECK: confirm X is integer counts in both objects, subset both to the 22,902 shared genes before normalising, apply the same normalisation to both, and verify the maximum of the log matrix is plausible (below about 10). IF FOUND: train the model on the reference normalised exactly as the query will be, and never feed scaled or HVG-only matrices to a model trained on full log-normalised data. SOURCE: https://www.celltypist.org/tutorials/onlineguide and https://github.com/Teichlab/celltypist/issues/138

label: Pitfall: NK versus cytotoxic T cell confusion
text: PITFALL: NK cells and cytotoxic T cells (effector-memory CD8, gamma-delta T, MAIT) share the cytotoxic programme (NKG7, GNLY, GZMB, PRF1, KLRD1, CST7), and some CD8 TEM and gamma-delta T cells are KLRF1-positive, so label transfer moves cells between NK_cells and T_cells in either direction; NK cells also express CD3E, so CD3E alone does not prove T identity. CHECK: within cells called NK, look for CD3D, CD3G, TRAC, CD8A/CD8B, TRDC with TRGC1/TRGC2; within cells called cytotoxic CD8/gamma-delta/MAIT, look for CD3D/CD3G-negative cells with KLRF1, NCAM1, FCGR3A, TYROBP, FCER1G; sub-cluster the cytotoxic lymphocyte compartment on its own and check MKI67-positive 'cycling NK' calls for CD3D. IF FOUND: reassign at sub-cluster level using CD3D/CD3G/TRAC/TRDC (T) versus their absence plus KLRF1/NCAM1 (NK), and report how much the NK and T percentages move. SOURCE: https://apps.allenimmunology.org/aifi/resources/imm-health-atlas/cell-type-descriptions/cd8-t-cells-gdt-cells-and-mait-cells/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10768068/

label: sc30 data header facts
text: DATA HEADER FACTS (library read the header only, no analysis): the .h5ad at /scbench-data/157798549.node has X as a dense int64 matrix of 6420 cells x 19973 genes (about 1 GB in memory), one sample category '4T1_viable', obs columns only 'sample' and a pre-existing 'n_genes', an empty var table, mouse gene symbols from an older annotation (many 'RP23-...' clone names), a 'Kate2' reporter transgene in var_names, and NO var_names starting with 'mt-' or 'MT-' (no mt-Co1, mt-Nd1, mt-Cytb etc. under any spelling).

label: Pitfall: dendritic cells versus monocytes and pDC misassignment
text: PITFALL: Dendritic cells are a small share of PBMCs and overlap transcriptionally with monocytes (cDC2 and CD14-positive DC3 versus classical monocytes), while pDCs carry GZMB and can be pulled toward B/plasma or NK labels; because the true DC share is small, a few dozen misassigned cells change the Dendritic_cells percentage by a large relative amount. CHECK: sub-cluster the myeloid compartment and score monocyte markers (CD14, S100A8/S100A9, VCAN, C5AR1 = CD88, FCAR = CD89, FCGR3A for non-classical) against cDC markers (FCER1A, CD1C, CLEC10A, HLA-DQA1; CLEC9A, XCR1 for cDC1) and pDC markers (CLEC4C, LILRA4, IL3RA, TCF4); count how many cells each method calls DC or pDC and whether they form coherent sub-clusters. IF FOUND: assign DC versus monocyte at sub-cluster level from these markers rather than from coarse clusters or raw per-cell votes, and report the DC percentage with the count behind it. SOURCE: https://www.cell.com/immunity/fulltext/S1074-7613(19)30334-6 and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5775029/

label: PITFALL no mitochondrial genes in matrix
text: PITFALL: The standard mitochondrial-percent QC filter cannot be computed here because the matrix appears to contain no mitochondrial-genome genes; a case-insensitive '^mt' pattern instead matches about 68 nuclear genes (Mt1, Mt2, Mtor, Mthfd2, Mtch1...) and yields a meaningless 'mito %' that would remove healthy cells (metallothionein-high tumor cells). CHECK: count var_names that start exactly with 'mt-' (mouse) and confirm the hits are the 13 mt-encoded protein genes (mt-Nd1..6, mt-Co1..3, mt-Atp6/8, mt-Cytb); if the count is 0, print the genes any looser pattern matches. IF FOUND: do not apply any mitochondrial filter and do not substitute nuclear Mt*/Mrp* genes; base QC only on total counts and genes detected, and say so. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/639 ; https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/1919 ; https://github.com/czbiohub-sf/tabula-muris/issues/221

label: PITFALL low-RNA neutrophils removed by default thresholds
text: PITFALL: Textbook lower cut-offs (min_genes=200, min_counts=500, nFeature>200) delete real low-RNA cell types; neutrophils express only a few hundred genes and look like background, and tumors such as 4T1 are heavily neutrophil-infiltrated, so a default threshold can remove a whole population rather than 'clearly low-quality' cells. CHECK: plot log10 total counts and log10 genes detected as histograms and look for a distinct low mode; for the cells below each candidate threshold, test whether they coherently express neutrophil/immune markers (S100a8, S100a9, Retnlg, Csf3r, Cxcr2, Il1b, Ptprc) versus a diffuse ambient-like mix. IF FOUND: place the lower threshold below that population (at the valley under it, or a very permissive floor such as the scanpy tutorial's min_genes=100) instead of 200/500, and count how many cells each choice removes. SOURCE: https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/tutorials/cr-tutorial-neutrophils ; https://www.cell.com/immunity/fulltext/S1074-7613(19)30126-8 ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

label: Pitfall: cluster-level labelling and majority voting hide rare or mixed populations
text: PITFALL: Assigning one label per coarse cluster (the query ships with 20 Seurat clusters at resolution 1), or using majority voting, erases rare populations that sit inside a larger cluster (DCs inside monocytes, pDC or plasma cells inside B cells, NK inside cytotoxic T), while pure per-cell labels are noisy from dropout; majority voting also depends on the clustering and latent space it is run on. CHECK: cross-tabulate per-cell predicted labels against clusters and flag any cluster where the top five-category label is below about 80-90 percent; compare the five percentages from per-cell labels against those from cluster-majority labels. IF FOUND: over-cluster or sub-cluster the mixed clusters and vote within the sub-clusters, validated by markers; if per-cell and cluster-level percentages differ materially for a category, the difference is the uncertainty to report. SOURCE: https://www.celltypist.org/faq and https://www.sc-best-practices.org/cellular_structure/annotation.html and https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.basic/cell-type-annotation.html

label: PITFALL data may be pre-filtered, stale n_genes
text: PITFALL: The object may already have been cell-filtered upstream (obs carries an 'n_genes' column, which is what sc.pp.filter_cells writes, and the sample is labelled 'viable'), so re-applying a default threshold may remove nothing or remove cells for no reason, and the stored n_genes may be stale. CHECK: recompute genes detected and total counts from X, compare with obs['n_genes'], and look at the minimum of each for a hard floor (e.g. every cell >= some round number of genes or UMIs). IF FOUND: treat the floor as the already-applied filter, do not report an unchanged count as if QC was done without saying so, and justify any further removal only by a clearly separated low-quality tail in the recomputed metrics. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.filter_cells.html ; https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/common-considerations-for-quality-control-filters-for-single-cell-rna-seq-data

label: Pitfall: reference class imbalance under-calls rare cell types
text: PITFALL: The composition of the reference biases label transfer: a PBMC benchmark of five label-transfer methods found that the number of reference cells per type changes results and that the reference design must fit the method, and rare types (DC, pDC, plasma, cycling NK) are an imbalanced classification problem that neighbour-voting and unweighted classifiers under-call in favour of abundant T cells and monocytes. CHECK: tabulate reference cells per label; rerun the transfer with a class-balanced reference (down-sample each type to a cap, or class_weight='balanced') and compare the five percentages with the full-reference run. IF FOUND: prefer the balanced or stratified reference (it also makes the 118,685-cell reference tractable), keep all reference samples represented, and treat categories that move between runs as uncertain. SOURCE: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/bioinformatics/articles/10.3389/fbinf.2023.1150099/full and https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12859-021-04469-x

label: PITFALL MAD outliers on multimodal tumor data
text: PITFALL: MAD-based outlier thresholds assume one roughly unimodal population in which most cells are good; a tumor sample mixes large RNA-rich carcinoma cells with small immune cells, so median +/- k MADs on a bimodal metric can cut off a real population, and 3 MADs (stringent) removes far more than the 5 MADs recommended for lenient filtering. CHECK: compute thresholds on log1p(total counts) and log1p(genes) and report, per metric and per tail, how many cells are flagged at 3 and at 5 MADs and whether the lower bound even falls inside the data range; inspect the histograms for multimodality. IF FOUND: use the lenient 5-MAD rule on the log scale (or a fixed cut at a visible valley), not 3 MADs, and do not accept an automatic threshold that slices through a mode. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://bioconductor.org/books/3.24/OSCA.basic/quality-control.html ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9912498/

label: Pitfall: doublets and platelet aggregates distort composition
text: PITFALL: Heterotypic doublets and cell-cell complexes (T cell-monocyte, B-T, platelet-leukocyte aggregates) survive standard filtering in blood data, form their own clusters with mixed-lineage expression, and are forced into one lineage by label transfer; doublet callers miss a sizeable fraction and removing cells changes the denominator of every percentage. CHECK: run a doublet caller per sample (Scrublet or scDblFinder), and look for clusters with high total counts co-expressing CD3D with LYZ/CD14, MS4A1/CD79A with CD3D, or PPBP/PF4 with a leukocyte lineage. IF FOUND: do not silently drop cells; compute the five percentages both with the suspect cells kept in the denominator as 'other' and with them removed, state which is reported, and prefer keeping the denominator at all supplied query cells since the query is already QC-filtered. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9204188/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7666012/ and https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12574873/

label: PITFALL upper thresholds remove tumor cells
text: PITFALL: An upper cut-off on counts or genes (max_genes=2500/5000/7000, upper MAD tail) is a doublet heuristic, not a low-quality filter, and in tumors it removes genuine large, RNA-rich malignant cells; the task asks to remove only clearly low-quality cells. CHECK: for cells above any candidate upper cut-off, test whether they are single-lineage tumor cells (Epcam, Krt8, Krt18, Kate2 positive, Ptprc negative) or co-express mutually exclusive lineage markers; count how many cells the upper cut-off alone removes. IF FOUND to be real cells: apply no upper threshold (or only one above an isolated extreme tail) and leave doublets to a dedicated tool such as Scrublet rather than folding them into the QC count. SOURCE: https://www.10xgenomics.com/analysis-guides/common-considerations-for-quality-control-filters-for-single-cell-rna-seq-data ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

label: Pitfall: thresholding fine-label prediction scores
text: PITFALL: Prediction-score thresholds are not a validated filter: Seurat/Azimuth developers recommend no fixed cut-off, and a low score often only means the vote is split between two subtypes of the same lineage (e.g. CD4 central versus effector memory), so discarding or relabelling low-score cells as 'unknown' removes real T cells and distorts the five broad percentages. CHECK: sum prediction probabilities across fine labels within each of the five broad categories before judging confidence; look at the score distribution per predicted type and at which broad category the low-score cells fall into. IF FOUND: score confidence at the broad five-category level, keep cells whose ambiguity is within one category, and reserve 'other' for cells that are ambiguous between categories or poorly represented by the reference. SOURCE: https://github.com/satijalab/seurat/issues/5513 and https://github.com/satijalab/azimuth/issues/93 and https://github.com/satijalab/azimuth/issues/86

label: PITFALL complexity filters flag neutrophils
text: PITFALL: Extra 'complexity' criteria copied from pipelines (outliers in pct_counts_in_top_20_genes, log10GenesPerUMI > 0.8, ribosomal or hemoglobin percent cut-offs) flag specialised cells whose transcriptome is dominated by a few genes, such as neutrophils (S100a8/S100a9), and so quietly turn a conservative filter into an aggressive one. CHECK: for each criterion separately, count the cells it flags and look at which genes dominate them and which lineage markers they express. IF FOUND that flagged cells are a coherent cell type: drop that criterion; keep only criteria whose flagged cells look broken (very few counts AND very few genes with no lineage identity). SOURCE: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-022-02820-w ; https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/

label: PITFALL univariate union over-filters
text: PITFALL: Thresholding each QC metric separately and taking the union removes more cells than intended; guidance is to consider count depth and genes detected jointly, be as permissive as possible, and revisit only if downstream clusters are uninterpretable. CHECK: scatter total counts against genes detected (log axes), and tabulate cells failing each criterion alone, their union, and their intersection; report the fraction removed. IF FOUND that the union removes much more than the visibly detached low tail: tighten to the joint low-count-and-low-gene corner and prefer the smaller removal. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

label: PITFALL diagnose cell-type loss in discarded pool
text: PITFALL: QC metrics are not independent of biology, so a threshold can silently discard a cell type and the remaining data still look clean. CHECK: after choosing thresholds, compare mean expression of the discarded pool against the retained pool (log fold change per gene) and list the genes most enriched in the discarded cells. IF FOUND that those genes are lineage markers (e.g. neutrophil, T cell, erythroid genes) rather than a diffuse ambient/damage signature: the filter is removing a population, so relax the threshold until the discarded pool has no cell-type identity. SOURCE: https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.advanced/quality-control-redux.html

label: PITFALL filter_cells boundary and ordering
text: PITFALL: The reported integer depends on boundary and ordering details: sc.pp.filter_cells(min_genes=k) keeps cells with n_genes >= k (inclusive) and accepts only one of min_counts/min_genes/max_counts/max_genes per call, and running sc.pp.filter_genes(min_cells=3) before computing per-cell metrics lowers n_genes and can push boundary cells out. CHECK: compute per-cell metrics on the full raw integer matrix first (confirm X holds raw counts), apply cell filters, then report adata.n_obs; test whether the count changes with < versus <= at the threshold. IF FOUND sensitive: state the inclusive convention used and report the cell count from cell filtering only, since gene filtering does not change the number of cells. SOURCE: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.filter_cells.html

label: sc32 data and model header facts
text: DATA FACTS (from file headers only, no analysis): 158618536.node is an AnnData h5ad with 100,000 cells x 40,352 genes (gene symbols, plus ENSG-style names for unnamed genes); X is a sparse CSR of RAW INTEGER COUNTS (float32 dtype), with no layers, no .raw, no obsm and no neighbour graph; obs has donor (12 donors), cytokine (91 categories), treatment (PBS vs cytokine), sample (1092 donor_cytokine combos), split-pool barcode wells (bc1/bc2/bc3, i.e. Parse-style combinatorial barcoding) and QC columns gene_count, tscp_count, pct_counts_MT. 158562712.node is a 55 KB CellTypist-format pickle (dict with keys Model = sklearn LogisticRegression one-vs-rest, Scaler_ = StandardScaler, description), pickled with scikit-learn 1.7.2 and numpy>=2 (numpy._core paths); it has 7 classes: 'B cell', 'DC', 'ILC', 'Monocyte', 'NK cell', 'Progenitor cell', 'T cell', and 888 feature genes, all 888 of which are present in the dataset's var names.

label: PITFALL raw counts must be log1p CP10k for CellTypist
text: PITFALL: The data X holds raw integer counts, but a CellTypist model stores per-gene mean/sd learned on log1p(counts normalised to 10,000 per cell) and re-applies them to the query, so feeding raw counts, a different target sum (median/1e6), SCT/Pearson residuals or z-scored data gives wrong scores or an 'Invalid expression matrix' / '.raw' error. CHECK: confirm X is integer before normalising, then after sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4); sc.pp.log1p(adata) verify np.expm1(adata.X[:10]).sum(axis=1) is 10000 for every row. IF FOUND: normalise exactly once to 1e4 then log1p on ALL 40,352 genes (never normalise twice, never sc.pp.scale before prediction, never normalise after subsetting genes). SOURCE: https://github.com/Teichlab/celltypist/issues/138 ; https://github.com/Teichlab/celltypist/issues/89 ; https://github.com/teichlab/celltypist

label: PITFALL model has ILC class absent from answer schema
text: PITFALL: The pretrained model has 7 classes including 'ILC', but the required answer has only 6 fields (T, monocyte, B, NK, DC, progenitor) that must sum to 100, so any cells predicted 'ILC' make the six percentages sum to less than 100 unless a rule is chosen, and the choice (fold ILC into NK vs drop ILC cells and renormalise vs leave) changes the numbers. CHECK: count cells labelled 'ILC' under both per-cell predicted_labels and majority_voting; compute the six percentages under each rule and see how far each field moves; also check the six rounded values sum to exactly 100.0. IF FOUND: if ILC count is zero the issue vanishes; if non-zero, state the rule explicitly - NK cells are group-1 innate lymphoid cells and CellTypist's own immune hierarchy files 'NK cells' under the high-level label 'ILC', so merging ILC into NK is the lineage-consistent option, while renormalising over the six named classes is the alternative; report both if they differ by >0.1 point. SOURCE: https://www.celltypist.org/encyclopedia/Immune/v2/?celltype=NK+cells ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41590-024-01885-y

label: PITFALL predicted_labels vs majority_voting change rare-type proportions
text: PITFALL: CellTypist returns two different label columns - per-cell 'predicted_labels' (deterministic, depends only on expression) and 'majority_voting' (each Leiden over-cluster takes its dominant label) - and their proportions differ, mostly for rare classes (DC, Progenitor cell, ILC), which get absorbed into the dominant neighbour label; majority voting also depends on the neighbour graph, Leiden version/seed and resolution (default 25 for 100k-200k cells; the graph is built by CellTypist if absent, as here), so it is not reproducible across environments and is memory-heavy on 100k cells. CHECK: run both, cross-tabulate predicted_labels vs majority_voting, and compare the six percentages; look at which rare classes shrink or vanish under voting. IF FOUND: if the two differ by more than ~0.5 point in any field, say which one is reported and why; per-cell labels are the direct output of the provided model, majority voting is CellTypist's optional refinement - do not mix the two, and never compute proportions from a custom coarse clustering instead of the model's labels without saying so. SOURCE: https://celltypist.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notebook/celltypist_tutorial.html ; https://celltypist.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/celltypist/classifier.html ; https://github.com/Teichlab/celltypist/issues/119

label: PITFALL gene filtering before prediction drops model features
text: PITFALL: CellTypist silently uses only the genes shared between query and model, so any gene filtering or renaming before prediction (HVG subset, min_cells filter, dropping MT/ribosomal/lncRNA or ENSG-named genes, symbol conversion) removes model features and changes scores without an error; here all 888 model features exist in the raw var names, including ENSG-style names, so nothing needs converting. CHECK: confirm len(set(model features) & set(adata.var_names)) == 888 at the moment of prediction, var_names are unique, and the CellTypist log says '888 features used for prediction'. IF FOUND: if fewer than 888 are used, undo the gene filter/rename and predict from the full 40,352-gene, CP10k-log1p matrix; do any HVG selection only on a copy used for clustering/UMAP. SOURCE: https://github.com/teichlab/celltypist ; https://github.com/Teichlab/celltypist/issues/145

label: PITFALL sklearn/numpy version mismatch and manual CellTypist reimplementation
text: PITFALL: The model pickle was written with scikit-learn 1.7.2 and numpy>=2, so loading it elsewhere can fail (ModuleNotFoundError numpy._core on old numpy; missing/removed multi_class attribute across sklearn versions) or emit InconsistentVersionWarning, and if celltypist is not installed analysts may reimplement prediction wrongly (using sklearn predict_proba/softmax, forgetting the scaler, wrong gene order, or no clipping). CHECK: record sklearn/numpy versions and any unpickle warning; reproduce CellTypist's exact pipeline manually - take the CP10k-log1p matrix restricted to the model's 888 features IN THE MODEL'S ORDER, compute (X - Scaler_.mean_) / Scaler_.scale_, set values > 10 to 10, scores = Xs @ coef_.T + intercept_ (shape cells x 7), label = classes_[argmax(scores)], probability = sigmoid(scores) - and confirm it matches the tool's labels on a sample of cells. IF FOUND: if the library path errors or disagrees, use the manual linear-algebra path (it is version-independent); densify only the 100,000 x 888 feature block, never the full 100,000 x 40,352 matrix. SOURCE: https://github.com/Teichlab/celltypist/issues/29 ; https://celltypist.readthedocs.io/en/stable/_modules/celltypist/models.html ; https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.exceptions.InconsistentVersionWarning.html ; https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/28703

label: NK clonal involvement is biologically real
text: PITFALL: Treating NK involvement in the MDS clone as implausible and over-filtering until no sample passes; published single-cell work shows NK cells from MDS/CCUS patients often share the myeloid driver genotype (e.g. TET2, DNMT3A; NK cells and MDS clones from the same patient share TET2 mutations), so a result of zero samples is not a safe default, and neither is all samples. CHECK: for each sample, report NK mutant fraction for each candidate somatic driver variant next to the myelomonocytic fraction (should be high) and the T-cell fraction; true NK participation shows NK fraction between T-cell background and myeloid level, driven by the same variant that dominates myeloid cells. IF FOUND: count a sample only when the NK signal comes from a variant that is clearly clonal in myelomonocytic cells and NK exceeds the 1.0% threshold with >=2-3 cells; give a sensitivity table (raw vs quality-filtered vs germline-excluded) so the director can see which choice moves the count. SOURCE: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-023-36193-w ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-58662-0

label: Tapestri filter flag semantics
text: The Mosaic data-structure docs state that ca/filtered, ra/filtered and layers/FILTER_MASK in a Tapestri h5 are computed from metadata cutoffs (af_cutoff, dp_cutoff, gq_cutoff, missing_cells_cutoff, missing_variants_cutoff, mutated_cells_cutoff) and do not remove anything; their 0/1 polarity is not documented there, and in GSE276492 sample S7 the first CSF3R variants have ca/filtered=1, so analysts must empirically test polarity (e.g. cross-tab FILTER_MASK against DP<10/GQ<30) before using these flags. Source: https://missionbio.github.io/mosaic/v2.4.1/4_data_structure.html

label: QC filtering shifts composition
text: PITFALL: Cell-level QC filtering (min genes/counts, max pct_counts_MT, max counts) changes the denominator and is cell-type biased: count caps remove mostly monocytes (high RNA content), while min-gene and MT cutoffs preferentially remove small/low-RNA cells and rare types, so the same model gives different percentages depending on the filter. CHECK: inspect distributions of gene_count, tscp_count and pct_counts_MT in obs to see whether the data are already filtered (e.g. a hard floor on gene_count); compute the six percentages on all 100,000 cells and after any proposed filter, and tabulate which predicted labels the filter removes. IF FOUND: if data appear pre-filtered, annotate all cells without extra filtering (the task gives no QC instructions); if you filter, use lenient MAD-based thresholds, report the number of cells removed per label and the unfiltered percentages alongside. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://docs.nygen.io/CyteArc/tutorials/quality-control/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13059-023-02859-3

label: doublet removal choice
text: PITFALL: Doublets/multiplets (also present in split-pool combinatorial barcoding like Parse) get forced into one of the 7 classes, and doublet removal is optional and tool/seed-dependent (scDblFinder/Scrublet should be run per sample, not on aggregated multi-batch data), so removing them shifts proportions in a non-reproducible way. CHECK: only if considering removal - run doublet detection per sample/well-group, report the predicted doublet rate and the per-label breakdown of flagged cells, and compare the six percentages with and without removal. IF FOUND: for a coarse-proportion answer from a provided model, default to no doublet removal (keeps the answer reproducible); if removal moves any field by >0.5 point, report both versions and state which is submitted. SOURCE: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11374959/

label: cytokine stimulation and pooling
text: PITFALL: The dataset pools 12 donors x 91 cytokine/PBS conditions (1092 samples); cytokine stimulation alters transcriptional state (e.g. IFN-induced genes, activated monocytes/DC, proliferating lymphocytes) and in vitro culture shifts composition, so a reference model trained on resting cells may misassign stimulated cells (e.g. activated monocytes as DC, proliferating cells as 'Progenitor cell'), and the overall percentage depends on whether one pools cells or averages per sample. CHECK: tabulate predicted-label percentages by treatment (PBS vs cytokine) and by cytokine; flag cytokines where DC or Progenitor fractions jump far above PBS levels and check canonical markers (CD34 for progenitors, FCER1A/CLEC10A/CD1C for DC, CD14/LYZ for monocytes) in those cells. IF FOUND: the requested answer is the pooled cell-level percentage over all cells (do not reweight by sample or donor); report outliers as caveats, but do not override model labels with manual relabelling unless explicitly stated. SOURCE: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33627475/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326076/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13073-026-01721-y

label: rounding to sum 100
text: PITFALL: Rounding six percentages independently to 1 decimal often makes them sum to 99.9 or 100.1, failing the 'sum to 100' requirement. CHECK: after computing counts/total*100 for the six fields (with the chosen ILC rule), round and sum. IF FOUND: apply largest-remainder rounding (adjust the field with the largest rounding remainder by 0.1) so the sum is exactly 100.0, and note the adjustment. SOURCE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Largest_remainder_method

label: bc1 well = sample; position nested in treatment
text: PITFALL: In split-pool (ParseBio/SPLiT-seq) data the round-1 well (bc1_well) is the sample barcode, so each treatment (cytokine, often x donor) occupies its own fixed wells; position and treatment are then confounded/nested by design, and a 'position effect' cannot be separated from a treatment effect by any normalization. CHECK: crosstab cytokine x bc1_well (and donor x bc1_well); count how many distinct wells each cytokine uses and whether any well holds >1 cytokine; compute Cramer's V or chi-square on edge/center x treatment. IF FOUND: report confounding explicitly; treat confounding as a fact about design, then judge whether the position effect is large enough to matter rather than claiming correction can fix it. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11011421/ ; https://doi.org/10.1002/bimj.202200284

label: Judge edge effect by R2/effect size, not p
text: PITFALL: Confounded does not automatically mean correction is warranted; the decision hinges on effect size of position on cell counts. A statistically significant p-value with huge n (cells) is meaningless. CHECK: aggregate to one row per bc1_well (cells per well), define edge (row A/H or col 1/12 of 96-well plate) vs interior, fit cells_per_well ~ edge (and ~ row + col), report R-squared and the edge-vs-center % difference. IF FOUND: if R-squared is tiny (e.g. <0.02) and edge/center difference small, edge normalization is not warranted; if large (e.g. R2>0.3 or consistent ~>20-35% lower recovery at edges) it is. SOURCE: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8024881/ ; https://www.agilent.com/cs/library/technicaloverviews/public/te-evaluation-of-edge-effect-cell-analysis-5994-4697en-agilent.pdf

label: Use wells, not cells, as unit
text: PITFALL: Running the position-effect test at the cell level (each cell as an observation, e.g. regressing a per-cell variable or chi-square on millions of cells) is pseudoreplication and inflates significance; the experimental unit for cell recovery is the well. label: Verify X is raw integer counts
text: PITFALL: The file stores X as float32 CSR (966768 nuclei x 32227 genes, 172M stored values) with no layers and no .raw, so X is the only candidate raw matrix and it may already be normalized or logged; normalizing an already-normalized matrix gives silently wrong means. CHECK: confirm X.data are all non-negative and integer-valued (np.all(data==np.round(data))) and inspect max values, on a chunk and ideally all of data. IF FOUND non-integers: X is not raw UMI counts; do not CP10K/log1p it again, report the discrepancy to the director instead of guessing. SOURCE: https://discourse.scverse.org/t/does-scanpy-stores-raw-count-as-int-or-float/2177

label: Recompute QC, do not trust obs columns
text: PITFALL: obs already contains total_counts, n_genes and n_genes_raw columns, and the two n_genes columns can differ (e.g. computed before/after gene filtering), so filtering on a precomputed column can keep a different nuclei set than the task's definition. CHECK: recompute total_umi = row sums of X and n_genes = count of entries > 0 per row directly from X, and compare against obs columns (count mismatches). IF FOUND mismatch: use the recomputed values for the n_genes > 1000 filter (strictly greater than) and report how many nuclei differ. SOURCE: https://github.com/theislab/scanpy/issues/1434

label: CP10K target_sum and size factor
text: PITFALL: scanpy normalize_total defaults to target_sum=None (median depth, not 10000) and offers exclude_highly_expressed; either changes the CP10K values. Also the size factor must be total UMIs over ALL genes including mito genes. CHECK: verify after normalization that each kept row sums to 10000 (within float error). IF FOUND otherwise: normalize manually as counts / total_umi * 1e4 with total_umi from all genes, target_sum=1e4 explicit, exclude_highly_expressed=False. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/scanpy.pp.normalize_total.html

label: Mean of log1p over all kept nuclei incl zeros
text: PITFALL: The requested value is the mean of log1p(CP10K) over all kept nuclei, including the nuclei where the gene is zero; computing the mean over sparse stored values only, or log1p of the mean CP10K, or expm1 back, gives different numbers (mean of logs != log of mean). CHECK: compute sum over kept nuclei of log1p(cp10k) divided by the number of kept nuclei (both age groups pooled), using natural log (np.log1p), not log2. IF FOUND a different formula in your code: switch to this one. SOURCE: https://github.com/scverse/scanpy/issues/1364

label: Use float64 accumulation
text: PITFALL: With ~1M nuclei, accumulating sums or means in float32 (X is float32) can lose precision noticeably, especially for row totals and column means. CHECK: cast to float64 before summing totals, dividing, log1p and averaging (np.sum(..., dtype=np.float64)); compare with a float32 run on one gene. IF FOUND differences beyond ~1e-6: report the float64 results. SOURCE: https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/9393

label: Explicit zeros in sparse n_genes
text: PITFALL: Sparse matrices can store explicit zeros, so n_genes computed as nnz per row (indptr diff) over-counts genes detected and can let extra nuclei pass the n_genes > 1000 filter. CHECK: count (X.data == 0).sum(); compute n_genes as the number of entries with value > 0 per row. IF FOUND explicit zeros: use the >0 count (or eliminate_zeros first). SOURCE: https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.sparse.csr_matrix.nnz.html

label: Exact gene-symbol matching
text: PITFALL: Gene lookup errors (case-insensitive matching, fuzzy/alias matching, or Ensembl IDs) can return the wrong gene or a false 0.0. In this file var_names are unique mouse symbols (e.g. Xkr4, mt-Nd1) and 13 mito genes start with 'mt-'. CHECK: match each of Ednrb, Edn1, Gja1, Fabp7, Pecam1, Isl1 by exact, case-sensitive string against var_names and print which are found. IF FOUND absent: use 0.0 only for genes truly absent by exact match; do not substitute case variants or aliases. SOURCE: https://anndata.scverse.org/en/latest/generated/anndata.AnnData.var_names_make_unique.html

label: Memory: chunked processing, no subsampling
text: PITFALL: The matrix (~1.45 GB file, 172M nonzeros, 966768 x 32227) is too big to densify, and full in-memory scanpy pipelines may crash or tempt shortcuts like subsampling, which changes the answer. CHECK: plan memory before loading; never call .toarray() on full X. IF FOUND memory pressure: stream rows with h5py over X/indptr chunks (compute row totals, n_genes, and per-target-gene sums of log1p(cp10k) in one pass) or use anndata backed='r'; never subsample. SOURCE: https://anndata.scverse.org/en/stable/generated/anndata.io.read_h5ad.html

label: No extra QC filters beyond n_genes>1000
text: PITFALL: Standard scanpy tutorials add extra QC steps (pct_mito cutoffs, min_cells gene filtering, doublet removal, highly variable gene subsetting) that the task does not ask for; pct_mito is to be computed but NOT used for filtering, and applying any of these changes the kept nuclei or genes and therefore the means. CHECK: confirm the only cell filter is n_genes > 1000 and no gene filter is applied before normalization; log number of kept nuclei. IF FOUND extra filters: remove them. SOURCE: https://scanpy.scverse.org/en/stable/tutorials/basics/clustering.html

reason: The choice of HVG flavor and its input is the single largest unstated decision in the task and directly determines the third reported number; the team needs to make it deliberately, avoid the silent flavor/input mismatch, and record the alternative.
text: PITFALL: the 'median number of cells in which the 2,000 HVGs are detected' depends strongly on the HVG method, and the task names no flavor. Methods select very different gene sets, and flavor must match input scale: scanpy's default flavor='seurat' (and 'cell_ranger') expects log-normalised data and applies expm1 internally, so calling it directly on raw counts silently gives a meaningless ranking; 'seurat_v3' expects raw integer counts and only warns if given normalised data. If a log-normalised route is used, the scale factor is a further hidden choice (normalize_total defaults to the median count per cell, Seurat/tutorials use 1e4), and on shallow data where depth is far below the scale factor this changes which genes rank as variable. CHECK: before the HVG call, assert whether the matrix passed is integer-valued and whether adata.uns has 'log1p', and that this matches the flavor. Compute the HVG set and its median prevalence under at least seurat_v3 on raw counts and flavor='seurat' on log-normalised data, and report the overlap and both medians. IF they differ materially: prefer the method that needs no unstated steps for the data as given (raw counts with a fixed n_top_genes=2000 corresponds to seurat_v3 / Seurat vst, which needs no scale factor), and state the flavor, the input, and the alternative value explicitly rather than hiding the assumption.

reason: A missing dependency or loess error commonly leads to a quiet fallback to another flavor or a changed span, which changes the HVG set and therefore the reported prevalence without anyone noticing.
text: PITFALL: seurat_v3 HVG selection can fail or get silently swapped. It needs the optional scikit-misc package (loess), and the loess fit can raise 'reciprocal condition number' / 'near singularities' errors, attributed to an excess of all-zero genes in the cells being fitted, most often when batch_key is used. CHECK: try 'import skmisc' before the run and make sure the min-cells gene filter was applied first. IF it fails: install scikit-misc (pip install scikit-misc) rather than falling back to the default dispersion flavor; remove all-zero genes for the failing subset rather than altering span; if a different flavor or span is truly unavoidable, report it as a deviation.

reason: Which matrix each statistic is computed on, and whether any unrequested cell QC is applied, changes all three reported values; the team should decide this explicitly and check sensitivity.
text: PITFALL: the three requested numbers can end up computed on different matrices, and habitual extra QC shifts all of them. The task states the gene filter (<10 cells) as a step before HVG selection, while median UMIs per cell and the percent of non-zero entries equal to 1 are worded as dataset-level statistics. Computing those two after gene filtering removes rare-gene entries (disproportionately counts of 1) and lowers cell totals. Cell filtering (min_genes, mito/MAD thresholds, doublet removal) is not requested and would change the median, the percentage and every gene's detection count. CHECK: compute median UMIs/cell and pct-equal-1 both on the unfiltered matrix and after the gene filter and see whether they differ at the reported precision; assert the number of cells is unchanged at the end. IF they differ: report the unfiltered-matrix value for the two dataset-level statistics as primary, note the post-filter value, and apply no cell filtering.

reason: An off-by-one or wrong-kind filter changes the gene universe the HVG ranking is fitted on, and taking prevalence from the wrong matrix or a stale column changes the third reported number.
text: PITFALL: gene-filter threshold semantics are easy to get wrong by one or by kind. 'Filter genes detected in fewer than 10 cells' means keep genes with n_cells >= 10: sc.pp.filter_genes(min_cells=10) is inclusive and correct, whereas min_counts=10 thresholds total UMIs instead, and a strict '> 10' drops genes detected in exactly 10 cells. The filter must run BEFORE HVG selection because the mean-variance trend (seurat_v3 loess) and the dispersion bins are fitted over all genes present, so the gene universe changes the ranking. CHECK: after filtering, assert the minimum over genes of (X > 0).sum(axis=0) is >= 10 and count how many genes sit exactly at 10. Compute HVG prevalence from the raw count matrix (cells with count > 0), not from normalised or scaled values, and not from a stale var['n_cells'] column computed before later subsetting.

reason: The answer format demands integers and exactly 2,000 genes; a silently short/long HVG set or an unstated rounding of a .5 median changes the reported value.
text: PITFALL: the HVG set may not contain exactly 2,000 genes, and the final integers hide rounding choices. With dispersion-based flavors a mean-expression bin holding a single gene gets its normalised dispersion set to 1 and NaN dispersions can occur; with n_top_genes set, all mean/dispersion cutoffs are ignored. The median of 2,000 prevalence values is the mean of the two middle values and can end in .5, while the answer must be an int. CHECK: assert adata.var['highly_variable'].sum() == 2000; check for NaN in the ranking statistic; compute the median prevalence as a float and see whether it is fractional; confirm the median UMI is taken over per-cell sums of raw counts (axis=1). IF found: fix the selection so exactly 2000 genes are flagged; if the median is x.5, state the rounding rule used.

reason: Stored-entry counts are the natural shortcut for both the percentage and gene prevalence, and they are wrong if the sparse matrix holds explicit zeros or duplicates; the check is cheap and the percentage-vs-fraction scale affects the reported number.
text: PITFALL: counting non-zero entries with sparse .nnz / getnnz counts STORED values, including explicit zeros and un-summed duplicates, so both the denominator of 'percent of non-zero entries equal to 1' and per-gene detection counts can be inflated. CHECK: on X run (X.data == 0).sum(), X.has_canonical_format and (X.data < 0).sum(); compare X.nnz with X.count_nonzero(). IF any explicit zeros or duplicates exist: call X.sum_duplicates() and X.eliminate_zeros() first, define the percentage as 100 * (X.data == 1).sum() / (X.data != 0).sum(), and define detection as (X > 0) per gene. reason: Whether genes are scaled before PCA is the single choice that most directly changes pc1_top_abs_load, and the scanpy default (no scaling) is easy to take without noticing.
text: Scaling decision drives the PC1-loading diagnostic. scanpy's sc.pp.pca only zero-centres genes; it does NOT scale them to unit variance. On unscaled log-normalised data each gene is weighted by its variance, so one or a few very high-variance genes (often abundant lineage or secreted genes) can own PC1. The PC1 loading vector has unit norm, so max |loading| lies between 1/sqrt(n_genes) (fully spread; about 0.022 for 2000 genes) and 1.0 (a single gene). CHECK: run PCA with and without sc.pp.scale on the same gene set, print the top 10 genes by |PCs[:,0]| and see whether one gene's loading is several-fold larger than the next. IF one gene dominates: z-score the selected genes (sc.pp.scale with max_value=10) or use Pearson residuals before PCA. Counter-view to weigh: standardisation also down-weights genuinely informative high-variance genes and up-weights noisy ones, and there is no community consensus, so decide from the diagnostic on this dataset and say which choice you made and why, rather than scaling or not scaling out of habit.

Running PCA on all ~20k genes of log1p(CP10k) data lets abundant and noisy genes set the axes; on log-normalised UMI data PC1 then tends to track the per-cell fraction of zeros and log total UMI (reported in the literature on negative-control data). reason: The choice between cell-level and pseudobulk testing changes the DEG count by orders of magnitude; this is the single largest method decision.
text: Unit of replication: do not test individual cells as replicates (scanpy rank_genes_groups Wilcoxon/t-test, Seurat FindMarkers). Cells from one donor are not independent; cell-level tests give tiny p-values and a DEG count inflated by hundreds to thousands that grows with cell number, not donor number. Instead sum the raw counts of CD14 Mono cells per donor per condition into pseudobulk samples (at most 12 IFN-beta + 12 PBS columns) and test with a bulk negative-binomial method (DESeq2/PyDESeq2 or edgeR). text: Gene filter ('at least 10 total counts across all samples'): the set of genes tested changes the BH-adjusted p-values and so the DEG count. Build the pseudobulk matrix first (retained donors x {IFN-beta, PBS}, CD14 Mono only, i.e. after donor exclusion), then keep genes whose row sum across those pseudobulk columns is >= 10, and apply this before dispersion estimation, not after testing. Common mistakes: summing over all 100k cells or all cell types; filtering before donor exclusion; using var['n_cells'] (it comes from the full 10M atlas); or using a per-sample rule such as edgeR filterByExpr or 'count >= 10 in >= n samples' instead of a row-sum rule. reason: The paired and unpaired designs give different DEG counts and the task does not say which was intended; the team must make this choice deliberately and document it.
text: Design formula: every donor contributes both an IFN-beta and a PBS pseudobulk (paired/blocked design). Fitting '~condition' alone leaves donor baseline variation in the dispersion, which inflates standard errors and changes how many genes pass padj<0.05 (it lowers power rather than raising false positives; one simulation found ~68% of true DEGs detected paired vs ~23% unpaired in DESeq2). The statistically correct model for paired data is '~ donor + condition' with the condition term last and the contrast IFN-beta vs PBS. However, the task text does not mention pairing, so it may have been scored with the simpler '~condition' design. Confirm each retained donor has exactly one pseudobulk per condition, run both designs, record both DEG counts and how far apart they are, and state clearly which design the reported number uses and why.

reason: Leftover categorical levels and implicit contrasts are easy silent errors in PyDESeq2 that would produce a wrong coefficient and a wrong count; the ISG sign check lets the team catch it.
text: Contrast and factor levels: after subsetting, the obs categoricals still carry 91 cytokine and 12 donor levels; unused levels or dropped donors can give a rank-deficient design or the wrong coefficient. Call remove_unused_categories() on donor and cytokine after subsetting. Reference levels default to alphabetical ('IFN-beta' sorts before 'PBS'), so request the contrast explicitly as ['cytokine','IFN-beta','PBS'] (numerator IFN-beta, denominator PBS). In a '~donor + condition' fit, make sure you extract the condition coefficient, not a donor coefficient; the design matrix should be full rank with n_donors + 1 columns. Some PyDESeq2 versions rewrite underscores in factor levels to hyphens, and the deprecated ref_level argument is ignored. Sanity check: canonical interferon-stimulated genes (ISG15, IFIT1, IFIT3, MX1, IFI44L, OAS1) should show large positive LFC and very small padj. The DEG count is symmetric in sign, but a wrong coefficient or rank-deficient design gives a completely different count.

reason: Shrunken vs unshrunken LFC and post-hoc filter vs threshold test each give a different DEG count; the team needs to know which reading matches the task wording.
text: Which log2FC and which test: the '|log2FC| > 1' count depends on the LFC used. Unshrunken maximum-likelihood LFCs are large and noisy for low-count genes (a 10-total-count filter keeps many such genes in small pseudobulks); apeglm/ashr-shrunken LFCs pull them toward 0 and give a different count. Separately, a threshold test (results(lfcThreshold=1) / lfc_null=1) is a different, much stricter procedure than the default Wald test of LFC=0 followed by a post-hoc |LFC|>1 filter. The task wording ('adjusted p-value < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| > 1.0') matches the conventional post-hoc filter on the default results table: padj<0.05 from the default LFC=0 Wald test plus unshrunken |LFC|>1. Use that for the reported number; shrunken-LFC and threshold-test counts are sensitivity figures only and must not be silently substituted. Shrinkage does not change padj.

reason: Independent filtering, Cook's handling and the alpha setting change which genes get a padj and therefore the count, and they behave differently under the two candidate designs.
text: padj NaN handling and filtering defaults: DESeq2/PyDESeq2 set padj to NA/NaN for genes removed by independent filtering (low mean count) and p-value to NA for Cook's-distance outliers. PyDESeq2 defaults are DeseqStats(alpha=0.05, cooks_filter=True, independent_filter=True) and DeseqDataSet(refit_cooks=True, min_replicates=7). These interact with the design: with '~condition' and >=7 donors per arm, outlier counts are replaced and refit; with '~donor + condition' there are no replicates per design cell, so outlier replacement does not occur. The independent-filter alpha should equal the padj cutoff, 0.05 (R's results() default is 0.1, so set it explicitly in R). NaN padj silently counts as not significant; make that explicit (e.g. fillna(1)). Keep package defaults with alpha=0.05 for the reported number; count genes with NaN pvalue/padj, and optionally re-run with independent_filter=False and cooks_filter=False to see how many DEGs these switches move.

reason: With very small pseudobulks the default normalization may fail or be driven by a handful of genes; the team needs to know what to check and what the fallback is, since it shifts LFCs around the |LFC|>1 cutoff.
text: Size factors: median-of-ratios normalization can be distorted here in two ways. (1) Sparse pseudobulks: with only ~5-30 cells per sample most genes have a zero in at least one sample, so median-of-ratios uses only the few genes non-zero in every sample, or fails with 'every gene contains at least one zero'. (2) IFN-beta shifts a large, mostly up-regulated block of genes, violating the assumption of balanced changes and biasing all LFCs, hence which genes cross |LFC|>1. Check how many genes have no zeros across the retained pseudobulks, compare the size factors with per-sample total counts and cell numbers, and check that the LFC histogram/MA plot mode sits at 0 for the bulk of genes. Keep default median-of-ratios for the headline number unless it fails outright; if the checks look bad, report it and run an alternative normalization (poscounts-type, library-size/TMM, or control genes restricted to stably expressed genes) as a sensitivity analysis.

reason: The task says kNN in PCA space among pericytes and all other types; building the graph on a subset or on a different representation gives a different number.
text: Build the kNN graph on ALL cells in PCA space, with the PCA fitted on all cells. Subsetting to pericytes (or pericytes plus CAFs) before PCA or kNN, building the graph on UMAP coordinates, or building it on the full gene matrix instead of the PCA embedding changes the neighbours entirely. If the file has no obsm['X_pca'] and you have not computed one, sc.pp.neighbors will silently compute its own PCA with defaults; n_pcs=None uses all stored PCs. Check: assert the embedding given to the neighbour search has shape (n_cells_total, n_pcs) and is the obsm['X_pca'] you computed, and that neighbour indices range over all cells. Use use_rep='X_pca' and state n_pcs.

reason: The choice between connectivities and the true directed kNN list changes the edge counts that go into both numerator and denominator of the ratio.
text: scanpy's obsp['connectivities'] is NOT the kNN graph: it is the UMAP fuzzy-union graph, symmetrised and weighted, with many more than k neighbours per cell. Counting its non-zeros or summing its weights as 'kNN edges' gives different cell-type fractions than the true directed kNN in obsp['distances'] (exactly k-1 non-zeros per row). Direction matters too: edges going OUT of pericytes (their own nearest neighbours) differ from edges coming IN from other cells, because abundant types pull in many incoming edges. Use the directed, unweighted neighbour lists of the pericyte cells (from obsp['distances'] or sklearn NearestNeighbors indices) as the primary definition of 'kNN edges of pericyte-labeled cells'; check that each pericyte row has exactly k-1 neighbours. Treat the symmetrised/weighted variant only as a sensitivity check and flag it if the ratio changes materially.

reason: Mixing scanpy and sklearn conventions gives k versus k-1 real neighbours, which shifts the cross-type counts; knowing the ratio is invariant to the fraction denominator saves the team from debating that definition.
text: Watch for an off-by-one in k from self-neighbours. scanpy's n_neighbors=15 counts the cell itself, so each cell gets 14 real neighbours. sklearn NearestNeighbors.kneighbors(X) with the training data passed as X returns each cell as its own first neighbour, whereas kneighbors() with no argument excludes self. Check: assert no neighbour index equals the query index and print the number of real neighbours per pericyte cell. Drop self-edges and state the k actually used. Note: the requested ratio (CAF fraction / max other fraction) is unchanged by whether pericyte-pericyte or self edges remain in the denominator of the fractions, because both fractions share that denominator; the ratio depends only on the cross-type edge COUNTS, and those do change with k.

reason: Getting the label set or the denominator wrong (CAFs in the max, substring matches, merged labels, enrichment z-scores) changes the reported ratio directly.
text: Specify the comparison set exactly. The library reports 11 labels in the cell-type annotation: B cells, CAFs, Endothelial cells, Epithelial/Cancer cells, M2-like Macrophages, Macrophages, Monocyte-derived cells, Neutrophils, Pericytes, Proliferating myeloid cells, T/NK cells (confirm with value_counts on the label column). The denominator of the ratio is the maximum over non-pericyte types OTHER than CAFs (9 labels if the list is right); including CAFs in the maximum caps the ratio at 1. Use exact label equality, not substring matching ('Macrophages' also matches 'M2-like Macrophages'; 'CAF' vs 'CAFs'), and do not merge myeloid labels. Raw adjacency fractions are not abundance-corrected, but the task asks for the raw-fraction ratio, so do not substitute a permutation-based neighbourhood-enrichment score; an abundance-normalised view may be mentioned as context only.

reason: The answer is a single float that may be sensitive to parameters the task leaves open; the team needs a stated default to report and a way to know how fragile that number is.
text: The ratio is a quotient of two small edge counts and may be unstable or undefined. Pericytes are usually a small, tight cluster, so most of their kNN edges stay within pericytes and only a few go to other types; the denominator (largest non-CAF, non-pericyte type) may rest on a handful of edges or be zero, so the ratio can swing with small changes in k, number of PCs or HVGs. Check: print the pericyte cell count and the raw edge COUNTS (not only fractions) to every other label, and recompute the ratio over a small grid (k = 10, 15, 20, 30; n_pcs = 30, 50; scaled vs unscaled). Report as the answer the value from the canonical scanpy defaults (2000 HVGs, scale max_value=10, 50 PCs, n_neighbors=15, euclidean) and state the range seen across the grid. If the denominator is zero, say so explicitly rather than returning inf silently.

reason: With few cross-type edges, an approximate or unseeded neighbour search can move the ratio between runs; fixing solver, seed and exact search makes the reported number reproducible.
text: PCA and neighbour search can be non-deterministic. sklearn randomized PCA is not exactly reproducible across platforms, and arpack has reported run-to-run or thread-count differences. The library reports that scanpy uses exact brute-force kNN only for small data (euclidean metric with fewer than 8192 cells, or fewer than 4096 otherwise) and approximate PyNNDescent beyond that or for other metrics such as cosine; at about 6420 cells euclidean would be exact and cosine approximate. Small neighbour changes matter when only a few cross-type edges exist. Check: run the pipeline twice and compare the pericyte edge-count table, and cross-check scanpy's neighbours against exact sklearn NearestNeighbors(algorithm='brute') on the same X_pca. Fix svd_solver='arpack' and random_state=0, use exact kNN, and keep the euclidean metric as the default.

reason: Decides the scope of the normalized matrix (all five samples versus one) and how the reported fraction is aggregated across samples of different size.
text: PITFALL: the h5 is a merged multi-sample file (5 samples). Reading only the first group silently normalizes about a fifth of the data, and methods that estimate anything across cells (per-antibody CLR, NSP, dsb, z-scoring) mix sample-specific depth and staining differences if run on the pooled matrix; cell barcodes can also repeat across samples. text: PITFALL: a textbook centred log-ratio (log(x) minus mean log(x), with no pseudocount) or any plain log applied to antibody read counts returns -Inf/NaN wherever a count is zero; muon documents that its flavor='standard' CLR 'may yield infinite values if the input contains zeros'. CHECK: count zeros in read_counts before normalizing; after normalizing, compute np.isfinite(dense_matrix).sum() / dense_matrix.size on the full cells x antibodies matrix that is actually stored (not on sparse .data only, and not after np.nan_to_num). reason: These are silent failures that affect whether a correct normalized layer exists and whether it is finite and reproducible; the checks define what 'well-formed' should mean operationally.
text: PITFALL: implementation traps that corrupt the normalized layer without raising an error. (1) The counts are int64, so in-place division or assignment back into the integer array truncates values. (2) Mission Bio Mosaic's asinh/NSP methods add random Gaussian jitter (sd 0.5) to the counts, which makes output non-reproducible unless random_state is set and makes some jittered counts negative, so a hand-written log applied after jitter yields NaN. (3) NSP additionally rescales reads and resets its scale to 1 if more than 5% of cells would end with zero reads. CHECK: cast counts to float64 before normalizing; the normalized layer is float, has exactly the same shape as the counts, and is stored as a named layer alongside the untouched raw counts; fix the random seed.

reason: The task asks for 'a reasonable method'; this tells the team which common default is not reasonable for antibody data and removes the axis ambiguity that makes two runs both labelled 'CLR' produce different matrices.
text: METHOD CHOICE for antibody counts. (a) The RNA recipe (scale each cell to a common total, then log1p) is a poor fit: with a few dozen pre-selected antibodies the counts are strongly compositional, one or two abundant markers dominate the per-cell total, and OSCA says library-size factors for ADTs introduce composition bias. CHECK: per cell, the share of protein reads taken by the top 1-3 antibodies. Prefer a ratio-based method (CLR with pseudocount, Mosaic NSP/asinh, or control/median-based size factors) over normalize_total+log1p. (b) 'CLR' means two different things and tools default differently: within each cell across antibodies (original CITE-seq, Mosaic, Seurat margin=2, muon axis=1) versus per antibody across cells (Seurat default margin=1, muon default axis=0). Per-cell CLR corrects per-cell depth but assumes total antibody signal is comparable across cells; per-antibody CLR fails when sequencing depth per cell varies a lot. A transposed matrix silently swaps the two. CHECK: confirm orientation (n_cells x 48) and which axis the function centres on; for an unshifted per-cell CLR the row means of the output are about 0. Choose the axis deliberately and record the axis and pseudocount used.

reason: The presence of an all_barcodes table invites a background-based method; the barcode-format mismatch and zero-SD division are file-specific traps that would otherwise cost time or produce non-finite values.
text: PITFALL (only if you consider dsb / background-based normalization): dsb looks applicable because unfiltered barcodes and isotype controls exist, but it standardizes each antibody by the mean and standard deviation of background droplets, so an antibody with zero spread in the chosen background gives a division by zero, and a badly chosen background (one that includes real cells, or only near-zero barcodes) distorts every value. In this file the all_barcodes barcode strings are stored with a different width than the called-cell barcodes, so cells cannot be excluded from the background without first reconciling the formats. CHECK: background barcodes exclude called cells after matching barcode formats; every antibody has non-zero SD in the background; result is finite. If these cannot be met, fall back to pseudocount CLR.

reason: The CLR definition is ambiguous and the variants are not affine-equivalent, so the choice can change method A's count and the final ranking.
text: PITFALL (which CLR): 'CLR' names several transforms that give different marker distributions: (i) per cell across antibodies (original CITE-seq; log counts centred on the cell's own mean log count; what a Tapestri/Mosaic-style CLR is believed to do), (ii) per antibody across cells (Seurat default margin; effectively log1p(x/constant) per marker with no cell-depth correction), plus formula variants log((x+1)/geomean(x+1)) versus Seurat's log1p(x / exp(sum(log1p(x[x>0]))/length(x))). The dip test is invariant only to affine maps, so these variants can give different bimodal-marker counts. CHECK: compute the CLR count under per-cell and per-antibody versions and both formula variants, with all 48 antibodies (isotypes included) in the per-cell geometric mean. IF FOUND (count differs): use the per-cell, across-antibody log-ratio with a +1 pseudocount (log1p(x) minus the per-cell mean of log1p(x)) as the primary definition, state it explicitly, and report the alternatives as sensitivity. CAVEAT: the exact Mosaic CLR formula could not be retrieved (only 'Centered Log Ratio, per sample' is documented), so the log1p form is an assumption, not a verified fact.

reason: Method B has to be re-implemented from a partial description; the team needs the documented steps and a way to tell whether their implementation choices, rather than the data, drive the ranking.
text: PITFALL (NSP is not public): NSP (Noise corrected and Scaled Protein) is a proprietary Mission Bio Mosaic algorithm; a home-made version can differ enough to decide the A/B/C ranking. What the docs specify: Gaussian jitter (mean 0, sd 0.5) is added to raw read counts, an arcsinh is applied, per-cell background and signal are each assumed to depend linearly on the cell's total protein reads, a linear model is fitted to background and to signal and that depth dependence is removed; optionally reads are first divided by a scale factor for over-sequenced runs (reset to 1 if it would leave >5% of cells with 0 reads); it is run per sample; a correct run shows signal and background distinct and both flat versus read depth. Not documented (unknown): how background versus signal antibodies are chosen per cell, and any further internal steps. CHECK: after your NSP, regress per-cell background level and signal level against log total reads (slope ~0 after correction, clearly non-zero before); rerun with 3+ jitter seeds and at least one alternative reasonable background definition (e.g. isotype controls vs lowest-expressed antibodies per cell). IF FOUND (NSP count moves across seeds/variants by as much as the gap between methods): say the ranking is implementation-sensitive, report the range, and base the answer on the variant that follows the documented steps most literally, not on whichever variant wins.

reason: Method C has an unstated cofactor and jitter choice that can change its count, and its lack of depth correction can add depth-driven calls.
text: PITFALL (asinh parameter and depth): asinh(x/c) is linear below about c and logarithmic above. With c=1 on raw integer counts, separate spikes remain at 0,1,2 (false modes); a large c (5 as in CyTOF, 150+ as in flow) compresses the negative population and can merge or split peaks. Mosaic's asinh option exposes only a jitter (sd 0.5), i.e. plain arcsinh of jittered counts. Unlike CLR and NSP, asinh does not remove per-cell total-read differences, so structure in total reads per cell (low-quality cells, doublets, cell-size classes) is copied into every antibody. CHECK: dip test and histogram of log total protein reads per cell per sample; correlation of each asinh-normalized antibody with log total reads; rerun asinh with cofactor 1 and 5, with and without jitter. IF FOUND (count changes with cofactor, or markers are bimodal only because total reads are): use plain arcsinh of sd-0.5-jittered counts as the primary asinh definition, report the cofactor sensitivity, and note which asinh calls are depth-driven rather than marker-specific.

reason: Tie handling differs by method and can create false significant markers unevenly across the three methods, which directly affects the comparison.
text: PITFALL (discrete counts and the dip test): Hartigan's dip test assumes continuous data. Integer AOC counts have atoms at 0,1,2,3... which any per-marker monotone transform (asinh, or a per-marker CLR) preserves, so low-count antibodies get spuriously significant dips (even 11 tied values at 3 levels give p=0.044). Mosaic adds N(0, sd=0.5) jitter to the counts for asinh and NSP only, not for CLR; a per-cell CLR breaks ties implicitly through each cell's geometric mean, so the three methods are not compared like-for-like unless ties are handled deliberately. CHECK: per antibody, the fraction of cells with raw count <= 3 and the number of distinct normalized values; run the dip test with and without sd-0.5 jitter on the counts; see whether the isotype controls become 'bimodal'. IF FOUND (markers significant only without jitter, or low-count/isotype markers significant): treat those as discreteness artefacts, use jittered counts for asinh and NSP as the tool specifies, state what was done for CLR, and report how each method's count changes with and without jitter.

reason: Gives the team a negative control (isotypes) for telling real positive/negative splits from normalization artefacts, and a decision on whether isotypes count as markers.
text: PITFALL (CLR compositional artefacts): per-cell CLR divides every antibody by the cell's geometric mean over the whole panel, so a few abundant, strongly bimodal lineage antibodies shift the denominator in one cell type and imprint a mirror-image split on unrelated or non-expressed antibodies, including isotype controls; CLR also does not remove protein-specific background and the negative population is not centred at zero. CHECK: use the 3 isotype controls (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b) as negative controls, which should be unimodal under every method; for each CLR-significant marker test whether its two modes simply track the cell's mean log count or another marker's positive/negative status; compare the same marker under asinh/NSP. IF FOUND (isotypes or clearly non-expressed markers bimodal under a method): report the count with and without isotype controls, flag those calls as normalization artefacts, and say whether excluding them changes which method has the most bimodal markers.

reason: The whole answer rests on dip p-values; an unvalidated implementation or a null for the wrong n would corrupt all three counts.
text: PITFALL (hand-written dip test): if no dip-test package is available, hand-written code is error-prone (the original published Fortran had a bug) and p-values depend strongly on n with no closed form; the reference implementation interpolates a table in sqrt(n)*D or simulates P = mean(D_obs <= dip(runif(n))) with B=2000 uniform samples of the same n. CHECK before use: (a) dip is unchanged by x -> a*x+b and x -> -x; (b) uniform samples give roughly uniform p (about 5% below 0.05); (c) N(0,1) samples with n~5000 give p near 1; (d) a 50/50 mixture of N(0,1) and N(4,1) gives p near 0; (e) the minimum possible dip is 1/(2n). Build the null by simulating the dip of uniform samples at each sample's actual n (B>=2000; one null per n can be reused for all markers and methods). IF FOUND (a validation fails, or p-values came from a table for the wrong n): fix the implementation first; use one identical null, seed, cell set and marker set for all three normalizations so differences come only from the normalization.
