reason: All three reported numbers come from this metric code and from the choice of how many clusters to make; a counting error or an over-clustered solution changes the answer directly, and using labels inside the clustering would invalidate it.
text: PITFALL (purity is inflatable, and the metric code is easy to get wrong): cluster purity rises trivially with the number of clusters (one cell per cluster gives 100%), and the task's 'average purity' is an unweighted mean over clusters, so many tiny pure clusters raise it while hiding large mixed ones. A resolution chosen only to maximise purity is over-clustered and not a meaningful result. CHECK: over a resolution sweep tabulate n_clusters, distinct types captured, unweighted mean purity, cell-weighted purity, minimum cluster size and the purity of the 5 largest clusters, and see whether purity gains come only from cluster count. Verify the metric code: purity on a 0-100 scale; captured = number of DISTINCT dominant cell types (not number of clusters); total_clusters = exactly the clusters used to compute purity (the final labelling, including any sub-clusters); no empty/unused categories and no NaN labels in the type-by-cluster crosstab. IF FOUND: among solutions that reach at least 17 captured types with stable purity, prefer the one with the fewest clusters, and state cluster count and cell-weighted purity next to the reported figure. Never feed the cell_type labels into the clustering itself: labels may only score or choose among unsupervised partitions, and any such label-guided tuning must be disclosed.

reason: The goal is 17 of 18 types, so the rare types decide success; this tells the team why a plain resolution sweep can stall below 17 and what to do instead.
text: PITFALL (resolution limit hides rare types): modularity-based Leiden/Louvain merges communities smaller than a scale set by total graph size. In a graph of about 100,000 cells at default resolution (~1.0), rare PBMC types (the library names HSPC, ILC, pDC, Plasmablast, cDC, NK CD56bright as the likely ones) can be absorbed into neighbours and never be the plurality of any cluster. Raising global resolution does not fix this cleanly: it shatters the large populations at the same time. CHECK: for every run build an 18-row capture table (one row per cell type: type size, the cluster holding most of that type, share of the type in that cluster, whether the type is dominant in any cluster) and run it across resolutions (e.g. 0.5 to 5); note which types remain uncaptured. IF FOUND: sub-cluster only the parent cluster(s) that contain the missing type (sc.tl.leiden with restrict_to, or re-run HVG + PCA + neighbours on that subset) instead of cranking global resolution; the CPM quality function is an alternative without this limit.

reason: About half of the 18 labels are T/NK subsets; if they are not captured the 17-type goal fails, and they will dominate the average-purity figure, so the team needs a compartment-specific step rather than one global clustering.
text: PITFALL (fine T/NK subsets are not discrete RNA clusters): T-cell states vary continuously, CD4 vs CD8 is poorly resolved by RNA (low CD4 transcript), and in a large T-cell atlas unsupervised clusters mixed CD4 and CD8 whatever the feature selection or PCA/Harmony, being driven by metabolism, TCR, immunoglobulin and HLA transcripts rather than subset markers. Labels such as CD4/CD8 Naive vs Memory, Treg, MAIT, NKT and ILC were probably assigned by reference mapping or protein, so one global clustering is likely to leave several of them never dominant and to hold most of the impure clusters. CHECK: print the type-by-cluster confusion matrix restricted to the T/NK clusters; list which T/NK types have no cluster where they are the plurality and which clusters are below about 60% purity. IF FOUND: subset the T/NK compartment, re-select HVGs inside the subset (consider dropping TR*V, IG*, HLA, ribosomal and mitochondrial genes from the HVG list), recompute PCA and neighbours, and cluster that subset at higher resolution. Expect purity in this compartment to stay well below the myeloid and B-cell clusters, and say so.

reason: Using the ready-made PCA or UMAP is the quickest route and may be unable to separate the fine subsets the task counts; the team should decide between supplied and recomputed embeddings by test, not by default.
text: PITFALL (do not trust the supplied embedding): for abundant, very different cell types the feature choice barely matters, but for subtle differences (naive vs memory T, Treg, MAIT, NKT, NK CD56bright) the number of features and the selection method strongly change the clusters. The file's precomputed obsm['X_pca'] is described in its own metadata as a 'sample-based PCA' with 34.6% variance explained and lists only 100 hvg_genes, so it may rest on too few genes. CHECK: cluster once on the supplied X_pca and once on a pipeline recomputed from raw counts (normalize_total, log1p, 2000-4000 HVGs, 50 PCs) at a matched number of clusters, and compare types captured and purity; check whether known subset markers (e.g. FOXP3, SLC4A10, CCR7, NCAM1, KLRB1) are in the HVG set. IF FOUND: use the recomputed embedding. Never cluster on the 2-D UMAP.

reason: Normalisation state and number of PCs are set before any clustering and determine whether rare types can be separated at all; an error here cannot be repaired by tuning resolution later.
text: PITFALL (preprocessing can silently drop rare-type signal): clustering raw counts, log-transforming twice, or keeping too few PCs removes it, because the PCs that separate rare populations explain little total variance and fall below an elbow-plot cut-off. Log-normalisation and Pearson residuals perform similarly overall, but Pearson residuals give marker genes of small populations high variance. CHECK: confirm X holds integer counts before normalising (X.data equals its rounded self; look at the maximum) and that it is not already logged; compare 30 vs 50 PCs and log1p-CP10k vs analytic Pearson residuals (scanpy.experimental.pp) on the per-type capture table (for each of the 18 types: is it dominant in any cluster). IF FOUND: normalise from raw counts exactly once, keep about 50 PCs rather than cutting at the elbow, and switch to Pearson-residual HVG/PCA if it captures a rare type that log-normalisation misses.

reason: A team that only sweeps resolution leaves an equally strong parameter untested; k decides whether the smallest types can form a cluster of their own.
text: PITFALL (the kNN graph matters as much as resolution): the neighbour graph is fixed before Leiden runs. A larger n_neighbors gives a more global view and merges small populations into neighbours; going from k=15 to k=50 usually changes the cluster count more than a resolution change does. A population with fewer cells than a few multiples of k cannot hold its own neighbourhood. CHECK: note the size of the smallest cell type and compare it with k; rebuild neighbours at k=10, 15 and 30 on the same PCs and compare, at a matched number of clusters, which of the 18 types are dominant in at least one cluster. IF FOUND: use the smaller k (10-15) for the global graph or for the sub-clustering step aimed at the rare type, and record k, number of PCs and distance metric alongside resolution.

reason: Tells the team to test for a condition/donor structure that would otherwise be mistaken for cell-type structure, and gives a decision rule for whether to integrate.
text: PITFALL (donor and stimulation can drive the clusters): this dataset is multi-donor, stimulated-vs-control PBMC (12 donors x 91 cytokine conditions, with a PBS control). Stimulation (interferon-type cytokines change hundreds of genes in every cell, monocytes most strongly) and donor identity can drive the top PCs, so cells group by condition or donor rather than by type. Splitting one type by state only adds clusters, but a shared response programme can also pull different types together, lowering purity or losing a captured type. CHECK: for each cluster compute the largest donor share and the largest cytokine share (and PBS vs cytokine share) and compare with the global shares; correlate the top PCs with donor and treatment; flag mixed-type clusters dominated by one cytokine or donor. IF FOUND: select HVGs batch-aware (batch_key = donor or sample), integrate the PCs with Harmony on donor (optionally also cytokine), re-cluster, and compare the per-type capture table against the unintegrated run; keep whichever captures more types at an equal number of clusters.

reason: Counterweight to the donor/stimulation item: integration is the standard reflex for multi-donor data and here it can cost the rare-type captures the goal depends on.
text: PITFALL (batch integration can over-correct and erase rare types): Harmony's objective is biased toward major cell types, so small populations can be blended into large neighbours; MNN, scVI and LIGER can alter the data considerably. Integrating by default may lose exactly the rare types needed to reach 17 of 18. CHECK: before vs after integration, at the same number of clusters, compare which of the 18 types are dominant in at least one cluster and the purity of the clusters dominated by rare types (HSPC, ILC, pDC, Plasmablast, cDC, NK CD56bright). A rare type that was dominant somewhere before integration and nowhere after is over-correction. IF FOUND: use the uncorrected PCA, or integrate on donor only with a weaker setting. Treat integration as an option that must be justified by the capture comparison, not as a required step.

reason: Gives a specific cause and remedy for a low-purity mixed cluster that resolution tuning alone would not explain or fix.
text: PITFALL (a mixed 'cycling' cluster): proliferating cells from different lineages (activated T, NK, B) share a cell-cycle programme that can be stronger than their type markers, so they form one cycling cluster. Cytokine-stimulated PBMC are likely to contain such cells, and the 18 labels have no 'proliferating' class, so that cluster would be a low-purity mix. CHECK: score S and G2M phases (sc.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle) or look at MKI67/TOP2A per cluster, and inspect the label composition of any cluster with high cycling scores. IF FOUND: sub-cluster that cluster on an HVG set with cell-cycle genes removed (or regress S/G2M scores before PCA) so that it splits by lineage, and compare the result with the original. Do not regress cell cycle blindly across the whole dataset, since regression can remove other biology.

reason: The pass mark is a threshold (17 of 18); the team should know whether its count is stable or an accident of one seed before reporting it.
text: PITFALL (seed dependence): Leiden is stochastic and has no null model; a different random seed changes the partition, so a result of 17 or 18 captured types that rests on one small borderline cluster can flip between runs, and the reported cluster count and purity move with it. CHECK: re-run the chosen configuration with 3-5 random_state values (and, if cheap, on an 80% subsample) and record captured types, n_clusters and mean purity each time. IF FOUND: prefer a configuration whose capture count is the same across seeds, fix and report random_state, and report the range across seeds rather than the best seed.
